title: nostr: fragmented WS frame reassembly delivers tail-only buffer to parser
description:
Live evidence from Rev B (192.168.128.77, btclock_v4-lwf.9 verification run on 2026-05-12):

After landing lwf.9 (queue+worker handoff), the device is stable across
faucet topups (uptime monotonic 202s→213s+ across multiple kind-23197
notifications) but parse_fail in /api/nwc/debug grows in lock-step
with notification arrivals while by_kind[23197] stays at 0.

Hard evidence on this branch (feat/nostr-nip4x HEAD = lwf.9 work tree):

  faucet topup #1: frames_chunk 5→11 (+6), parse_fail 0→4 (+4),
                   by_kind[23197] 0
  faucet topup #2: frames_chunk 11→25 (+14), parse_fail 4→8 (+4),
                   by_kind[23197] 0

last_parse_fail_head dump (truncated, but signature is unambiguous):

  fWx5cZx8dcG4mdMfStVaar6r2GCcgJdIzldoq9Wkn0E6ld5t9o+Z...
  ...mDzrjft3D","sig":"a4017b0d3baa701f36ee7933870ff92a7d...44037"}]\n

That is the TAIL of a kind-23197 event frame — starts mid-base64
content, ends with the canonical `,"sig":"..."}]` closer. The
frame head (`["EVENT","<subid>",{"id":...`) is missing.
Conclusion: the fragment accumulator in
components/nostr/src/relay_client.cpp (cf9394e) is dropping the
first chunk(s) and forwarding only the last chunk's buffer to
on_frame_.

frames_chunk==frames_complete (25==25) is misleading: it agrees only
because the accumulator's clear-on-payload_offset==0 path is firing
on EVERY chunk (likely because esp_websocket_client reports
payload_offset==0 on every event of a multi-event delivery, not
just the first), so each chunk both increments and 'completes' the
buffer.

## Hypothesis

The current logic:

  if (ev->payload_offset == 0) fragment_buf_.clear();
  fragment_buf_.append(ev->data_ptr, ev->data_len);
  const int total = ev->payload_offset + ev->data_len;
  if (total >= ev->payload_len) { emit; clear; }

If esp_websocket_client sets payload_offset==0 on each chunk of a
multi-chunk delivery (instead of the cumulative offset within the
logical frame), every chunk wipes the buffer, so only the LAST chunk
makes it to on_frame_. That matches the tail-only dump exactly.

## Suggested fix

Drive reassembly by op_code instead of payload_offset:

  * op_code 0x1 (TEXT initial fragment): clear buffer, append
  * op_code 0x0 (CONTINUATION): append
  * fin bit indicates 'last fragment' — emit when fin set

If esp-idf does not expose the fin bit directly (event data is
'final' if data_len == payload_len after this event), fall back to
tracking accumulated size against the first event's payload_len.
Cross-check against mempool_kraken_source.cpp (referenced in
cf9394e's commit message) since it uses the same pattern.

## Verification

Same recipe as lwf.9: python3 /tmp/verify_arrows.py 1000 — expect
by_kind[23197] >= 1, parse_fail unchanged, on_payment_dispatched >= 1.

## Why this matters

lwf.9 (queue+worker) prevents the device from CRASHING on
notification arrival, and host tests prove the worker path works
end-to-end against well-formed events. But without a working parser
the worker is never exercised on the device, and notification-driven
features (arrow overlay, payment-screen flash, balance bump) stay
dark.
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: Djuri Baars
comments.text:
Fixed in components/nostr/src/relay_client.cpp. Root cause confirmed via per-event chunk diagnostics on Rev B (172.16.101.112):

  seq=  6 op=1 fin=0 emit=1 off=    0 plen= 1024 dlen= 1024  <- fragment 1 of msg
  seq=  7 op=0 fin=1 emit=1 off=    0 plen=  497 dlen=  497  <- fragment 2 (final)
  seq=  8 op=1 fin=0 emit=1 off=    0 plen= 1024 dlen= 1024  <- fragment 1 of next msg
  seq=  9 op=0 fin=1 emit=1 off=    0 plen=  705 dlen=  705  <- fragment 2 (final)

These are WS-protocol fragmented TEXT messages from Alby's relay. Each fragment is dispatched as a separate WEBSOCKET_EVENT_DATA event with payload_offset=0 — the offset resets per fragment, NOT per logical message. The cf9394e accumulator cleared the buffer on every fragment (because every fragment satisfies payload_offset==0), so only the final fragment ever reached the parser as a tail-only buffer.

Fix: drive reassembly off op_code + fin (WS protocol semantics) instead of payload_offset:

  if (op_code == 0x1 && payload_offset == 0) buf.clear();
  buf.append(data, data_len);
  if (fin && payload_offset + data_len >= payload_len) {
    emit(buf); buf.clear();
  }

Verified end-to-end on Rev B against the live Alby wallet:

  incoming faucet topup 1500 sats:
    by_kind[23196]=1, by_kind[23197]=1
    on_payment_dispatched=2, last_payment={direction:1, amount_sats:1500}
    screen=90 data=['GOT','DN','STS','1','5','0','0']
  incoming faucet topup 1000 sats:
    on_payment_dispatched=4, last_payment={direction:1, amount_sats:1000}
    screen=90 data=['GOT','DN','STS','1','0','0','0']
  outgoing pay_invoice 250 sats (sent from local Python NWC client to a fresh recipient wallet's lud16):
    by_kind[23196]=3, by_kind[23197]=3
    on_payment_dispatched=6, last_payment={direction:2, amount_sats:250}
    screen=90 data=['PAID','UP','STS','2','5','0']
  parse_fail=0 across all of the above; uptime monotonic, no reboots.

Memory: see project_ws_fragment_op_code.md for the full distinction between WS-protocol fragmentation and within-frame chunked delivery.

Also recommended follow-up audit: main/sources/mempool_kraken_source.cpp uses the same broken payload_offset==0 pattern. Mempool.space may not fragment so it likely hasn't bitten us, but it's a latent bug.

title: NWC: dedicated worker task + bounded queue for payment notifications
description:
Notifications (kind 23197 NIP-44 v2 / 23196 NIP-04) crash the device on
first arrival because the heavy decrypt + JSON parse runs directly on
the esp_websocket_client RX-callback stack (~3-4 KiB). Same pattern as
the earlier esp_timer overflow we fixed: hot path must hand off to a
properly-sized task.

## Hard evidence (verified in session 016d57da, branch feat/nostr-nip4x)

1. Alby NWC wallet publishes spec-conform `payment_received` and
   `payment_sent` notifications (top-level `notification_type` present).
   Captured with a passive Python observer; full payload in
   /tmp/observer3.log.
2. A passive Python subscriber with EXACT our device filter
   (kinds=[23195,23197,23196], authors=[wallet], #p=[us], no `since`,
   no `limit`) receives kind 23196 + 23197 + 23195 directly after a
   faucet topup. The relay-side flow is healthy.
3. Notification event pubkey matches the wallet_pubkey from the URI.
4. cf9394e fix(nostr): reassemble fragmented WS text frames correctly
   merges multi-frame payloads — live counters confirm
   frames_chunk=41, frames_complete=41, last_frame_bytes=694. Keep
   this fix; necessary but not sufficient.
5. NEW root cause: device reboots within ~3-4 s of first notification.
   Uptime drops from 270+ s to ~35 s. Heap min was 120 KiB free — NOT
   heap exhaustion. Counters show on_balance_dispatched=N (works) but
   on_payment_dispatched=0 (crashes before reaching dispatcher).

## Architecture (user-approved)

Decouple the heavy path via a bounded FreeRTOS queue + dedicated worker:

- WS task: pushes RawNotificationEvent* (kind, ciphertext, event_id_hex)
  to xQueueSendToBack with timeout=0. On full: drop + counter++.
  Returns ASAP. Zero crypto on hot path.
- Dedicated nwc_notify worker (8 KiB stack, lower prio): xQueueReceive
  → Decrypt (NIP-44 v2 / NIP-04 by kind) → DecodePaymentNotification
  → existing on_payment_(pn) callback → delete event*.
- Queue depth 8 slots × ~1 KiB worst case = 8 KiB ceiling.
- Latency near-realtime (1-2 s OK).
- Responses (kind 23195) keep synchronous path; small + already work.

## Files likely touched

- components/nwc/include/nwc/queue.hpp (new)
- components/nwc/src/queue.cpp (new) — FreeRTOS xQueueCreate wrapper
- components/nwc/src/notif_worker.cpp (new) — task entrypoint
- components/nwc/include/nwc/client.hpp — split OnNotification into
  enqueue + worker-side handler
- components/nwc/src/client.cpp — light enqueue on hot path
- main/app/boot/init_nwc.cpp — create queue + start worker
- test_host/test_nwc_notif_queue.cpp (new)
- test_host/CMakeLists.txt — register

## Verification

1. Build Rev B, OTA flash to 192.168.128.77.
2. Run python3 /tmp/verify_arrows.py 1000 — polls /api/status +
   /api/nwc/debug every 250 ms, triggers faucet topup after 2.5 s.
3. Expect:
   - by_kind[23197] >= 1
   - on_payment_dispatched >= 1
   - last_payment.direction = 1, amount_sats = 1000
   - currentScreen briefly transitions to kNwcPaymentNotify slot
   - data array = ["GOT","DN","1","0","0","0"] during overlay
   - NO reboot; uptime monotonic
4. Push includes the in-flight d5ef674 arrow-glyph commit too.

## Pre-built tooling on disk

- /tmp/verify_arrows.py — live 250 ms poll, triggers topup, logs deltas
- /tmp/nwc_notify_observer.py — passive relay observer (ground truth)
- /tmp/nwc_filter_compare.py — confirms device filter == observer filter

URI (already on device):
nostr+walletconnect://1cfa99e077c187ab9835a949a323ec884b960522b37719e8a225903b741f5b79?relay=wss://relay.getalby.com&relay=wss://relay2.getalby.com&secret=907024c79b7112ec487520552768c0c02c1355a7e4648e522f346c732a0d9a8e&lud16=nwc1778599144031@getalby.com

Faucet topup:
POST https://faucet.nwc.dev/wallets/nwc1778599144031/topup?amount=N

comments.author: Djuri Baars
comments.text:
Landed queue+worker on feat/nostr-nip4x (this session). Code shape matches the approved arch:

- components/nwc/queue.{hpp,cpp}: bounded NotificationQueue (capacity 8) with TryPush/WaitPop/Shutdown + pushed/popped/dropped counters. Uses std::mutex + std::condition_variable + std::deque so it compiles on host and target with the same TU.
- components/nwc/client.{hpp,cpp}: OnNotification on the WS task now copies (kind, content, event_id) into a RawNotification and calls notif_enqueue_; no decrypt, no decode, no callback. Heavy path moved to public DispatchRawNotification → DispatchHeavy, which the worker drives. balance_msat_cache_ promoted to std::atomic<uint64_t> for the worker/WS race. EnsureConversationKey() now eager in Start() so the worker doesn't race first-decrypt setup.
- components/nwc/debug.{hpp,cpp}: notif_queue JSON block with capacity/size/enqueued/dropped/dispatched/queue_pushed/queue_popped/queue_dropped.
- main/app/boot/init_nwc.cpp: NotificationQueue + 8 KiB FreeRTOS task (priority 4, one below WS), wired SetNotifEnqueueFn before Start(). Worker WaitPop(timeout_ms=1000) → DispatchRawNotification → loop.
- main/app/app_ctx.hpp: forward-decl + unique_ptr<NotificationQueue> + TaskHandle_t nwc_notif_worker.
- main/app/boot/init_control_api.cpp: passes the new queue stats through to NwcDebugInfo.
- test_host/test_nwc_notif_queue.cpp (NEW, 9 test cases, 323 assertions): queue push/pop/order, drop-on-full, WaitPop timeout, Shutdown wakes waiter, NwcClient enqueues but doesn't decrypt when fn is set, DispatchRawNotification fires payment callback, NIP-04 (23196) round-trip, saturation drop counter agreement, legacy synchronous path still works when fn is null, and a 100-item threaded producer/consumer FIFO check.
- All 1084 host tests pass (no regressions; new tests + existing nwc/nostr/zap suites all green).
- Rev B firmware builds clean: 0x1b14b0 bytes (51% partition free).

Device verification on Rev B (192.168.128.77, USB /dev/cu.usbmodem101, MAC 90:e5:b1:b5:28:00):

  uptime 16s → 202s → 213s+ across multiple kind-23197 arrivals; NO REBOOT.
  notif_queue counters all zero (queue never used).
  parse_fail counter grew 0→4→8 in lock-step with faucet topups.
  by_kind[23197] stayed at 0.

So:
  ✓ root cause (WS-task stack overflow on decrypt) is GONE — the heavy path no longer runs on the WS callback stack.
  ✗ end-to-end verification (by_kind[23197]>=1, on_payment_dispatched>=1) blocked behind a NEWLY-OBSERVED parser regression — fragmented WS frames are delivered to ParseEnvelope as TAIL-ONLY buffers (head chunks dropped), so notifications never reach NwcClient. Filed as btclock_v4-lwf.10 with the smoking-gun dump.

Recommend: close lwf.9 (the queue+worker work IS done; the original crash mode is fixed) and pursue lwf.10 to unlock full end-to-end. The arrow overlay verification will work the moment lwf.10 lands because the dispatch path is proven against host fixtures.

title: [bug] Screen rotation: per-currency slots render wrong kind + crash risk after NWC balance added (kAgnosticSlots drift)
description:
## Symptoms (user-reported on feat/nostr-nip4x after NWC balance landed)

1. MOW/UNITS label is shown for ALL currency pairs (instead of "MSCW/TIME" on USD or "SATS/<CCY>" elsewhere).
2. BTC/USD ticker renders in the slot where SATS/EUR, SATS/JPY (etc.) are expected.
3. Mining pool global stats screen is "skipped" when the NWC balance screen is enabled.

## Root cause

main/app/screen_manager.hpp declared:

    static constexpr size_t kAgnosticSlots = 8;  // STALE
    static constexpr size_t kPerCurrencySlots = 3;

while main/app/screen_slot_map.hpp had already been bumped to
kAgnosticSlots = 9 when the NWC balance screen (api_id 90, slot 8)
was added (bd btclock_v4-lwf.6). rotation_plan::BuildRotationSequence
and every other rotation consumer reads the slot_map constant, so
ScreenManager was the only stale consumer.

### Cascading consequences

- KindForSlot(slot) per-currency stride uses (slot - 8) % 3, so
  for C=1 with NWC enabled:
    slot 9  (intended Moscow USD)   -> off=1 -> kBtcPrice
    slot 10 (intended BtcPrice USD) -> off=2 -> kMarketCap
    slot 11 (intended MarketCap USD) matches slot_count()-1 -> kBlockFeeRate
    slot 12 (the actual fee slot per slot_map) -> OOB currencies_[1]
    -> UB. Crashes/wedges the rotation, manifests as a "skipped"
    mining pool screen on the following cycle.
- current_currency() uses the same (slot-8)/3 arithmetic, so every
  per-currency slot binds the wrong ccy_idx -- bug 1 (MOW/UNITS
  everywhere) and bug 2 (BTC/<CCY> instead of SATS/<CCY>) are direct
  fallout: LayoutBtcPriceSuffixStrings(mow_mode=...) is called with
  the wrong mode for the wrong slot.
- For C=1 with NWC enabled, the fee slot OOB explains the
  "mining pool global stats wordt overgeslagen" report -- the
  rotation walks into UB right around the fee slot and never
  reliably gets back to slot 4.

## Fix

1. main/app/screen_manager.hpp now sources kAgnosticSlots and
   kPerCurrencySlots directly from slot_map::kAgnosticSlots /
   slot_map::kPerCurrencySlots, so the two can never drift again.
2. KindForSlot() carries a static_assert(kAgnosticSlots == 9, ...)
   so adding another agnostic slot without extending the switch is
   a compile error, not a runtime currency shift.
3. Host tests pin the slot_map invariants every consumer relies on
   (ApiIdForSlot(slot_count-1) == fee, ApiIdForSlot(8) == nwc,
   per-currency offsets at kAgnosticSlots+{0,1,2}).
4. Stale slot-layout header comment in screen_manager.hpp rewritten
   to reflect the post-NWC layout and pin the invariant.

## Verification

- ./build-host/btclock_host_tests -> 1068 tests pass.
- idf.py build on Rev B, Rev A, V8 -> clean.
- Device test deferred (another agent has hardware).

## Files touched

- main/app/screen_manager.cpp (static_assert)
- main/app/screen_manager.hpp (link kAgnosticSlots/kPerCurrencySlots
  to slot_map; rewrite header comment)
- test_host/test_screen_slot_map.cpp (regression for slot_map vs
  ScreenManager agreement)
- test_host/test_rotation_plan.cpp (comment refresh for new
  16-slot total at C=2)
notes: Fixed on branch fix/screen-rotation-and-labels (worktree off feat/nostr-nip4x). HEAD 2806d1d. Closing in-progress on host-test pass + Rev A/B/V8 IDF builds; device verification deferred to another agent who has hardware. PR: https://git.btclock.dev/btclock/btclock_v4/compare/feat/nostr-nip4x...fix/screen-rotation-and-labels
close_reason: kAgnosticSlots drift between slot_map and ScreenManager fixed by sourcing the constants from slot_map and pinning the agnostic switch with a static_assert. Host tests added. Device test deferred (other agent owns hardware).

title: OTA pre-flash hook crashed device: rendered UPDATE overlay from worker task
description:
POST /api/firmware/auto_update consistently aborted Rev B with 'glyph_buf called from second task — render is not MT-safe' after rc.9 was deployed. Root cause: the pre-flash hook callback fires on the ota_auto worker task (auto-update) or the httpd worker (push-OTA), and called RenderOtaUpdateScreen directly. That uses font.cpp's glyph_buf which is owned by the main task; the MT guard added in btclock_v4-71i caught it and aborted. Before that guard the same code corrupted the scratch buffer silently — visually the UPDATE overlay was painted but glyph_buf was racing.

Fix in commit 1857-style: dispatch the render onto the main task via an atomic flag + binary semaphore (mirrors the existing zap_notify_pending pattern). The hook raises ota_overlay_render_pending, kicks main_task via xTaskNotifyGive, and waits up to 5 s on ota_overlay_rendered_sem before continuing into the data-quiesce phase. Also made ScreenManager::ota_active_ std::atomic — it was being written from a worker task and read from the main task without synchronisation.

Verified on Rev B: UPDATE overlay visible within first second on all 7 panels, no abort, full auto-update flow completes cleanly.
acceptance_criteria: POST /api/firmware/auto_update on Rev B does not abort; UPDATE overlay visible on EPD before flash begins; serial log shows 'painting UPDATE + quiescing data' + no 'glyph_buf called from second task'; auto-update completes successfully end-to-end. All three variants (Rev A, Rev B, V8) build clean. Host tests green.
close_reason: Closed

title: ControlServer destructor: UAF op httpd_stop() terwijl PreviewWorker nog draait
description:
De destructor in components/webserver/control_server.cpp:429-440 wacht maximaal 200 ms (20 * 10 ms) op de preview worker en roept dan onvoorwaardelijk httpd_stop(server_) aan. Als een client streamt en de worker zit op dat moment midden in tdefl_compress_mem_to_mem + httpd_ws_send_data voor meerdere panels (V8 = 8 panels, 7.5 inch panel = 48 KB per panel met tot 4 retry rondes), gebruikt de worker een server_ handle die net is gestopt. Dat is een use-after-free in IDF httpd internals.

Bovendien wordt preview_task_ zonder mutex gelezen in regel 434/435 terwijl de worker het zonder mutex naar nullptr schrijft op regel 585. Formele data race; in praktijk veilig op Xtensa LX7 wegens atomaire 32-bit pointer stores, maar nog steeds undefined behavior.
acceptance_criteria: Destructor wacht echt totdat de worker klaar is voordat httpd_stop() wordt aangeroepen. Geen UAF meer mogelijk. Race-vrije signaling via SemaphoreHandle_t of std::atomic. Host-test of gerichte verificatie dat een streaming client tijdens shutdown geen crash veroorzaakt.
close_reason: Closed

title: connectionStatus.nostr=false when Nostr is the data source (shared WSS not probed)
description:
## Symptom

After switching dataSource=2 (Nostr) on both Rev A and Rev B, the
WebUI's connection badge reads "not connected" while the device is
actually receiving live data via the Nostr WSS — block height,
prices, etc. all updating on screen.

Reproduced 2026-05-04 on HEAD=dfbc65b, both boards on
relay.primal.net (same relay used for both data source and zap
listener), nostrZapNotify=true.

## Root cause

main/app/boot/init_control_api.cpp:328-330 wires the
connectionStatus.nostr probe to ctx.zap_relay only:

  if (nostr::RelayClient* zap_ptr = ctx.zap_relay.get()) {
    ccfg.nostr_connected = [zap_ptr]() { return zap_ptr->connected(); };
  }

Per af2ad6c (fix(nostr): share WSS between data source and zap listener),
when dataSource=2 + nostrZapNotify=true + relays equal, the zap
listener borrows the data source's SubscriptionManager and
ctx.zap_relay is left null (init_zap_listener.cpp:131-138). The if
guard fails -> ccfg.nostr_connected stays unset -> control_server.cpp
falls back to false (line 726).

So the only configuration that reports nostr=true today is "dedicated
zap WSS" (different relay or nostrZapNotify=false plus some other
listener). The configuration where Nostr is THE data source (the case
the user actually cares about for the badge) reads false.

## Fix direction

Add a bool relay_connected() probe to NostrDataSource and extend the
init_control_api wiring with an else-if that reads it when zap_relay
is null but nostr_source is set. Both branches are mutually
exclusive given the share-WSS logic; the data source's relay is the
right liveness signal in the shared case, and the only relevant
signal when there's no zap listener at all.

## Relates

- af2ad6c (the fix that introduced the shared-WSS topology)
- bd btclock_v4-17r (the heap-fragmentation issue af2ad6c closed)
close_reason: Fixed in b8343ba — added NostrDataSource::relay_connected() and an else-if fallback in init_control_api so the shared-WSS topology reports nostr=true. Verified on Rev A and Rev B with relay.primal.net.

title: Cold-boot rotation includes mining-pool & bitaxe screens when parent flags are off
description:
At first boot (and after factory reset), the auto-rotate sequence includes Mining Pool Hashrate (api_id 70), Mining Pool Earnings (71), Bitaxe Hashrate (80) and Bitaxe Best Diff (81) — even when the parent feature flags `miningPoolStats=false` and `bitaxeEnabled=false`.

Three compounded causes:

1. `main/app/rotation_plan.hpp` — `BuildRotationSequence` cold-boot fallback (empty `screenOrder` CSV) emits every slot 0..SlotCount-1 in index order **without** consulting the `is_enabled` predicate.
2. `main/app/boot/init_screen_manager.cpp` and `main/app/event_loop.cpp` — both `is_enabled` lambdas only check `screen<id>Visible`, never the parent feature flags. Default for `screen<id>Visible` is `true`, so even after wiring the predicate into the cold-boot path, ids 70/71/80/81 would still pass.
3. `components/webserver/control_server.cpp` — `on_screens_changed` only fires for screenOrder/screen<id>Visible/actCurrencies. PATCHing `miningPoolStats` or `bitaxeEnabled` at runtime does not rebuild rotation; user has to reboot.

Settings GET already filters cleanly via `ctx.mining_pool_stats_enabled` / `ctx.bitaxe_enabled`, so the WebUI looks correct — but the actual on-device rotation walks through these screens. Verified on Rev B at 192.168.20.236 with `miningPoolStats:false`, `bitaxeEnabled:false`.

Fix:
- Cold-boot fallback in `BuildRotationSequence` runs each slot through `is_enabled(slot_map::ApiIdForSlot(slot, currency_count))`.
- Both `is_enabled` lambdas additionally gate api_ids 70/71 on `miningPoolStats` and 80/81 on `bitaxeEnabled`.
- `on_screens_changed` also fires for those two pref keys.
- Host tests in `test_rotation_plan.cpp` cover the cold-boot path.
close_reason: Closed

title: No coredump partition or panic capture on production firmware
description:
A panic on a deployed device today loses the backtrace forever. With `CONFIG_LOG_DEFAULT_LEVEL_WARN=y` and `CONFIG_BOOTLOADER_LOG_LEVEL_WARN=y` even the panic preamble is muted unless someone happens to be on USB serial at the moment of the crash.

**Current state:**
- `sdkconfig.defaults` has no `CONFIG_ESP_COREDUMP_TO_FLASH=y`
- No `coredump` partition in `partitions_4mb.csv` / `partitions_8mb.csv` / `partitions_16mb.csv`

**Plan:**
1. Add `coredump,data,coredump,,64K,` partition to all three CSVs (carve from app slack — Rev A is tightest).
2. `CONFIG_ESP_COREDUMP_TO_FLASH=y` + `CONFIG_ESP_COREDUMP_DATA_FORMAT_ELF=y` in `sdkconfig.defaults`.
3. Expose `GET /api/coredump` (binary stream) + `DELETE /api/coredump` (clear partition) in `control_server.cpp`.
4. Document `espcoredump.py info_corefile -c dump.elf build-rev-b/btclock_v4.elf` in QUICKSTART.

**Risk:** Rev A 4MB partition layout is tight — verify there's slack before carving.
close_reason: Implemented in 7b6b61d. esp_core_dump_init in main; GET /api/coredump streams ELF; DELETE clears. Rev B/V8 capture; Rev A skips (4MB partition pressure).

title: xTaskCreate return value dropped at most call sites
description:
**Symptom:** On `pdFAIL` (heap/stack exhaustion) the task is silently lost and the rest of boot proceeds as if it succeeded. No log, no error path.

**Affected sites (audited):**
- `main/io/led_controller.cpp:637`
- `main/io/frontlight_controller.cpp:50`
- `components/bitaxe/src/bitaxe_source.cpp:93`

- `components/webserver/sse_server.cpp:119`
- `components/mining_pool_common/src/pool_base.cpp:94`

title: Queue/task creation failures crash silently with assertions disabled
description:
**Symptom:** `xQueueCreate` failures (heap pressure on Rev A) are guarded by `assert()`, but `sdkconfig.defaults` sets `CONFIG_COMPILER_OPTIMIZATION_ASSERTIONS_SILENT=y` and `CONFIG_HAL_ASSERTION_SILENT=y` — every assert is a no-op in production. The next-line `xTaskCreate` then spawns a task that does `xQueueReceive(nullptr, ...)`, undefined behavior.

**Affected sites:**
- `main/io/frontlight_controller.cpp:45-50` — task created unconditionally after asserted xQueueCreate

description:

title: SSD1680 partial refresh depends on invertedColor=true (polarity bug)
description: On Rev B, partial refresh only works correctly when the display setting invertedColor=true (white on black). With invertedColor=false (default black on white) partial refresh produces garbage / ghosted output. Same-hardware, same-firmware, toggling only the setting changes whether partial refresh functions. Strong signal that one RAM bank is being populated with inverted bits and the other isn't — when both are inverted (inverted=true) the diff is consistent; when only one is inverted (inverted=false) the panel sees wrong delta pixels.
notes:
Suspect the framebuffer-to-RAM conversion path: components/epd_ssd1680/epd_ssd1680.cpp ~line 413-415 writes both 0x24 (BW) and 0x26 (prev-BW) — if the buffer used for 0x26 isn't run through the same invert-if-needed transform as 0x24, this is exactly the observed symptom. Check WriteVram paths for each bank and the ShadowFb that's used as prev-buffer input. v3_fci handles this correctly when invertedColor=false, so compare. Diagnostic to confirm: flip invertedColor at runtime via settings and rerun transition test — should reproduce reliably.\n\nParked behind the v3_fci timing/mutex fix currently in flight on main. Investigate if transitions still show issues after that fix + GxEPD2 improvements (wip/epd-debug-v7-snapshot cherry-pick).
2026-04-24 investigation: WriteVram XOR is algebraically symmetric — both 0x24 (BW) and 0x26 (Red) go through the same WriteVram path, both getting the same XOR based on g_inverted flag. Not a pure polarity asymmetry bug. Cherry-picked cdb7387 (per-frame reinit + settle + activation retry from wip/v3fci-pattern-fixes) to main as commit 15190c4 — this fixes the first cross-screen transition with invertedColor=false on Rev B (without it the panels are completely wedged for cross-screen partial refresh). However subsequent transitions still fail: API advances but panel doesn't repaint reliably. Needs the full wip/v3fci-pattern-fixes branch (MCP mutex + reinit + cross-panel barrier), not just the SSD1680 reinit commit. The 'invertedColor=true works, invertedColor=false doesn't' observation is coincidental: with invertedColor=true the user's workflow triggers full refreshes (via PATCH) that happen to unstick the panel, while invertedColor=false exercises more partial-refresh paths that expose the state drift. Root cause is control-register drift + MCP23017 I2C contention between panels, not polarity.
close_reason: Fixed across SSD1680 driver port: 289dae4 (GxEPD2 driver + MCP23017 mutex), 7355319 (port reference driver faithfully), b19cdde/18784b1 (per-refresh reinit), 5d09d1b (BUSY assert wait), f2f8963/afa73e1 (MCP23017 recursive mutex), cdb7387 (per-frame reinit + settle + activation retry).

title: Port webserver + SSE to ESPAsyncWebServer (esp32async/esp_async_webserver)
description:
## Motivation

The stock `esp_http_server` handler path runs on the caller's task. Our current code has every control endpoint + SSE broadcast executing on the main task alongside the screen renderer, which deterministically stack-overflowed Rev B at ~60-90s of uptime with an active SSE client (see the 3584 B default main task; bumped to 8192 B in 36e9ebb as a bandaid).

Real fix: move the webserver onto its own task via ESPAsyncWebServer (esp32async/esp_async_webserver), which also retires our custom SSE frame assembler in favour of its built-in AsyncEventSource.

Library: https://components.espressif.com/components/esp32async/espasyncwebserver/versions/3.10.3/
GitHub: https://github.com/ESP32Async/ESPAsyncWebServer

## Scope

### Files to rewrite
- `components/webserver/control_server.{hpp,cpp}` — 40+ endpoints (status, settings, show/*, action/*, screen/*, scan, upload/webui, lights, frontlight, dnd, nostr, partitions, etc). Trampoline-to-method pattern replaced with lambdas bound to AsyncWebServerRequest.
- `components/webserver/provisioning_server.{hpp,cpp}` — portal (5 handlers). Simpler surface; do this first as proof of concept.
- `components/webserver/sse_frame.{cpp,hpp}` — retire. Replace with AsyncEventSource.

### Files to leave alone
- `components/webserver/mime.{cpp,hpp}` — mime-type map, library-agnostic.
- `components/webserver/show_text_parse.{cpp,hpp}` — payload parser, library-agnostic.
- `components/webserver/heap_metrics.hpp` — pure JSON builder, library-agnostic.
- `components/webserver/dns_hijack.cpp` — UDP-53 hijack, no HTTP involvement.
- Host tests — all pure logic, unaffected.

### New deps
- Add `esp32async/esp_async_webserver: "^3.10"` to `components/webserver/idf_component.yml`.
- The library may pull in AsyncTCP as a transitive dep.

## Non-goals

- Do NOT change endpoint URLs, request bodies, or response shapes. The WebUI (submodule under `data/`) consumes this API and must continue working without changes.
- Do NOT regress the provisioning verify-before-save flow landed in aa89376.
- Do NOT break the /upload/webui streaming path that feeds FlashWebuiImage().

## Acceptance

- All three variants compile clean (REV_A / REV_B / V8).
- Host tests still 317/317 passing.
- Rev B survives a 15-minute SSE client subscription + screen rotation without stack overflow (main task stack bump can be rolled back afterwards).
- V8 provisioning portal: TryConnect verify-before-save still returns structured 200 / 400 per aa89376.
- WebUI static pages serve from LittleFS with gzip Content-Encoding, same as today.

## Risk

- `max_uri_handlers` budget goes away — AsyncWebServer has no such limit.
- AsyncTCP lwip-hook interactions might need PSRAM tuning for connection buffers on Rev A (tight flash).
- Upload-body streaming API differs — FlashWebuiImage wrapper needs to become async-receiver-based.

title: Add wifi-only reset path (preserve other settings)
description:
In v3 you could wipe just the wifi credentials by holding button 1 during boot. v4 only has the all-buttons-held factory reset (wipes the entire NVS partition).

**Goal**: Add a wifi-only reset that clears only the STA credentials (`net/ssid`, `net/pw`) and `settings/wifiConfigured`, then reboots. The device comes back up in SoftAP provisioning mode while preserving every other user setting (timezone, currencies, screens, LEDs, frontlight, NWC keys, etc.).

**Implementation**:
1. Add `btclock::settings::PerformWifiReset()` next to `PerformFactoryReset` in components/settings/factory_reset.{cpp,hpp} — uses Prefs::Remove + Commit on the targeted keys, then `esp_restart()`.
2. Add `POST /api/wifi_reset` to control_server.cpp, gated by `{"confirm":"WIFI"}` (mirrors the factory_reset confirm gate but with a distinct sentinel so a user can't accidentally trigger one when meaning the other).
3. Wire `Config::on_wifi_reset` callback through init_control_api.cpp → calls PerformWifiReset.
4. Document the endpoint in data/static/openapi.json.

**Out of scope (file as follow-up)**: hardware combo (boot-time button-hold). Would need raw MCP polling before ButtonReader starts plus a visual cue — bigger UX surface than a one-line endpoint. Track as a follow-up issue once HTTP path lands.

Closed without an /api endpoint. The Rev A partition was already at 0x2390 free (~9 KB) at HEAD — adding the endpoint cost ~700 B for ~32 B saving compared to the button-only path, not worth it on Rev A.

Final shape:
- components/settings: PerformWifiReset() clears net/{ssid,pw} + settings/wifiConfigured then reboots; net/app (SoftAP password) preserved.
- main/app/boot/init_wifi_reset_button.{hpp,cpp}: polls MCP GPA0 (= physical "button 1", leftmost), 3 s continuous hold → call PerformWifiReset. LED flashes red (kFlashError) while held.

title: Miniz-compress font blobs to recover app-partition flash
description:
The fonts component embeds 17 .ttf blobs via EMBED_FILES (~162 KB raw) directly into the app partition. Rev A is at ~8% free on its 4 MB partition, so any new font (or new code) competes with the existing bundle for space.

Implementation: gzip each .ttf at CMake-configure time via 'gzip -n -9' into components/fonts/.gz_cache/<name>.ttf.gz, EMBED_FILES the .gz, and decompress at boot in Font's ctor using miniz from ESP_ROM (tinfl_decompress_mem_to_mem, raw deflate). Decompressed buffer lives in PSRAM for the lifetime of AppFonts.

Tradeoffs:
- Flash recovered: ~46.7 KB across the bundle. Rev A app partition went from ~8% free to 10% free (~37 KB after subtracting the helper code overhead).
- PSRAM cost: ~162 KB held permanently (eager-decode-at-boot strategy).
- Decoder is free: tinfl is in ROM.
- Boot cost: ~170 ms one-shot decode at AppCtx construction.

Files touched: components/fonts/CMakeLists.txt, components/fonts/font.cpp, components/fonts/include/font.hpp, .gitignore.
notes:
Hardware-verified working on Rev B (98:88:e0:9d:55:30) — Block Height and Fee Rate screens both render correctly post-flash. Final design:

1. EAGER decompression at Font ctor (lazy variant produced blank panels — fonts decompressed but render path silently failed; root cause not pinned, eager avoids it entirely).
2. tinfl_decompressor heap-allocated from PSRAM via heap_caps_malloc (not stack-allocated — the struct is ~12 KB which overflows the 8 KB main task stack during splash render).
3. PSRAM-only allocation for the decompressed font buffer (MALLOC_CAP_SPIRAM | MALLOC_CAP_8BIT, no internal-RAM fallback — internal-RAM fallback starves wifi_create_queue's task-queue allocations).
4. tinfl_decompress called with TINFL_FLAG_USING_NON_WRAPPING_OUTPUT_BUF — without it the streaming API treats the output buffer as an LZ77 wrap-around dictionary and demands a power-of-two size, returning TINFL_STATUS_BAD_PARAM (-3) on every font (~10 KB sizes are not powers of two).

Net effect: ~46.7 KB compressed savings on EMBED_FILES bundle; Rev A app partition went 8% → 10% free (~37 KB after helper code overhead). PSRAM cost ~162 KB held permanently for the decompressed bundle. Boot-time decode ~170 ms one-shot at AppCtx ctor.
close_reason: Verified on Rev B hardware — splash + screen rotation both render correctly with compressed fonts.

title: Proxy support: HTTP CONNECT + SOCKS4/4a/5 for all outbound TCP
description:
Route every device-originated outbound TCP connection (HTTP, HTTPS, WS,
WSS, OTA) through an optional user-configured proxy. Configurable via
NVS + WebUI. Supports HTTP CONNECT, SOCKS4, SOCKS4a, SOCKS5 (with
optional user/pass auth on SOCKS5 and HTTP CONNECT). TLS verification
continues to target the real destination — proxy sits below the SSL
layer.

## Why
Users on networks where outbound 443 is blocked or where Tor/SSH
SOCKS5 is the only path want the device to keep working. Today the ~11
HTTP/WS init sites all bypass any single chokepoint, so this needs a
proper transport-layer plumb-through, not a per-source flag.

## Hooks ESP-IDF v6.0.1 already gives us
- `tcp_transport/esp_transport_socks_proxy.h` ships SOCKS4 already.
- `esp_http_client_config_t.transport` accepts a custom
  `esp_transport_handle_t` behind
  `CONFIG_ESP_HTTP_CLIENT_ENABLE_CUSTOM_TRANSPORT=y`
  (esp_http_client.h:250).
- `esp_websocket_client_config_t.ext_transport` does too. The client
  uses the handle as-is (esp_websocket_client.c:1395), so we hand it a
  WS-on-TLS chain.

We own SOCKS5 + SOCKS4a + HTTP CONNECT. Reference impl
`transport_socks_proxy.c` is 224 LOC — SOCKS5 will be similar.

## Full plan
See `~/.claude/plans/proxy-support.md` (committed to design field).

- components/bitaxe/src/bitaxe_source.cpp:175
- components/pool_logo_fetcher/src/pool_logo_fetcher.cpp:245

proxying mDNS/DHCP/NTP.
design:
# HTTP CONNECT + SOCKS4/SOCKS4a/SOCKS5 proxy support for all device-originated TCP

## Goal
Route every outbound TCP connection the firmware initiates (HTTP, HTTPS,
WS, WSS, OTA) through an optional user-configured proxy. Settings live
in NVS + WebUI. All four protocols supported: HTTP CONNECT, SOCKS4,
SOCKS4a, SOCKS5 (with optional username/password auth on SOCKS5 + HTTP
CONNECT). Cert verification still targets the real destination, not the
proxy.

## Why it's tractable in IDF v6.0.1
The hooks already exist:
- `tcp_transport/esp_transport_socks_proxy.h` ships **SOCKS4**
  (`esp_transport_socks_proxy_init(parent, cfg)`).
- `esp_http_client_config_t.transport` accepts a custom
  `esp_transport_handle_t` when `CONFIG_ESP_HTTP_CLIENT_ENABLE_CUSTOM_TRANSPORT=y`
  (header at `components/esp_http_client/include/esp_http_client.h:250`).
- `esp_websocket_client_config_t.ext_transport` accepts one
  unconditionally (managed component header line 149). The client
  uses the handle as-is (`client->transport = ext_transport;`
  `esp_websocket_client.c:1395`), so we must hand it a WS-on-TLS
  handle, not a raw TCP one.

Missing pieces we own: SOCKS5, SOCKS4a (DNS-through-proxy variant of
SOCKS4), HTTP CONNECT. All three model on `transport_socks_proxy.c`
(224 LOC reference).

## Component layout

New: `components/proxy_transport/`

```
components/proxy_transport/
  CMakeLists.txt                   # REQUIRES tcp_transport esp-tls log
  include/proxy_transport/
    proxy_transport.hpp            # public C++ API
    proxy_config.hpp               # POD config struct (host-testable)
  src/
    proxy_transport.cpp            # build_chain() + dispatch
    socks5.c                       # esp_transport_socks5_init(parent, cfg)
    http_connect.c                 # esp_transport_http_connect_init(parent, cfg)
    socks4a.c                      # ATYP=domain extension to SOCKS4 (or
                                   # delegate to socks_proxy for ipv4)
```

### Public API (proxy_transport.hpp)

```cpp
namespace btclock::proxy {

enum class Kind : uint8_t { kNone, kHttpConnect, kSocks4, kSocks4a, kSocks5 };

struct Config {
  Kind kind = Kind::kNone;
  std::string host;            // empty when kind == kNone
  uint16_t port = 0;
  std::string user;            // optional
  std::string pass;            // optional, only honoured for SOCKS5/HTTP-CONNECT
  // Bypass globs evaluated against destination hostname. Default
  // includes "*.local", "127.0.0.1", "10.*", "192.168.*", "172.16.*"–
  // "172.31.*" so localPoolHost stays direct.
  std::vector<std::string> bypass;
};

bool ShouldBypass(const Config&, std::string_view dest_host);

// Build a WS-over-TLS-over-[proxy?]-over-TCP chain, used as
// websocket_cfg.ext_transport. Returns NULL on alloc failure; caller
// owns the handle and must esp_transport_destroy it after the client
// is destroyed.
esp_transport_handle_t BuildWsChain(const Config&,
                                    std::string_view dest_host,
                                    bool use_tls,
                                    const TlsParams&);

// Build a TCP-over-[proxy?] chain for esp_http_client.transport.
// esp_http_client adds its own SSL layer when scheme is https; we just
// return the proxied TCP handle here so the client's TLS code path
// stays in charge of SNI/ALPN/crt_bundle.
esp_transport_handle_t BuildHttpChain(const Config&,
                                      std::string_view dest_host);

}  // namespace btclock::proxy
```

### Helper: net_util

Add to `components/net_util/`:
- `MakeProxyConfigFromSettings()` — reads NVS once per request
- `ApplyProxyToHttpClient(esp_http_client_config_t&, dest_url)` — sets
  `cfg.transport` when needed; no-op when bypassed/disabled.
- `ApplyProxyToWebsocket(esp_websocket_client_config_t&, dest_url, tls_params)`

Call sites change from "configure cfg directly" to
"configure cfg + ApplyProxyTo*(cfg, url)".

## SOCKS5 framing (rfc1928)

Implement in C, mirroring `transport_socks_proxy.c`'s shape:

1. Greeting: `05 NMETHODS METHODS...`
   - if no auth: `05 01 00`
   - if user/pass: `05 02 00 02`
2. Server reply: `05 METHOD`. If 0x02, do user/pass sub-negotiation
   (rfc1929): `01 ULEN UNAME PLEN PASSWD` → `01 00`.
3. Request: `05 01 00 ATYP DST.ADDR DST.PORT`
   - ATYP=0x03 (domain) when caller passes a hostname → DNS resolves
     server-side.
   - ATYP=0x01 (ipv4) only when caller passes a literal IP.
4. Reply: parse REP byte, map to errno-ish.

Errors translate to a stable enum exposed via
`esp_transport_get_error_handle()` so existing log lines (e.g. ota's
"http GET begin") still surface useful messages.

## HTTP CONNECT framing

`CONNECT host:port HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: host:port\r\n[Proxy-Authorization: Basic <b64>\r\n]\r\n`

Parse status line; `200 ...` = success, anything else = fail. Read until
`\r\n\r\n`, discard headers, then hand the socket back to the parent
transport. Auth uses Basic only (we already pull mbedtls' base64 in via
crt_bundle).

## Settings schema additions

Add to `components/settings/include/settings/pref_keys.hpp` +
`schema.hpp`:

| key             | kind   | boot_only | notes                              |
|-----------------|--------|-----------|------------------------------------|
| `proxyEnabled`  | bool   | no        | master switch                      |
| `proxyType`     | uchar  | no        | 0=none 1=http 2=socks4 3=socks4a 4=socks5 |
| `proxyHost`     | string | no        | host or IP                         |
| `proxyPort`     | uint   | no        | 1..65535                           |
| `proxyUser`     | string | no        |                                    |
| `proxyPass`     | string | no        | NVS-encrypted via existing pattern |
| `proxyBypass`   | string | no        | comma-separated globs              |

Boot-only=no: proxy config is read at the start of each request, so
swapping does not require reboot. Already-open WS connections need
explicit reconnect — emit a `kReconnectAll` control event when any
proxy* field changes (mirrors `on_mdns_changed` pattern).

## Call sites to migrate

Each one swaps `esp_http_client_init(&cfg)` /
`esp_websocket_client_init(&cfg)` for two lines: build the chain via
the helper, set `cfg.transport` / `cfg.ext_transport`. List from
current grep:

- `components/bitaxe/src/bitaxe_source.cpp:175`
- `components/pool_logo_fetcher/src/pool_logo_fetcher.cpp:245`
- `components/btclock_data/btclock_currencies_fetch.cpp:54`
- `components/btclock_data/btclock_data.cpp:78`  (WS)
- `components/btclock_data/btclock_data.cpp:408` (HTTP)
- `components/ota/ota_manager.cpp:71`
- `components/ota/ota_manager.cpp:360`
- `components/nostr/src/relay_client.cpp:24` (WS)
- `components/mining_pool_common/src/pool_base.cpp:180`
- `main/sources/mempool_kraken_source.cpp:68` (WS)
- `main/sources/mempool_kraken_source.cpp:104` (WS)

OTA matters: the firmware-fetch HTTP client AND the optional manifest
fetch both go through the helper, so OTA inherits proxy support
automatically. Verify on a release where the GitHub host is reachable
only via the proxy.

## Kconfig & sdkconfig

`sdkconfig.defaults`:
```
CONFIG_ESP_HTTP_CLIENT_ENABLE_CUSTOM_TRANSPORT=y
```

This is the gate that exposes `esp_http_client_config_t.transport`.
Without it, the field exists but the client ignores it.

## TLS verification

For HTTP/HTTPS via `esp_http_client`: leave `crt_bundle_attach` set.
The client's SSL layer sees the destination URL and validates SNI/cert
against the real host — proxy is below the TLS layer, invisible to
mbedtls.

**Do NOT touch `esp_http_client_config_t.skip_cert_common_name_check`
or `common_name`.** A future implementer might reach for them assuming
the proxy disturbs CN validation; it doesn't. With both unset (default),
the client validates the cert's CN against the URL hostname, which is
already the real destination. Setting either weakens the verification
without need.

If anyone later replaces our hand-rolled OTA HTTP client with
`esp_https_ota`: `esp_https_ota_config_t.http_config` is just an
`esp_http_client_config_t`, so `.transport` is inherited and the proxy
chain works there too. No additional plumbing.

For WSS via custom chain: build TLS layer ourselves
(`esp_transport_ssl_init` + `esp_transport_ssl_crt_bundle_attach` +
`esp_transport_ssl_set_alpn_protocols` if needed) **with hostname =
real destination**, not the proxy. The `tls_gate` mutex still wraps
`esp_transport_connect()`.

## Host tests

`test_host/test_proxy_transport.cpp`:
- SOCKS5 greeting/reply parser: feed canned bytes, assert state machine
  advances + emits the right outgoing bytes.
- SOCKS5 user/pass sub-negotiation, including failure path (0x01 0x01).
- HTTP CONNECT request formation; status-line parser for 200 / 407 / 502.
- Bypass matcher: `*.local`, RFC1918, exact host.
- `MakeProxyConfigFromSettings()` round-trips the schema.

No real sockets — pull-out the framing code into pure functions that
take/produce `std::vector<uint8_t>`, plus a thin transport adapter that
wires those to `esp_transport_read/write`. The adapter is firmware-only;
the tests exercise the pure half.

Add a small fake `esp_transport` shim in `test_host/` if we want to
exercise the chained `connect` end-to-end without IDF.

## WebUI

Svelte form panel under existing settings page:
- Master toggle (proxyEnabled).
- Type dropdown (none / http / socks4 / socks4a / socks5).
- Host + port inputs (validate port 1..65535, host non-empty when
  enabled).
- Username/password (shown only for http+socks5).
- Bypass list (textarea, one entry per line, comma-stored).
- "Apply" patches `/api/settings`; toast notes that open WS connections
  reconnect.

Auto-tests: extend the existing `tests/api/settings.test.ts` with proxy
fields.

## Acceptance criteria

1. With `proxyEnabled=false`, every existing test passes unchanged
   (no behavioural drift on the default code path).
2. With proxyType=socks5 + working SOCKS5 server (ssh -D 1080 to
   localhost via test rig), the device:
   - boots clean (no TLS-gate starvation),
   - hits all data sources (mempool/kraken WS, btclock_data WS,
     pool HTTPS, bitaxe HTTPS, nostr WSS, currencies HTTPS, logo HTTPS),
   - serves /api/status with `wifi.connected=true` and live data.
3. OTA update via `POST /api/ota/start` works through the proxy.
4. Bypass list keeps `localPoolHost.local` (mDNS) and 192.168.*
   addresses on direct connections.
5. Host tests cover SOCKS5 + HTTP CONNECT framing, bypass, and the
   settings round-trip.
6. WebUI: proxy panel passes lint + e2e settings test.
7. Docs: add a "Proxy" page to mkdocs site listing supported types,
   limitations (no UDP, no SOCKS5 GSSAPI), and the bypass syntax.

## Out of scope

- UDP via SOCKS5 (only TCP).
- SOCKS5 GSSAPI auth (rare, large mbedtls hit).
- Per-source proxy override.
- Auto-detection (PAC files, WPAD).
- Proxying mDNS / DHCP / NTP — those are LAN-direct.

## Sequencing

The work splits cleanly into branches that can land independently:

1. **Foundation** — new `proxy_transport` component with SOCKS5 +
   HTTP CONNECT + SOCKS4a (delegating SOCKS4 to existing IDF impl);
   host tests for framing and bypass.
2. **Settings + helper** — schema fields, NVS round-trip, `net_util`
   helpers, `kReconnectAll` event; `proxyEnabled=false` default keeps
   the old code path bit-identical.
3. **Call-site migration** — swap each of the ~11 init points to use
   the helper. One commit per call site (cheap to revert).
4. **WebUI** — settings panel + e2e test.
5. **Docs** — mkdocs page + screenshot.
6. **Hardware verification** — flash Rev B with proxyEnabled=true
   pointing at a local SSH SOCKS5 + a tinyproxy HTTP CONNECT; capture
   screenshot, validate /api/status. Repeat once over OTA.

Each phase has its own beads child issue under the parent.

1. With proxyEnabled=false, all existing host + firmware tests pass

2. With proxyType=socks5 against a localhost ssh -D 1080 SOCKS5: device

   pool HTTPS, bitaxe HTTPS, nostr WSS, currencies HTTPS, logo HTTPS),
   /api/status shows live data.
3. OTA update via POST /api/ota/start works through the proxy.
4. Bypass list keeps *.local and RFC1918 on direct connections.
5. Host tests cover SOCKS5 framing, HTTP CONNECT framing, bypass, and
   settings round-trip.
6. WebUI proxy panel passes lint + e2e settings test.
7. Mkdocs page documents supported types, bypass syntax, and known
   limitations.

title: [bug] BtclockDataSource::OnWatchdogTick stack-overflows Tmr Svc on TLS HTTPS probe
description:
## Symptom

Rev A (and likely all variants) reset unexpectedly with this panic, recovered from `/api/coredump`:

```
***ERROR*** A stack overflow in task Tmr Svc has been detected.
```

Coredump observed on board MAC `dc:54:75:d6:00:fc` on 2026-05-06.

## Root cause

`BtclockDataSource::OnWatchdogTick()` is registered as a FreeRTOS software-timer callback (`xTimerCreate` at [components/btclock_data/btclock_data.cpp:110](components/btclock_data/btclock_data.cpp#L110)) and therefore runs on the `Tmr Svc` task.

`Tmr Svc` runs at the IDF default stack size — `CONFIG_FREERTOS_TIMER_TASK_STACK_DEPTH = 2048 words = 8 KiB`. There is no override in `sdkconfig.defaults` or any per-variant fragment.

Inside the callback, `FetchUpstreamHeight()` ([btclock_data.cpp:360](components/btclock_data/btclock_data.cpp#L360)) does a synchronous **HTTPS** request via `esp_http_client_perform` with `esp_crt_bundle_attach` for TLS certificate validation. A full TLS handshake plus mbedTLS context plus the HTTP client state easily exceeds 8 KiB, blowing the stack.

The comment at [btclock_data.cpp:318](components/btclock_data/btclock_data.cpp#L318) acknowledges the constraint ("the timer task has a small stack; keep this short") and then immediately violates it.

## Why it looks like "out of nothing"

The watchdog tick runs every 5 min, but only invokes `FetchUpstreamHeight` when WS data has been stale ≥ 60 min (`kStaleThresholdMs`). On a healthy connection it takes a 60+ min relay/network gap to trip the path, so the panic appears rare and unpredictable.

## Fix

Move the HTTP probe + reconnect logic off `Tmr Svc`. The cleanest minimal fix is to spawn a transient worker task from the timer callback (only when staleness threshold is met), give it a real stack (>= 6 KiB), and let it run `FetchUpstreamHeight` + `ForceReconnect` there. Track an in-flight flag so a backed-up timer queue can't stack probe tasks, and have `Stop()` wait for any probe to finish before tearing down the WS client.

Alternative considered: bump `CONFIG_FREERTOS_TIMER_TASK_STACK_DEPTH` system-wide. Rejected — wastes RAM for every timer callback and doesn't fix the underlying design smell of running TLS on a shared timer task.

## Verification plan

- Host tests: `cmake --build build-host && ./build-host/btclock_host_tests` (the watchdog logic itself isn't host-tested, but the build must stay clean).
- On-device: build + flash Rev A, confirm normal operation, then force a stale condition (point to an unreachable WS to keep `last_change_tick_` from updating) and confirm the watchdog probe runs without panicking.
- Re-check `/api/coredump` after a multi-day run to confirm the partition stays empty.
close_reason:
Fixed in commit 97a9cd7. Watchdog HTTPS probe moved off Tmr Svc to a transient 6 KiB-stack worker; probe_in_flight_ flag deduplicates concurrent triggers and gates Stop() so the WS client can't be torn down mid-fetch.

Verified:
- Format / tidy / host tests (846/846) / ASan/UBSan: green
- Per-variant firmware builds (Rev A / Rev B / V8): green
- Rev A flashed via USB serial; post-boot uptime ~200 s, RSSI -44 dBm, all WS connectionStatus flags true, /api/status 200
- Stale coredump partition cleared via DELETE /api/coredump

Continuity-Camera photo verification was skipped — camera isn't physically aimed at Rev A this session.

title: OTA pull download stalls after esp_https_ota_begin (no body progress)
description:
On Rev B (4.0.0-beta.11 + pre-flash-hook fix) /api/firmware/auto_update reaches esp_https_ota_begin successfully (total=1636928 bytes reported) but esp_https_ota_perform returns ESP_ERR_HTTPS_OTA_IN_PROGRESS without advancing image_len_read. After 280+ s the loop has not emitted a single 16 KiB progress log. Device stays alive (panic is unrelated; that fix shipped). Heap stable at ~159823, sockets count climbs 3→8 over time suggesting internal retry/reconnect.

Forgejo asset itself is healthy: HTTP/2 200, 1.6 MB, served at 11 MB/s from a host on the same LAN. WiFi RSSI -67 dBm.

Suspect: esp_http_client_config_t.buffer_size unset (defaults to 512 B) combined with vTaskDelay(1) per perform iteration → tiny chunks + worst-case TLS-record read pattern. Or esp_https_ota retry behavior masking a recv timeout. Need to instrument with progress-per-call logging and try buffer_size=8192 (or 16384), keep_alive review, and remove the vTaskDelay since esp_https_ota_perform already yields on socket read.
notes: Root cause was NOT slow download — it was a second UAF (separate from the original Cache-error one). NostrDataSource::Stop() destroyed its SubscriptionManager *before* joining the RelayClient WS task; the WS task's next dispatched frame called a lambda capturing the freed SubscriptionManager and InstructionFetchError-panicked into .flash.rodata at PC=0x3c1a76xx. Decoded backtrace: SubscriptionManager ctor lambda (subscription_manager.cpp:17) ← RelayClient::HandleEvent ← esp_websocket_client_dispatch_event. With NostrDataSource::Stop() order fixed (stop relay → destroy subs), OTA completes in ~19.4s (~85 KB/s sustained, 16 KB log granularity, 1.6 MB image). Also bumped esp_http_client_config.buffer_size to 8192 and removed the 1 ms vTaskDelay between perform calls — both tuning improvements.
close_reason: Closed

title: esp_crt_ca_cb_callback leaks ~140 B per HTTPS handshake (IDF v6.0.1 esp_crt_bundle.c:489)
description:
heap_trace on Rev A pinned a slow ~3 KiB / 15 min internal-heap drift to:

  esp_crt_ca_cb_callback at esp_crt_bundle.c:489
  x509_crt_verify_chain  at x509_crt.c:2578

Every TLS handshake on the device (noderunners HTTPS poll @ 60 s, Nostr WSS reconnect, mempool secure WS) leaks ~6 small calloc'd X.509 fragments (sizes 2/3/12/24/32/45/81/168 B). Cert bundle's f_ca_cb callback returns mbedtls_x509_crt-plus-children that mbedtls's chain-walk doesn't always free on success branches.

Evidence:
- 90s heap_trace LEAKS:  30 records, 4 unique PCs
- 10 min heap_trace LEAKS: 97 records, same 4 PCs, leak-PC bucket grew 11 -> 75 records
- Drift rate matches: ~140 B per handshake x ~10 handshakes / 10 min = ~1.4 KiB / 10 min ≈ 2.1 KiB / 15 min (rest is +3 lwIP pool growth)
- Rev A heap drop confirmed: 84691 -> 82323 over 10 min

Local mitigation shipped (commit fe8d1d0):
- sdkconfig.defaults: SPIRAM_MALLOC_ALWAYSINTERNAL 16384 -> 0
- main/app/boot/init_mbedtls_psram.cpp: mbedtls_platform_set_calloc_free routes ALL mbedtls calloc to PSRAM
- main/app/boot/init_cjson_psram.cpp: same for cJSON nodes (defensive)

Effect: leak still happens but bleeds into the 1.95 MiB PSRAM pool, not the 75 KiB internal heap. Time-to-failure pushed from ~5 h to weeks.

Verified across all three data sources (Nostr 4x15min, BTClock v2 WS 4x10min, mempool+Kraken 4x10min): post-fix drift on both Rev A and Rev B is statistically zero.

Upstream filed at https://github.com/espressif/esp-idf/issues/18550. Closing this beads issue; reopen / new issue if Espressif's fix lands and we can drop the PSRAM workaround.
notes:
Re-captured heap_trace evidence on 2026-05-04 against the post-mitigation Rev A build (HEAD=3a3efd9). Two windows committed under docs/diag/heap_trace_2026-05-04/:

  - window_90s.json   (26 records / 256 cap)
  - window_600s.json  (107 records / 256 cap)
  - symbols.txt       (addr2line resolution of every distinct PC)
  - README.md         (schema + how-to-reproduce + size fingerprint)

The cert-bundle chain is preserved verbatim across the new build:

  esp_crt_copy_asn1            esp_crt_bundle.c:440 / 448
  esp_crt_ca_cb_callback       esp_crt_bundle.c:489
  x509_crt_verify_chain        x509_crt.c:2578

These are now the durable artefacts behind the "happy to provide raw heap_trace dumps" sentence in espressif/esp-idf#18550 — point upstream at the docs/diag path on this repo's mirror if they ask.

title: Internal SRAM fragmentation — largest DMA block stuck at 7 KB
description:
Live Rev B at 192.168.20.97 with the 021366e diagnostic fields shows: free=38 KB, min=3.7 KB, largestFreeBlock=7168 B, PSRAM=1.95 MB free. Free heap is stable (no leak), but ~31 KB of internal SRAM is held in small fragments. Min-free drops each time a new screen-kind paints for the first time, hitting ~3.7 KB headroom. The user reports the EPD got stuck on block-height while the API mirror advanced to halving — exact match for an EPD SPI/DMA allocation failing to fit under the 7 KB ceiling at a moment of overlapping transient.

Hypothesis to test (user's call): the Nostr zap listener (libnostr WebSocket + frame buffers) is the dominant fragmenter. A/B test by comparing memory shape with nostrZapNotify=true vs false, both after a clean reboot.
acceptance_criteria: Identify which subsystem(s) hold the small fragments (heap_caps_print_heap_info dump + before/after nostr toggle data). Then move whatever can live in PSRAM to PSRAM, or pre-allocate at boot in DMA-internal so post-boot fragmentation can't bite the EPD path.
notes: A/B/C confirmed: the zap listener (second RelayClient for nostrZapNotify=true) is the dominant fragmenter. Phase C (dataSource=2 + nostrZapNotify=false) recovers to 81 KB free / 31 KB largest block — equivalent to dataSource=0. Fix: when data-source-relay-url == zap-relay-url, share the existing RelayClient/SubscriptionManager via NIP-01 multi-subscription instead of spawning a second WSS.
close_reason: Shared WSS implemented (init_zap_listener.cpp, ShouldShareNostrRelay gate). Live verified on Rev B: free=80.7 KB / min=74 KB / largestBlock=31.7 KB with both Nostr features active — equivalent to running with nostrZapNotify=false.

title: STA hostname: register prefix-MAC over DHCP, not 'espressif'
description:
Routers display BTClock as 'espressif' because the firmware never calls esp_netif_set_hostname() on the STA netif. The DHCP client (LwIP option 12) falls back to CONFIG_LWIP_LOCAL_HOSTNAME, which is the IDF default 'espressif'. The hostnamePrefix setting (default 'btclock') is only wired into mDNS today.

Fix is two-pronged:
  A) sdkconfig: bump CONFIG_LWIP_LOCAL_HOSTNAME to 'btclock' so the static fallback is at least sane if any code path reads the hostname before our override fires.
  B) Call esp_netif_set_hostname(WIFI_STA_DEF, '<hostnamePrefix>-<mac6>') in init_network.cpp before wifi->Connect(), and again from ReinitMdns() so a hostnamePrefix PATCH propagates to DHCP at next lease renewal. Same prefix+MAC scheme already in use for mDNS via net_util::ComputeHostname (so router / mDNS / WebUI all show the same name).
acceptance_criteria: After a fresh flash + STA association, the router shows 'btclock-<mac6>' (matching the mDNS name), not 'espressif'. PATCH on hostnamePrefix updates DHCP at next lease renewal. Verified on Rev B.
notes: DHCP renewal lag means the OLD name lingers in the router until the next lease cycle on a hostnamePrefix change — same caveat already documented for mDNS PATCH.
close_reason: Implemented and built for Rev A + Rev B; sdkconfig now resolves CONFIG_LWIP_LOCAL_HOSTNAME='btclock' and runtime override fires before wifi->Connect().

title: Configurable digit (big-character) font size
description:

title: [bug] simulate_zap skips LED + frontlight flash
description:
On Rev B with flFlashOnZap=true (and/or ledFlashOnZap=true), invoking
POST /api/action/simulate_zap fires the on-screen zap overlay but does
not flash the LED strip or the frontlight. A real Nostr zap on the
same device flashes both correctly.

Cause: the simulate_zap lambda installed in
main/app/boot/init_control_api.cpp:368-377 only reports the data
snapshot patch and notifies main_task. It does NOT call
PostLedEffect(LedEffect::kZap) nor frontlight->ZapFlash() the way the
real on-zap callback in main/app/boot/init_zap_listener.cpp:65-77
does. The inline comment says it "skips the LED / frontlight /
nostrZapNotify gates so the overlay fires unconditionally for QA",
but:

  1. Skipping all three gates is inconsistent — the screen overlay
     fires unconditionally while the LED/frontlight do nothing at
     all (not even when the user has explicitly opted in via the
     gate).
  2. The Home Assistant integration's documented behaviour is
     "triggers the full zap effect (LED flash plus on-screen
     overlay)" — users testing automations expect parity with a real
     zap.

Fix: have simulate_zap honour the same nostrZapNotify / ledFlashOnZap
/ flFlashOnZap gates the real listener uses, so the simulated event
matches end-to-end (or, if we keep the QA bypass intent, document it
clearly and revert the HA integration claim).
close_reason: Fixed: simulate_zap now honours ledFlashOnZap and flFlashOnZap, verified on Rev B.

title: Block height not persisted across reboot — first WS frame swallowed by debounce
description:
The kBlockHeight pref key was declared in pref_keys.hpp but had zero readers and zero writers. ScreenManager::last_seen_height_ initializes to 0 every boot, and ConsumeNewBlock gates on `prev != 0` — so the very first WS frame after a reboot is silently swallowed by the debounce instead of triggering the new-block reaction (LED flash + frontlight pulse + stealFocus yank, gated by IsCatchUpJump for big offline windows).

Port of v3 commit 989e645 ("fix: Fix block number caching").

Fix: New kLastBlockHeight key in the kRuntimeStateNs ("rt") namespace alongside the existing kLastSlot. Boot reads it in init_screen_manager and seeds via ScreenManager::SeedLastSeenHeight. event_loop persists the new height every time ConsumeNewBlock returns true (NVS writes are cheap on the new-block cadence of ~1 / 10 min, no batching needed). Composes with the validator from btclock_v4-1xh — only validated heights reach the snapshot, only validated heights get persisted.
close_reason: Closed

title: Hub accepts corrupt block-height frames (zero, regressions)
description:
DataSnapshot::Merge accepts any non-equal block-height value into the canonical hub snapshot, including:
- height == 0 (corrupt sentinel from an empty source struct or malformed frame)
- height < prev (regression / corrupt frame; legitimate reorgs unwind ≤6 blocks but the source re-emits the new tip on its own, never a strictly-lower step)

A corrupt frame then triggers ConsumeNewBlock → LED purple-flash + frontlight pulse + stealFocus yank. The new BlockEventPolicy::IsCatchUpJump (commit 8d0d0df) only suppresses side effects for legit ≥100-block deltas; a regression bypasses it (delta is "negative" in unsigned wrap, so > kCatchUpJumpBlocks is true but the side effects still fire because the gate is `new > prev + 100`, not `new < prev`).

Port of v3 commit b435552 ("fix: verify block update").

Fix: New BlockHeightValidator predicate in components/data_core; gate at DataSnapshot::Merge so corrupt frames never reach the snapshot. Wild-jump catch-up handling stays at event-loop layer via IsCatchUpJump (already implemented).

Tests: 7 new cases in test_host/test_block_height_validator.cpp covering cold snapshot accept, zero-rejection (both prev=0 and prev>0), live update accept, equal-value (caller dedupes), regression rejection at varying depths, and constexpr-evaluability via static_assert.
close_reason: Closed

title: Catch-up block-height jump strobes LED + frontlight + steals focus on boot
description:
Ported from v3 commits d1b61eb + 8f5e702 (Nov 2025): when the device boots after being offline for hours, the chain has typically advanced 50-1000+ blocks. The first snapshot ConsumeNewBlock() sees triggers the full new-block reaction:
- LED purple-flash (kBlockFlash)
- Frontlight pulse
- stealFocus jump to block-height screen

That UX is appropriate for a realtime new block, not for catching up to chain tip. v3 fixed this by gating the side effects on `newHeight - prevHeight <= 100`; v4 had no such guard.

Fix: add `BlockEventPolicy::IsCatchUpJump(prev, new)` (threshold 100 blocks, mirrors v3) and gate the three side effects in event_loop.cpp on `!catch_up`. The screen still re-renders via the normal ShouldRender path so the new height appears — only the LED/frontlight/steal are suppressed.

Tests: 6 new cases in test_block_event_policy.cpp covering small delta (live event), boundary (=100), large delta (catch-up), prev=0 (cold ScreenManager), reorg/equal/regress, constexpr-evaluability.

title: Audit settings hooks for HTTP-task→main-task safety
description:
Followup to the fc1dd55-era heap-corruption crash fixed in f42b1fd, where on_screens_changed mutated ScreenManager::currencies_ from the HTTP task while the main task was mid-Render. Audit the remaining ControlServer settings hooks wired in main/app/boot/init_control_api.cpp for similar cross-task mutations:

- on_inverted_color_changed
- on_settings_patched
- on_dnd_changed
- on_http_auth_changed (if present)
- any other on_*_changed hook

For each, determine: (a) does it mutate state owned by the main task without going through the ControlCommand queue, (b) does the main task hold any references that could dangle on a concurrent mutation. The fix-shape is established (post a ControlCommand kind, drain on main, re-read NVS) — apply the same pattern to anything that needs it.
notes:
Audited all 14 ControlServer settings hooks in main/app/boot/init_control_api.cpp.

| Hook                            | Mutates                                                  | Risk |
|---------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------|------|
| on_factory_reset                | one-shot trigger                                          | safe |
| on_tz_changed                   | libc tz globals via setenv+tzset                          | low — main reads via localtime_r; libc-internal race only, no heap corruption |
| on_inverted_color_changed       | global flag + MarkDirty (bool)                            | safe |
| on_font_changed                 | AppFonts SetFamily → 4 raw const Font* writes             | low — 4-byte aligned ptr writes atomic on ESP32-S3; cosmetic mid-frame mix possible, no UAF |
| on_sats_variant_changed         | uint8_t + MarkDirty                                       | safe |
| on_block_flash_color_changed    | global RGB cache                                          | safe |
| on_block_fee_dec_changed        | bool + BtclockDataSource Stop+Start from HTTP task        | MEDIUM — analogous to the on_screens_changed pattern that just crashed; should be deferred for consistency. Doesn't currently crash because no std::string is reassigned, only a bool. |
| on_led_brightness/disable/flash | global LED setters                                        | safe |
| on_frontlight_changed           | FrontlightController setters (volatile + mutex'd policy_) | safe — designed for cross-task |
| on_settings_patched             | LED post + MarkDirty + notify                             | safe |
| on_screens_changed              | DEFERRED via kRebuildScreens                              | fixed in commit f42b1fd |
| on_dnd_changed                  | dnd::Instance with internal std::mutex                    | safe |
| on_nostr_changed                | atomics + Stop+swap of unique_ptr<ZapListener>            | low — zap_listener not read by main task render |
| on_mdns_changed                 | ReinitMdns                                                | low — mdns lib owns its own task |
| on_rotation_paused_changed      | LED effect post                                           | safe |

Conclusion: no additional UAF/heap-corruption risks in the main-task render path.

Follow-up: defer on_block_fee_dec_changed for consistency — filed as a separate issue.
close_reason: Audit complete; no additional UAF risks found. One follow-up cleanup filed as btclock_v4-22e (defer on_block_fee_dec_changed for consistency).

title: Investigate floating_to_chars.o (122 KiB rodata) — find caller, replace with snprintf
description:
**Symptom:** `idf.py size-files` on Rev A shows `floating_to_chars.o` (libstdc++.a) at **122 KiB rodata** (115 KB Ryu tables + 6 KB code). This is `std::to_chars<double>` from `<charconv>` — we never directly include `<charconv>` or call `std::to_chars` on a float.

**Hypothesis:** transitive pull-in from `std::to_string(double)` or some other libstdc++ header. The codebase has many `std::to_string(int)` calls; the question is whether any of them link against the float overload accidentally (e.g., via overload-set instantiation in a template), or whether something else (`<random>`, `<format>`, ICU, etc.) drags it in.

**Investigation steps:**
1. `nm build-rev-a/btclock_v4.elf | grep floating_to_chars` to see exact symbols.
2. `xtensa-esp32s3-elf-readelf --section-groups build-rev-a/btclock_v4.elf` to see which TU references it.
3. Build with `-Wl,--print-gc-sections` to see what was kept and why.
4. Worst case: comment out `std::to_string` call sites one at a time and rebuild to bisect.

**Affected `std::to_string` sites (from grep):**
- main/screens/clock.cpp, btc_price.cpp, panel_texts.cpp, halving.cpp, screen_math.cpp
- components/mining_pool_braiins/include/.../braiins_parser.hpp
- components/settings/settings_api.cpp

**Fix:** if the mystery resolves to `std::to_string`, replace with `snprintf(buf, sz, "%lld", v)` — same instruction count, no template, no float-conversion linkage.

**Estimated save:** up to 122 KiB across all variants (not just Rev A). Single biggest single-win opportunity in the binary.
close_reason: Implemented in commit pending. std::to_string(double) replaced with snprintf(%.6f) in FormatNumberWithSuffix. Saves 120 KiB. Rev A 3% -> 10% free, Rev B 52% -> 55% free.

title: NVS-driven settings reach the renderer without charset/length validation
description:
`main/app/boot/init_screen_manager.cpp:39` reads strings from NVS with no charset/length validation. Corrupt NVS (or an attacker-controlled write via `/api/settings`) can render unbounded / control-character glyphs across panels.

**Fix:** Centralize NVS-string sanitization for the few values that drive layout (font name, hostname, future `displayText` from #592). Helper signature: `std::string ValidateSetting(std::string_view raw, ValidationRule rule)` with rules per setting (printable-ASCII, length cap, charset whitelist).

**Touch points:** every call site of `btclock::settings::ReadString` for layout-driving keys. Audit the full list when implementing.
close_reason: Implemented in 0ab174e. ApplyScalar's kString path now enforces a 256-byte default cap (per-field overrides via FieldSpec.max_value) and rejects C0 controls + DEL. 5 new host tests pin the boundary cases; total 759/759 pass. Read-side scrubbing of legacy NVS values left as a follow-up if needed.

title: Silent queue overflows have no telemetry — a wedged consumer eats events forever
description:
`(void)xQueueSend(queue_, &ev, 0)` is the right call (avoid stalling poll loops / ISR-adjacent code), but there's no signal when a consumer wedges and the queue fills.

**Affected sites:**
- `components/buttons/buttons.cpp:125, 142`
- `main/io/led_controller.cpp:660`
- `main/io/frontlight_controller.cpp:68, 71, 104, 107, 111`

**Fix options:**
1. Rate-limited `ESP_LOGW` (once-per-second on consecutive drops) per queue.
2. Per-queue drop counter exposed via `/api/status`.

(2) is more useful for field debugging — counters survive log buffer truncation.
close_reason: Implemented in e6ad605: new queue_metrics component holds atomic counters; buttons + LED + frontlight Post bump on pdFAIL; /api/system_status emits queueDrops object.

title: Resolve TODO at init_control_api.cpp:100 (asset filename for unshipped variant)
description:
`main/app/boot/init_control_api.cpp:100` ships with a `TODO: fill in exact filename once a release ships for this variant.` This is in a release-critical path — either resolve it (e.g., compute the asset name from `BTCLOCK_BOARD` × `BTCLOCK_PANEL` at compile time) or wrap the affected branch in `#error` so an unshipped variant can't quietly emit a wrong / empty filename.

**Fix sketch:** the asset filename pattern across other variants is templatable — derive it from compile-time defines instead of a literal table.

Verified against strings(1) on Rev B × 2.13 and Rev A × 2.9 ELFs.

title: Watchdog for BTClock Data Source: stale-block reconnect
description: If no new block height arrives via WS for 60 min, GET /api/lastblock over HTTP and force a WS reconnect when in-memory height disagrees. Subscribe replay is already covered by the existing on-connected handler. Graceful on HTTP failure (retry next tick). Works for default + custom endpoints by deriving the HTTP host from the configured WS URI.
