title: WASM AA mode mis-rotates verticalDesc label panels
description:
The wasm tool's anti-aliased preview path (`render*AlphaBuffer` bindings, exposed as the "Pixel + AA" mode in `tools/wasm/preview.html`) renders verticalDesc label panels in their pre-rotation logical layout instead of the rotated layout the device shows.

## Reproduction

1. `tools/wasm/build.sh`
2. Open `tools/wasm/preview.html`, switch to Pixel mode, enable "Anti-aliased (show alpha)", leave "Vertical description" checked (it is by default in the firmware).
3. Render Block height (or any screen with a `kLabelSplit` slot — block height, halving, fee rate, etc.).

The label panel (slot 0) shows "BLO" / "HEI" reading horizontally with the right side clipped, instead of the vertically-rotated "BLOCK / HEIGHT" the 1-bpp framebuffer mode shows correctly.

## Root cause

`main/screens/common.cpp::PaintSlotIntoFb` sets `lfb.rotation = Rotation::k90Cw` for `kLabel` / `kLabelSplit` slots. The framebuffer path goes through `SetPixelLandscape`, which folds that local rotation into the native pixel write — so the 1-bpp FB ends up correct after the global k180 inverse.

The alpha sidechannel in `tools/wasm/font_wasm_aa.cpp::WritePixel` writes at `(lx, ly)` *before* the rotation transform is applied. The label panel's k90Cw rotation never lands in the alpha buffer; the text ends up drawn horizontally in the upper-left of a 122×250 buffer, where it gets clipped past the panel's narrow horizontal extent.

This blocks the doc renderer (`tools/wasm/render_doc_screens.mjs`) from using the AA path for clean glyph edges — for now we resample the 1-bpp FB with Lanczos as a workaround.

## Fix sketch

`wasm_aa::WritePixel` needs to apply the same per-call `Rotation` that `SetPixelLandscape` applies. The `LandscapeFb::rotation` is in scope at the font.cpp call sites; thread it through the WritePixel call (or wrap both writes into a single helper that emits to both sinks with the rotation applied).

Smoke test should cover this: assert the alpha label panel has full-ink columns near `lx == W/2` (vertical text center) rather than ink concentrated near `(0, 0)`.
close_reason: Fixed in commits 4c0ab30 (font + wasm wiring) + db27a9f (renderer switch) + 30e07f1 (re-rendered docs/img). RotateLogicalToUserUpright threads the per-panel rotation through the AA sidechannel; smoke test now pins label-panel ink distribution to catch regressions. Verified Rev A + Rev B firmware both still build clean (font.cpp change is a no-op on device — wasm_aa hooks compile to inline empty stubs).

title: Add ASan + UBSan host-test build to CI
description:
Add a sanitizer-enabled host-test build that runs alongside the normal host_tests job. AddressSanitizer + UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer catch use-after-free, out-of-bounds reads, signed overflow, misaligned loads — bugs that boot fine on macOS local but misbehave on the ESP32-S3 in production.

## Implementation

1. **CMake option in `test_host/CMakeLists.txt`:**
   ```cmake
   option(BTCLOCK_HOST_TESTS_SANITIZE "Build host tests with ASan + UBSan" OFF)
   if(BTCLOCK_HOST_TESTS_SANITIZE)
     add_compile_options(-fsanitize=address,undefined -fno-omit-frame-pointer -O1 -g)
     add_link_options(-fsanitize=address,undefined)
   endif()
   ```
   Default OFF so existing builds are unchanged. `-O1` because ASan with `-O0` is glacial AND misses some optimizations' bugs; `-O1` is the standard sanitizer compromise.

2. **vendor/cJSON.c** is built with `-w` already; ASan instrumentation should still apply to it (we want the ASan checks even on vendored C). Verify it doesn't introduce sanitizer reports we have to NOLINT — if it does, add `set_source_files_properties(vendor/cJSON.c PROPERTIES COMPILE_FLAGS "-w -fno-sanitize=undefined")` (keep ASan, drop UBSan if cJSON has alignment quirks).

3. **CI job** in `.forgejo/workflows/host_tests.yaml` — add a second job `sanitize`:
   - Same base image as `host_tests`.
   - Install `build-essential cmake clang` (ASan/UBSan ship with both gcc and clang on Ubuntu 24.04 — gcc is fine; pick whichever the existing job uses for consistency).
   - Configure `cmake -S test_host -B build-host-san -DBTCLOCK_HOST_TESTS_SANITIZE=ON`.
   - Build, then run with `ASAN_OPTIONS=detect_leaks=1:abort_on_error=1` and `UBSAN_OPTIONS=print_stacktrace=1:halt_on_error=1` so the test binary exits non-zero on any sanitizer report.
   - **Gate the merge** — sanitizer reports indicate real bugs.

4. **README** — add subsection under `## Linting`:
   ```bash
   cmake -S test_host -B build-host-san -DBTCLOCK_HOST_TESTS_SANITIZE=ON
   cmake --build build-host-san
   ASAN_OPTIONS=detect_leaks=1 UBSAN_OPTIONS=print_stacktrace=1 \
     ./build-host-san/btclock_host_tests
   ```

## Verification

- Local: build with the option, run — expect 729/729 to still pass with no sanitizer reports. **If any sanitizer report fires on existing tests, the bug is real; fix it.** That's the whole point of adding this gate.
- Likely places for first-time finds: `test_screen_*`, `test_panel_texts`, anywhere that does pointer arithmetic on `std::array` slots, or `std::string::data()` writes.

## Out of scope

- ThreadSanitizer (TSan). Host tests are single-threaded; TSan adds value on the firmware itself, which we can't run under sanitizers without qemu.
- MemorySanitizer (MSan). Requires libc++ rebuild — not worth the operational cost.
- Sanitizers on the firmware. Not feasible without qemu; out of scope for the host-test focus.

## Notes for the agent

- `-fsanitize=address,undefined` is supported by gcc 8+ and clang 6+. CI's gcc-13 / clang-22 both work.
- Some UBSan checks are disabled by default in older toolchains; explicit `-fsanitize=undefined` covers the standard set including `signed-integer-overflow`, `null`, `vptr`, `bounds`. That's enough for first pass.
- macOS local: works with Apple clang. ASan reports stack traces with line numbers when the test binary is built with `-g` (already added by the option block).
- If the leak detector flags the static `kFields` schema array or doctest's static state, `LSAN_OPTIONS=suppressions=test_host/leak_suppressions.txt` is the escape hatch. Don't add it unless needed — start strict.
- Verify the existing `host_tests.yaml` job + ESP-IDF firmware builds are unaffected.
close_reason: Implemented in commit 30500d1: ASan+UBSan gating CI job + opt-in CMake option; 729/729 pass clean

title: Add code coverage (gcovr) for host tests
description:
Add a CMake-driven coverage build of the host test suite, plus a CI job that publishes the HTML report as an artifact.

## Implementation

1. **CMake option in `test_host/CMakeLists.txt`:**
   ```cmake
   option(BTCLOCK_HOST_TESTS_COVERAGE "Build host tests with gcov instrumentation" OFF)
   if(BTCLOCK_HOST_TESTS_COVERAGE)
     add_compile_options(--coverage -O0 -g)
     add_link_options(--coverage)
   endif()
   ```
   Default OFF so the standard `cmake -S test_host -B build-host` path stays fast and matches today's behaviour exactly.

2. **CI job** in `.forgejo/workflows/host_tests.yaml` — add a second job `coverage` (parallel to `host_tests`):
   - Image: `ghcr.io/catthehacker/ubuntu:js-24.04` (matches existing job).
   - Install `build-essential cmake gcovr`.
   - Configure `cmake -S test_host -B build-host-cov -DBTCLOCK_HOST_TESTS_COVERAGE=ON`.
   - Build, run binary, then `gcovr --root . --filter 'components/' --filter 'main/' --html-details build-host-cov/coverage.html --txt --print-summary --output build-host-cov/coverage.txt build-host-cov/`.
   - Upload `build-host-cov/coverage.html` and the per-file `*.html` siblings as a Forgejo artifact (retention 14 days).
   - Print the textual summary into the job log so the line-coverage % is visible without downloading the artifact.
   - **Do not gate** — informational only on first pass. Add a threshold later (separate issue) once a baseline is known.

3. **Filters** — exclude `test_host/vendor/` (cJSON, doctest), `test_host/test_*.cpp` themselves (we want coverage of code-under-test, not of tests), and any generated headers (e.g. `font_bundle_map.hpp`). Use `--exclude` flags rather than `--filter` if cleaner.

4. **README:** add a `## Coverage` subsection under `## Linting` documenting the local invocation:
   ```bash
   cmake -S test_host -B build-host-cov -DBTCLOCK_HOST_TESTS_COVERAGE=ON
   cmake --build build-host-cov && ./build-host-cov/btclock_host_tests
   gcovr --root . --filter 'components/' --filter 'main/' --html-details build-host-cov/coverage.html
   open build-host-cov/coverage.html
   ```

## Verification

- Local: configure with the option, build, run, generate HTML — verify a known-tested file (e.g. `components/btclock_data/include/btclock_data_parse.hpp` — exercised by `test_btclock_data_parse.cpp`) shows >50% line coverage.
- CI: confirm the new job appears, runs to completion, and the artifact is downloadable.

## Out of scope

- Coverage gating (fail-on-drop). File a follow-up after the first run reveals the baseline.
- Coverage of firmware-side TUs (would need running the binary on-device or under qemu).

## Notes for the agent

- macOS local runs need `gcovr` from brew (`brew install gcovr`); the `--coverage` flags work with both gcc and clang. If the host is using clang, the `*.gcno`/`*.gcda` artifacts go to the same place gcovr expects.
- Don't add coverage flags to `vendor/cJSON.c` — it already gets `-w`. Same for `vendor/doctest.h` (header-only, not compiled separately).
- Verify both ESP-IDF firmware build and existing `host_tests.yaml` job still work (CMake option default is OFF, so no behavioural change to either).

title: Umbrella: dead schema keys (wpTimeout, ledTestOnPower, inverseButtons, etc.)
description:
Several schema keys round-trip cleanly through GET/PATCH but no
firmware code reads them. Users see the toggle, save it, and nothing
changes. Group similar fixes per area to keep PRs reviewable.

| Key | Schema line | v3 reference | v4 status |
|---|---|---|---|
| `kWpTimeout` | `schema.hpp:227` | `defaults.hpp::DEFAULT_WP_TIMEOUT=15*60` | provisioning portal runs without a timeout |
| `kLedTestOnPower` | `schema.hpp:162` | `defaults.hpp::DEFAULT_LED_TEST_ON_POWER=true` | `init_boot_leds.cpp` always posts `kSetBoot` |
| `kInverseButtons` | `schema.hpp:149` | v3 button_handler.cpp:80 | `components/buttons/` does not read it |
| `kEnableDebugLog` | `schema.hpp:109` | v3 config.cpp:779 | not read at boot; ESP-IDF log level fixed at compile |
| `kTxPower` | `pref_keys.hpp:106` | v3 actions.cpp:154 persists value | live PATCH works (`/api/wifi_set_tx_power`) but pref is never re-read at boot, so power cycles drop user value |

**Suggested fix**: per-key resolution. Wire most up; for keys v4
architecturally cannot honor (e.g. `minSecPriceUpd` if WSS-push is the
only data source), remove the schema slot. Sub-issues can be filed as
each lands.

See `docs/HARDCODED_AUDIT.md` finding #7.

title: Frontlight flAlwaysOn / flDisable / flFlashOnUpd schema keys never read
description:
**Source**: schema declares `kFlAlwaysOn` (`schema.hpp:114`),
`kFlDisable` (`:115`), `kFlFlashOnUpd` (`:117`). Grep across `main/`
and `components/` (excluding `settings/` itself) shows zero read sites
for any of the three.

**v3 reference**: `btclock_v3_fci/src/lib/system/defaults.hpp:21,52`
defines `DEFAULT_FL_ALWAYS_ON=true`, `DEFAULT_DISABLE_FL=false`,
`DEFAULT_FL_FLASH_ON_UPDATE=true`. Each toggled distinct frontlight
behaviour: `flAlwaysOn` overrode the ambient-off rule, `flDisable`
muted the controller entirely, `flFlashOnUpd` flashed on
block/price events.

**Suggested fix**: wire all three through the same forwarder added in
btclock_v4-7xv (frontlight live PATCH). `flAlwaysOn` gates the
ambient-auto-off branch; `flDisable` short-circuits Post() before the
queue; `flFlashOnUpd` adds a flash event in the block/price update
paths analogous to `flFlashOnZap`.

**Rationale**: P2 — three user-visible Rev B settings do nothing.

See `docs/HARDCODED_AUDIT.md` finding #6.
close_reason: Fixed in f923269. flAlwaysOn / flDisable / flFlashOnUpd are now read by FrontlightController::Post() with precedence flDisable > flAlwaysOn > flFlashOnUpd. Hardware-verified on Rev B.

title: Frontlight runtime prefs persist but PATCH does not apply live
description:
**Source**: `main/app/boot/init_hardware.cpp:97-133` reads
`kLuxLightToggle`, `kFlOffWhenDark`, `kFlMaxBrightness`,
`kFlEffectDelay` once at boot. `init_control_api.cpp:174` only
marks the screen dirty on PATCH; no frontlight forwarder exists.

The schema flags these as `boot_only=false` (`schema.hpp:114-122`),
so the WebUI doesn't prompt for reboot — but a PATCH has no visible
effect until the next power cycle.

**v3 reference**: `btclock_v3_fci/src/main.cpp:31-47` — the ambient
loop re-read `flOffWhenDark` and `luxLightToggle` on each tick. v4
removed the per-tick read for performance, fine, but the PATCH-time
hook to push new values into `FrontlightController` was never added.

**Suggested fix**: add `on_frontlight_settings_changed(...)` to
`ControlServer::Config`, fired from `ApplyPatch()` whenever any of
`kLuxLightToggle`, `kFlOffWhenDark`, `kFlMaxBrightness`,
`kFlEffectDelay` is touched. Forward to
`FrontlightController::Set{LuxThreshold,OffWhenDark,
ConfiguredBrightness,EffectDelay}` (already exposed).

**Rationale**: P2 — UX bug (Rev B only). The settings panel pretends
the changes are live; they aren't.

See `docs/HARDCODED_AUDIT.md` finding #5.
close_reason: Fixed in f923269 (fix/frontlight-live-patch). Verified on Rev B hardware: brightness, flAlwaysOn, flDisable, luxLightToggle all live-PATCH without reboot. flFlashOnUpd persistence verified; block-flash gate not exercised (needs real block).

title: LED brightness/disable/flashOnUpd PATCH no-ops (separate "led" namespace)
description:
**Source**: `main/io/led_controller.cpp:31-35`

```cpp
constexpr const char* kNvsNamespace = "led";
constexpr const char* kKeyBrightness = "brightness";
constexpr const char* kKeyDisable = "disable";
constexpr const char* kKeyFlashUpdate = "flashUpdate";
```

`kLedBrightness="ledBrightness"`, `kDisableLeds="disableLeds"`,
`kLedFlashOnUpd="ledFlashOnUpd"` into `kSettingsNs="settings"` — those
keys are dead. Only `kBlockFlashColor` is mirrored at boot
(`init_boot_leds.cpp:46-48`).

**v3 reference**: `btclock_v3_fci/src/lib/system/defaults.hpp:8-11`
declares all four with non-zero defaults. v4 schema
(`schema.hpp:158,101,159`) preserves the defaults but no bridge to the
`led` namespace.

**Suggested fix**: at boot, mirror `settings/ledBrightness` →
`led/brightness`, `settings/disableLeds` → `led/disable`,
`settings/ledFlashOnUpd` → `led/flashUpdate` (same pattern as the
existing `blockFlashColor` mirror in `init_boot_leds.cpp`). Add live
forwarders in `init_control_api.cpp` so PATCH applies without reboot.

**Rationale**: P2 — three user-visible LED toggles do nothing today.

See `docs/HARDCODED_AUDIT.md` finding #4.
close_reason: Fixed by 75c9f5b (LED settings now read from canonical 'settings' namespace, live PATCH supported).

title: Boot splash text hardcoded — restore v3 displayText pref
description:
**Source**: `main/boot_ui.cpp:8`

```cpp
constexpr const char* kSplashLetters = "BTCLOCK!";
```

The boot-time splash spells one letter of `BTCLOCK` per panel (and `!`
on V8's 8th panel). The literal is fixed at compile time.

**v3 reference**: `btclock_v3_fci/src/lib/drivers/epd/epd.cpp:151`

```cpp
String customText = preferences.getString("displayText", DEFAULT_BOOT_TEXT);
```

v3 used `displayText` (`pref_keys.hpp::DisplayText`,
`defaults.hpp::DEFAULT_BOOT_TEXT="BTCLOCK"`) as the boot splash and as
the buffer the `/api/show/text` endpoint writes into. v4 has no
`displayText` key in the schema or `pref_keys.hpp` at all.

**Suggested setting**: `kDisplayText` (string, default `"BTCLOCK"`,
boot-only — splash paints once). Pad/truncate to NUM_SCREENS at read.

**Rationale**: P2 — direct UX impact, lost feature from v3. Users
who powered on a custom-branded device today can't change the splash.

See `docs/HARDCODED_AUDIT.md` finding #3.

title: Zap listener relay + pubkey read from wrong NVS namespace
description:
**Source**: `main/app/boot/init_zap_listener.cpp:31-37`

```cpp
Prefs zap_prefs("nostr");
const bool zap_enable = zap_prefs.GetBool("zapEnable", true);
```

description: After the GxEPD2 driver port (commit 7355319), the initial 3-transition acceptance test (block height → sats/USD → ticker → mining) was clean across all six photos. However, a later transition path (mining → auto-rotated to Bitaxe → force20 ticker) produced faded panels on indices 3 and 4. notes: Not confirmed reliably reproducible — agent was about to rerun when halted. Possible causes: (1) shadow buffer drift across auto-rotation ticks because the auto-advance path doesn't feed its last-rendered frame into shadow_ the same way /api/screen/next does; (2) partial-waveform fatigue when consecutive transitions accumulate without an intervening full refresh (fullRefreshMin should clamp this but may not engage for short intervals); (3) interaction with RefreshPolicy's stale-frame counter.\n\nPlanned after btclock_v4-2zo (invertedColor=true full-refresh hook). Do not reopen the EPD driver for speculative fixes — reproduce first with a scripted sequence: /api/screen/next x N with 10s sleeps, photographing each.

Root cause: SSD1680 doesn't auto-copy 0x24→0x26 after partial activate, so 0x26 stayed stuck on whatever the last full refresh wrote there. title: refactor(screens): decouple cell-diff-reset from EPD full-refresh mode
description:
Partial-refresh-on-screen-change was the whole point of honoring refrScrnChange=false + fullRefreshMin, but the current implementation can't do it.

## The coupling

Every data renderer (block_height, moscow_time, etc.) derives BOTH its cell-diff mask AND the EPD refresh mode from the same 'prev_value' parameter:

```cpp
const bool full_refresh = (prev_height == 0);  // EPD mode
update[i] = full_refresh || new_digits[i] != old_digits[i];  // cell diff
PaintDataScreen(..., label_full_refresh, ...);  // → PaintDataScreen's full_refresh arg
```

So to force cell repaint on a screen transition (block-height via /api/show/screen?s=0), screen_manager.cpp passes prev_value=0. That correctly makes all cells update — but also forces EPD full refresh regardless of what the refresh policy decided.

## What 777fb0a actually shipped

Band-aid: added force_repaint = screen_change_pending_ || dirty_ || force_full; used it to drive the prev_value=0 sentinel. Transitions now repaint (bug fixed) but they're always full-refresh. Commit message flags the issue and promises a follow-up.

## Proper fix

Add a separate bool full_refresh_mode parameter to each renderer function, independent from prev_value:

- prev_value → drives update[] (cell diff)
- full_refresh_mode → passed to PaintDataScreen's full_refresh arg (EPD mode)

ScreenManager then passes:
- prev_value = force_repaint ? sentinel : last_rendered_X
- full_refresh_mode = force_full (from RefreshPolicy::Decide)

## Scope

10 renderers to update (block_height, moscow_time, btc_price, fee_rate, clock, halving, bitcoin_supply, market_cap, mining_pool, bitaxe). Plus nostr_zap + show_custom + debug if they follow the same pattern. screen_manager.cpp call sites.

Tests: SHA-256 framebuffer hash pattern (per C.1's /tmp/bh_baseline.mjs) to confirm visual parity in full-mode AND confirm partial-mode actually exercises the partial path without ghosting the previous frame's content.

## User impact

With the band-aid in place, every screen rotation tick does a full EPD refresh → panels flash white between screens. User wanted partial-refresh for a cleaner rotation; the periodic fullRefreshMin sweep is the ghost-clear. Current behavior is effectively refrScrnChange=true regardless of pref.
close_reason:
Decoupled full_refresh_mode from prev_value in all 14 data renderers. Commit 1ae03f3.

## Changes

- Added bool full_refresh_mode arg to every Render<Screen>Screen template (block_height, moscow_time, btc_price, fee_rate, clock, halving, bitcoin_supply, market_cap, mining_pool_hashrate, mining_pool_earnings, bitaxe_hashrate, bitaxe_best_diff, nostr_zap, show_custom) in main/screens/screens.hpp.
- Renamed the old cell-diff-reset signal to cell_diff_reset in each .cpp so the intent is obvious when reading the renderer body. PaintDataScreen's full_refresh arg now takes full_refresh_mode directly; cell_diff_reset only drives the update[] mask OR-in so every cell repaints on transitions even at partial EPD mode.
- ScreenManager::Render now passes prev_value = force_repaint ? sentinel : last_rendered_X AND full_refresh_mode = force_full. force_repaint = force_full || screen_change_pending_ || dirty_.
- Updated tools/wasm/binding.cpp (both pixel and alpha variants) to pass full_refresh_mode=true so preview output stays bit-identical to main.
- Extended the WASM shim EpdPanel to capture last RefreshKind + count; added renderBlockHeightWithMode binding so /tmp/bh_mode_verify.mjs can prove the decoupling at the framebuffer level.

## fullRefreshMin honored

Confirmed fullRefreshMin is now honored end-to-end after this fix. The pure-logic RefreshPolicy::Decide was already correct (pinned by test_refresh_policy.cpp) — the previous bug was that renderers hard-coded full_refresh = (prev==sentinel), which 777fb0a set to true on every transition, overriding the policy. With the new arg the policy's decision flows through: screen-change within fullRefreshMin window → kPartial, past window → kFull.

## Verification

- Host tests: 594 pass (added one fullRefreshMin=60 scenario).
- IDF builds clean on REV_A, REV_B, V8.
- WASM smoke test: all pass.
- Framebuffer hashes: 32 test inputs across 7/8-panel variants, bit-identical pre-vs-post refactor.
- Decoupling verification (bh_mode_verify.mjs): 13/13 checks pass — confirms full=true→kFull, full=false+sentinel→kPartial+all cells paint, full=false+match→kPartial+0 cells paint, full=true+match→kFull+all cells paint.

title: Provisioning: verify WiFi creds before save; auto-fallback to portal on sustained failure
description:
## The bug

`ProvisioningServer::HandleWifi` (components/webserver/provisioning_server.cpp:206) accepts any SSID/password, writes them to NVS, and reboots — no attempt is made to actually associate with the AP before committing. Symptom: typo the password → device reboots into STA mode → loops forever on `wifi: disconnected reason=202` (AUTH_FAIL) → user must erase NVS via esptool (`esptool erase_region 0x9000 0x5000`) to recover.

This is a regression from the Arduino-era firmware which used WiFiManager's try-connect-then-save pattern.

Observed on V8 during first hardware bring-up on 2026-04-23 — stale Arduino-era creds in NVS, AP no longer accepts them, no self-recovery path without physical USB reflash access.

## Fixes (two parts)

### (1) Verify before save

In `HandleWifi`:
1. WiFi is already in APSTA (see components/wifi/wifi.cpp:170); keep SoftAP up.
2. Call `wifi.Connect(ssid, pw)` and wait up to ~15 s for `STA_GOT_IP` OR a `WIFI_EVENT_STA_DISCONNECTED` with a terminal reason (AUTH_FAIL=202, NO_AP_FOUND=201, ASSOC_FAIL=203, HANDSHAKE_TIMEOUT=204, CONNECTION_FAIL=205).
3. On success → save to NVS + respond 200 + `esp_restart()` after short delay.
4. On failure → respond 4xx with a JSON error body naming the reason (so the WebUI can surface 'wrong password' / 'SSID not found' / 'timeout'), keep portal running, don't save.

### (2) N-strikes fallback

In main.cpp / wifi_guard: if STA fails to get an IP N consecutive times (e.g. 10 attempts over 2 minutes) with AUTH_FAIL or NO_AP_FOUND reasons, clear the `net/ssid` pref and `esp_restart()` — device comes back up in provisioning mode. Catch-all for bricking via non-portal paths (old NVS from a different firmware, manual NVS write, AP renamed, etc.).

## Acceptance

- Provisioning portal with correct creds: saves + reboots + boots into data screens (existing happy path).
- Provisioning portal with wrong password: portal returns 4xx, EPD provisioning screen stays up, user can retry without flashing anything.
- Device currently running with stale/wrong creds in NVS: after 10 sustained auth failures, auto-boots back into provisioning portal.

## Risk

- APSTA connect attempt may briefly knock other portal clients off the SoftAP. Acceptable; portal client is the same user typing the creds.
- Wait-for-IP timeout must be long enough for slow DHCP (15 s ok) but not so long the portal feels dead (cap feedback at 15 s).
- N-strikes must NOT fire on transient outages (router reboot, etc.). Gate on disconnect reason — transient disconnects (AUTH_EXPIRE/ASSOC_LEAVE) don't count; only terminal reasons do.
close_reason: Implemented in commit aa89376 on main. Verify-before-save in ProvisioningServer::HandleWifi (15s TryConnect + structured 4xx error codes), N-strikes fallback in wifi_guard (10 terminal disconnects → clear net/ssid + esp_restart). Rev A/B compile regression from 93ca2b5 fixed in 95d70de.

title: Claude Code worktree isolation: agents get empty tree in this repo
description:
Sub-agents launched with isolation: worktree in this repo get a checkout rooted at git merge-base HEAD origin/main, which resolves to 525f43d (Apr 21) — 125 commits BEFORE the IDF PoC was merged. The idf_cpp_proto/ directory doesn't exist in that tree, so agents briefed to work on the PoC have no files to edit.

## Observed behaviour
- Multiple sub-agents launched across this session with isolation: worktree: dm9 (/api/status), jwz (settings schema), egh+xgv (DND + screen-rotation pause), parity (block-height 7-digit fix), zap-listener, SSE /events, data-handler decoration modes.
- All of them detected an empty tree and silently fell back to editing the primary checkout (/Users/padjuri/src/btclock_v3_fci).
- Because all 'isolated' agents actually share the same working tree, their edits race. Example: the SSE agent and data-handler agent both running concurrently produced a Rev A linker error on RenderMarketCapScreen<7> instantiation because data-handler changed the template signature while SSE was mid-build.

## Root cause
Claude Code's worktree add logic bases the new branch at merge-base(HEAD, origin/main). That's a sensible default for branches that regularly rebase onto main, but this project has a long-lived feature branch (feature/idf-cpp-poc) that has never been merged to main — so the merge-base is stuck far behind HEAD.

## Workaround in place
- CLAUDE.md updated with a 'do NOT use isolation: worktree' note.
- Future sub-agent launches should omit the isolation flag and accept single-checkout serialization.

## Permanent fixes (not yet taken)
1. Fast-forward 'main' to 'feature/idf-cpp-poc' HEAD. This would make merge-base = HEAD and restore worktree isolation. BUT 'main' is a durable ref and moving it has semantic weight — user decision required.
2. File upstream with Claude Code: add a per-repo config or sub-agent flag to base new worktrees at HEAD of current branch instead of the merge-base with origin/main.

## Evidence
- .claude/worktrees/agent-<id> has files like boards/, ci/, CMakeLists.txt, dependencies.lock — the OLD Arduino project top level — and no idf_cpp_proto/.
- 'git log worktree-agent-<id> -1' shows HEAD at 525f43d chore(data): bump submodule for dependency updates (Apr 21 2026).
- 'git merge-base HEAD origin/main' in this repo returns 525f43d.

title: NWC: client state machine in components/nwc/
description:
New component `components/nwc/` orchestrating the JSON-RPC layer over Nostr events.

## State machine
- bootstrap: subscribe to kind 13194 INFO event from the wallet pubkey to discover supported methods + encryption variants (NIP-44 v2 vs NIP-04).
- subscribe: one REQ to the wallet relay with filter { kinds: [23195, 23196], "#p": [our_pubkey] } — covers both JSON-RPC responses (23195) AND notifications (23196) on the same subscription. Saves one REQ slot and one cJSON tree per subscription on the relay client.
- idle: connected, refresh-tick driven balance polling via get_balance + reactive notification handling.
- in-flight: sent kind 23194 request, awaiting matching kind 23195 response (matched on `e` tag = request event id). Timeout 10 s.
- reconnect: exponential backoff if WSS drops; rebuild subscription on reconnect.

## Methods (v1)
- get_info (handshake) — capability + encryption variant discovery.
- get_balance (refresh tick) — polls every refresh_secs (default 60).

## Notifications (kind 23196) — v1 in scope
The wallet pushes encrypted kind 23196 events when payments arrive or are sent. Decrypt via the same dispatcher as 23195 responses. Payload shape per NIP-47:

  { notification_type: "payment_received" | "payment_sent",
    notification: { payment_hash, amount, fees_paid, created_at, expires_at, settled_at, description, description_hash, preimage, payer_pubkey, metadata } }

Dispatch flow:
- decode notification_type + amount + description.
- update NwcDataSource cached balance immediately (don't wait for next get_balance poll).
- fan out to UI subscribers: trigger the transient notification screen (issue lwf.6) + push SSE event so WebUI can flash a toast.

## WSS handle
Dedicated WSS for NWC (NWC relay URL != price/zap relay 99% of the time). Reuse `RelayClient` to instantiate a second socket. Steady-state RAM delta ~35-50 KiB heap (mostly TLS session, fits PSRAM). Relay-budget invariant from lwf.4 ensures TOTAL concurrent WSS stays <=4 — same internal-RAM ceiling as today.

## Files
- components/nwc/include/nwc/client.hpp
- components/nwc/src/client.cpp — state machine.
- components/nwc/src/jsonrpc.cpp — request build (kind 23194) + response decode (kind 23195) + notification decode (kind 23196).

## Verification
- Host test: mock relay sending crafted kind 23195 responses and kind 23196 notifications, verify state machine transitions, request/response matching, and notification dispatch.
- Host test: subscription filter contains both kinds.
- Integration test plan: pair against an Alby Hub instance on a dev relay; trigger an incoming sat to verify notification path end-to-end.
notes: Boot wiring + event-loop dispatch landed in commit 805f75c (feat(nwc): boot wiring + event-loop dispatch for payment notifications). InitNwc constructs dedicated RelayClient + SubscriptionManager + NwcClient; refresh tick is an esp_timer driving get_balance at nwcRefreshSecs cadence. SetOnPayment patches DataSnapshot and raises nwc_notify_pending so the event-loop pops the kNwcPaymentNotify overlay. RefreshNwcSettings handles runtime PATCH updates for refresh_secs + flash gate; URI + enabled remain boot-only per the schema's rebootRequired flag.

## Relay-budget invariant (3 + 1 dynamic split)

Total concurrent WSS to nostr-style servers must stay <= kMaxNostrRelays = 4 (internal-RAM ceiling). When NWC is enabled, the NWC relay counts as one of the four. Enforce:

  total = data_relays.size() + (nwc.enabled ? 1 : 0)
  reject if total > 4

Validation lives in:
- components/settings/settings_api.cpp — PATCH /api/settings/nwc must check the math (refuse enable if data_relays already = 4).
- components/settings/settings_api.cpp — PATCH /api/nostrRelays must check the math too (refuse adding a 4th data relay if NWC is enabled).
- data/src/lib/features/settings/sections/NostrRelayList.svelte — dynamic MAX_DATA_RELAYS = MAX_NOSTR_RELAYS - (nwcEnabled ? 1 : 0), show the dynamic cap to the user.

NVS schema: no break — existing nostrRelays array stays, just gets a tighter dynamic cap when NWC is on. Migration on enable: if user has 4 data relays at enable-time, return HTTP 400 with `{"error":"max 3 data relays when NWC is enabled; drop one first"}` — no silent truncate.

- components/settings/settings_api.cpp — endpoints + budget enforcement.
- components/webserver/control_server.cpp — register the trampolines (or one multiplexed handler).

- Possibly new data/src/lib/features/settings/sections/NwcSettings.svelte for the NWC URI + enable toggle.

## Verification
- Host test: parse round-trip of a valid NWC URI; reject malformed (wrong scheme, short pubkey, invalid relay).
- Host test: relay-budget enforcement on PATCH (4-relay user enables NWC -> 400; NWC-enabled user tries to add 4th data relay -> 400).
- max_uri_handlers budget check: confirm we're at <=49/50 after this lands.

## Acceptance

- WebUI shows dynamic budget.

title: NWC: implement NIP-44 v2 + NIP-04 encrypt/decrypt + dispatcher
description:
Add `components/nostr/src/nip4x.cpp` exposing encrypt(pubkey, plaintext) / decrypt(pubkey, ciphertext) dispatching on encryption variant tag.

## NIP-44 v2 (primary)
- mbedTLS ECDH on secp256k1 curve to derive 32-byte shared X (verify this gives raw X, not SHA-hashed compressed point — §8 open question).
- HKDF-Extract (shared_x, salt='nip44-v2') -> conversation_key (32 B).
- HKDF-Expand (conversation_key, nonce) -> chacha_key (32 B) + chacha_nonce (12 B) + hmac_key (32 B).
- Pad plaintext to next power-of-2 boundary per NIP-44 v2 padding scheme.
- ChaCha20 stream encrypt with chacha_key + chacha_nonce.
- HMAC-SHA256(hmac_key, aad || ciphertext) -> mac (32 B).
- Output: version (1 B = 0x02) || nonce (32 B) || ciphertext || mac, then base64.

## NIP-04 (fallback)
- mbedTLS ECDH on secp256k1 curve -> shared X (same as above).
- AES-256-CBC encrypt with PKCS#7 padding using a random 16-byte IV.
- Format: base64(ciphertext) + "?iv=" + base64(iv).

## Dispatcher
- Inspect target wallet's kind 13194 INFO event 'encryption' tag (added to NIP-47 in 2024). Prefer 'nip44-v2'; fall back to 'nip04' otherwise.
- If tag is missing entirely: default to NIP-04 (product decision per §8 open question).

## Verification
- Host test: NIP-44 v2 spec vectors verbatim from https://github.com/nostr-protocol/nips/blob/master/44.md#test-vectors.
- Host test: NIP-04 round-trip with known fixed keypair pair.
- Confidence test: encrypt with NIP-44 v2, decrypt — match plaintext for ≥10 random key+plaintext combos.

## Files
- New: components/nostr/include/nostr/nip4x.hpp
- New: components/nostr/src/nip4x.cpp
- New: test_host/test_nip4x.cpp
notes: Measured Rev A flash cost (anchor-pinned, all symbols linked): +8,560 B (~8.4 KiB) vs main baseline 1,729,808 B. Hand-rolled-vs-mbedTLS deltas: AES-256 +1.5 KiB, SHA+HMAC +0.8 KiB, base64 +0.4 KiB. Net +2.2 KiB vs research §2's 6.2 KiB mbedTLS-reuse estimate. Offset: lwf.1 (CHACHA20_C+HKDF_C in sdkconfig, planned +4.0 KiB) is no longer needed - hand-rolled path makes those mbedTLS modules unnecessary. Scenario 3 projection updates to ~28 KiB total (was 25.8 KiB plan); Rev A margin ~10.7 KiB. Safe.

title: NWC: enable secp256k1 schnorr sign-side + pin ECMULT_GEN_PREC_BITS=4
description:
Today only `secp256k1_schnorrsig_verify` is linked; we need sign-side for NIP-01 event signing in NWC requests (kind 23194).

## Steps
- Ensure ENABLE_MODULE_SCHNORRSIG stays on in components/secp256k1/CMakeLists.txt.
- Pin ECMULT_GEN_PREC_BITS=4 explicitly so an IDF bump doesn't change the precomputed table size on us (table is ~8 KiB rodata at PREC_BITS=4; doubles at PREC_BITS=2 and PREC_BITS=8 ladder up).
- Add a thin nostr_sign.cpp under components/nostr/src/ that calls secp256k1_keypair_create + secp256k1_schnorrsig_sign32 with a deterministic nonce function, so the sign-side symbols actually get linked. No callers yet from app code; the impl block waits for the NIP-44/04 issue.

## Verification
- Host test: BIP-340 test vectors for both verify (already pass today) and sign.
- `nm --size-sort build-rev-a/btclock_v4.elf | grep -E 'schnorrsig_sign|keypair_create|ecmult_gen'` shows expected symbols.
- Measure flash delta vs the ~8–12 KiB estimate, update §8.

## Risks
- Linker may pull additional transitive helpers (secp256k1_ec_seckey_negate, secp256k1_ec_pubkey_serialize). If delta > 12 KiB, file a sub-issue and re-evaluate scenario 3 fit.
notes:
Closed: components/nostr/src/event_sign.cpp lands with BIP-340 spec
vectors 0-3 green in test_host/test_event_sign.cpp. All four spec
fixtures produce bit-identical 64-byte signatures (sk in {3, 1, ...},
msg ∈ {0, π-digits, full-256-bit, all-0xFF}). VerifyEvent roundtrip
against a self-signed kind 23194 (NWC request) also green.

ENABLE_MODULE_ECDH was NOT enabled — every secp256k1 primitive we
need is exposed through the existing verify-side public API. The
precomputed_ecmult_gen table stayed DCE'd in all three variant builds
(verified via xtensa-esp32s3-elf-nm). secp256k1_schnorrsig_sign32 +
secp256k1_keypair_create are also NOT linked: BIP-340 is hand-rolled
on top of seckey_negate / seckey_tweak_add / seckey_tweak_mul /
ec_pubkey_tweak_mul, the same pattern used by lwf.3 for ECDH.

Cost (when lwf.4/.5 wire the calling sites): ~2.5 KiB code (signer +
local SHA-256 + tagged-hash) — well below the 8-12 KiB the research
doc estimated for the gen-table path.

description:

## Steps

title: Epic: Nostr Wallet Connect (NIP-47) — NIP-44 v2 + NIP-04 fallback
description:
Add NIP-47 (Nostr Wallet Connect) as a feature to BTClock with both NIP-44 v2 (must-have, forward-looking) and NIP-04 (fallback, ~1 KiB extra, keeps interop with legacy wallets).

## v1 in scope

- `get_balance` (primary refresh tick) + `get_info` (handshake / capability discovery).
- **NIP-47 notifications kind 23196** — `payment_received` and `payment_sent` events pushed by the wallet, decrypted via the NIP-44 v2 / NIP-04 dispatcher, surfaced as a transient screen + SSE event for the WebUI. (Subscribed alongside kind 23195 responses on the same REQ filter — ~0.3 KiB extra plumbing.)
- Single-wallet (single NWC URI).

## Target scenario

Scenario 3 from the sizing study: NIP-44 v2 + NIP-04 fallback + balance + notifications. Fits Rev A's 38.7 KiB OTA headroom with ~13 KiB margin (mid ~26 KiB Δ, worst-case 95% CI ~31 KiB Δ).

Full scenario (outgoing payments / tx history) is gated behind CONFIG_BTCLOCK_NWC_FULL — Rev B / V8 only; worst-case CI overshoots Rev A.

## Relay-budget invariant (≤ 4 total WSS, dynamic 3 + 1 split)

`kMaxNostrRelays = 4` is the internal-RAM ceiling on concurrent WSS+TLS sessions. NWC's relay is almost always distinct from data-source / zap relays. Keep the hard limit at 4 total; when NWC is enabled, allow at most 3 data relays + the 1 NWC relay. Enforce in settings_api.cpp on PATCH /api/settings/nwc and PATCH /api/nostrRelays; WebUI mirrors the dynamic budget. No NVS schema break — existing nostrRelays array stays; on enable check `data.size() + (nwc.enabled ? 1 : 0) <= 4`, reject with clear 400 if violated (no silent truncate).

## Dominant flash cost

secp256k1 schnorr **sign**-side + precomputed_ecmult_gen table: ~8–12 KiB. Currently only verify is linked. NIP-44 v2 primitives (ChaCha20 + HKDF) ~4 KiB combined. NIP-04 adds ~1 KiB on top because AES-CBC + base64 + secp256k1-curve ECDH-via-mbedTLS are already linked. Notification subscription + screen ~+1 KiB.

## Reference

Full sizing study, scenario breakdown, relay-budget invariant, open-questions list in docs/research/nwc_nip47_estimate.md. Implementation sequencing tracked as child issues of this epic.

## Out of scope v1

- Outgoing payments (`pay_invoice` / `make_invoice` / `pay_keysend` / `sign_message`) — scenario 4, child issue lwf.7, gated to Rev B / V8.
- `list_transactions` history pagination — same scenario 4 issue.
- Multi-wallet / multi-NWC-URI support — single wallet only in v1.
- LNURL-pay / LNURL-withdraw beyond what NWC's pay_invoice gives us (no LNURL plumbing).
notes: 2026-05-12: notification overlay regressed during end-to-end loop; child lwf.9 created with full evidence and architecture handoff. cf9394e fragmented-frame fix is correct and must stay; remaining work is queue+worker decoupling so WS RX task does not run NIP-44 decrypt on its small stack. See bd memory nwc-handoff-2026-05-12.

title: font.cpp glyph_buf() singleton is niet thread-safe
description:

Vandaag is dit veilig (single-threaded render via main task), maar als ooit een tweede caller wordt toegevoegd (bijv. de WS preview worker raakt dezelfde render-pad) → silent data corruption. Latente bug, geen crash vandaag.

Twee opties: (a) documenteren met comment dat dit single-threaded is en assert + check op task handle, of (b) guarden met een mutex. Optie (a) is goedkoper en past bij het huidige threadingmodel.
acceptance_criteria: Of een korte mutex/guard, of een expliciete assert + WHY-only comment dat documenteert waarom dit single-threaded is. Voorkomt regressie als toekomstige code per ongeluk vanuit andere taken rendert.

title: Suffix-compact formatters render "1000K" instead of "1.0M" at decade boundary
description:
Four formatters in v4 share the same shape:
1. Pick suffix from raw value via `if (v >= 1e6) suffix = M; v /= 1e6;`
2. Render with `%.0f` or `%.1f`
3. When the divided value rounds up across the next-decade boundary (e.g. 999.5K → "1000K"), the user sees a value with a "wrong" suffix one rung lower than the actual magnitude.

Affected formatters:
- main/screens/screen_math.cpp:63-150 — `FormatNumberWithSuffix` (Market Cap, Bitcoin Supply)
- components/bitaxe/src/bitaxe_parser.cpp:12-48 — `FormatBestDiff`
- main/screens/panel_texts.cpp:627-653 — `FormatZapAmountLocal`
- main/screens/nostr_zap.cpp:27-61 — `FormatZapAmount`

Concrete cases:
- num=999_500 → "1000K" instead of "1.0M"
- num=999_999_500 → "1000M" instead of "1.0B"
- bestDiff=999_950_000_000 → "1000G" instead of "1.0T"

NOT a v3 port — v3's commit 41b5fcf (which I initially suspected) was a different bug (shareDot+integer-price interaction) that v4 already handles via the `dot_pos != npos && dot_pos > 0` guards in panel_texts.cpp:334 and btc_price_suffix_layout.hpp:67-69, both pinned by PriceSuffixModeCompact1/2 parity tests in test_datahandler_parity.cpp.

This is a separate latent bug discovered during the v3 audit (May 2026). Surfaces in the field whenever a value sits in the 999.5x..999.9x band of any decade — uncommon but not vanishingly rare for market cap and bitaxe best-diff which can sit close to those boundaries for hours/days.

Fix shape (deferred): post-format check — if rendered string starts with "1000", bump suffix one rung up and re-render at the existing budget. Cleanest minimal change. Existing test_screen_math.cpp / test_panel_texts.cpp / test_bitaxe_panel_texts.cpp need new boundary cases for each affected decade transition (K→M, M→B, B→T, etc).

title: timerSeconds:0 PATCH does not persist
description:
Observed during the rotation-resume verification on Rev B (4d66391). PATCHing /api/settings with {"timerSeconds":0} returns 200 but the value reverts to 60 on the next GET /api/settings. Other timerSeconds values (e.g. 30) persist correctly.

  curl http://<IP>/api/settings | jq .timerSeconds                                                # returns 60

Pre-existing — not introduced by 4d66391.

title: Enable newlib nano printf on Rev A; verify suffix screens
description:
**Goal:** Drop `CONFIG_LIBC_NEWLIB_NANO_FORMATTING_ENABLE=y` (or its v6 equivalent) into sdkconfig.defaults.rev_a to swap full printf for nano printf. Saves an estimated 30–50 KiB of `stdio_vfs.c.obj` rodata.

**Known risk:** previous manual experiment broke the suffix screens (panel_texts.cpp / screen_math.cpp). Suspected cause: nano printf's reduced `%f`/`%g` precision handling around the K/M/B suffix branches.

**Test plan:**
1. Add the Kconfig knob to sdkconfig.defaults.rev_a only (Rev B/V8 keep full printf).
2. Build Rev A; record before/after binary size.
3. Flash + boot.
4. Drive every suffix path:
   - btc_price.cpp around the >7-digit threshold (price ≥ \$10M sats variant)
   - moscow_time.cpp around 7-digit sats (price < \$100)
   - bitcoin_supply.cpp / market_cap.cpp K/M/B/T suffixes
   - fee_rate_layout.hpp `%.2f` formatting
   - panel_texts.cpp `%.0f` / `%.1f` paths (mining pool hashrate, halving, supply)
   - nostr_zap.cpp `%.1f%s` for sats with k/M/B suffix
5. Compare against Rev B output (full printf) for each path — they MUST agree visually.
6. If divergence: file follow-up to refactor the offending site to use integer arithmetic instead of `%f`.

**Sequence:** do this AFTER the floating_to_chars investigation. If that yields 122 KiB, this becomes optional.
close_reason: Not applicable in IDF v6.0. The CONFIG_LIBC_NEWLIB_NANO_FORMAT knob is gated behind LIBC_NEWLIB=y, but IDF v6.0 switched the default libc to picolibc (LIBC_PICOLIBC=y; LIBC_NEWLIB is off). Setting the knob is silently ignored — verified by toggling it on Rev A: binary size identical (0x184570 both before and after). Picolibc has no equivalent nano-printf knob in v6.0; its printf is already designed for size. Additionally, audit found 18+ %lld/%llu format strings on the render path (fee_rate_layout, panel_texts, nostr_zap, screen_math) — these would need pre-refactoring before any future nano-printf-style swap, since nano printf doesn't support 64-bit integer formats. title: Enable ccache for IDF firmware builds in CI
description:
The release.yaml firmware matrix builds 4 variants (rev-a, rev-a-29, rev-b, v8). The existing cache covers `managed_components/` + per-variant `build-*` dirs, so warm cache hits are fast. **Cache misses (sdkconfig change, dependencies.lock bump, branch divergence) trigger a full rebuild of every IDF component per variant** — typically 8–10 minutes each, ~35 min total for the matrix.

## What ccache fixes

ccache hashes preprocessed compiler input + flags and stores `.o` outputs in a content-addressed cache. When the build cache is invalidated but the actual source bytes haven't changed (e.g. sdkconfig touched but only one #define affected), ccache still hits and the rebuild collapses to a link + a handful of recompiles instead of "compile every component from scratch".

ESP-IDF supports ccache out of the box via `IDF_CCACHE_ENABLE=1`.

## Implementation

1. **release.yaml: install ccache in the firmware matrix job.** The `espressif/idf:v6.0` image doesn't include it by default. Add to the variant build step (or a new dedicated step before it):
   ```bash
   apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends ccache
   ```

2. **Cache the ccache directory** via `actions/cache@v5`. Key on the IDF major + variant; restore-keys fallback to any prior cache for the same variant:
   ```yaml
   - uses: actions/cache@v5
     with:
       path: ~/.ccache
       key: ccache-idf-v6.0-${{ matrix.variant_label }}-${{ github.sha }}
       restore-keys: |
         ccache-idf-v6.0-${{ matrix.variant_label }}-
         ccache-idf-v6.0-
   ```
   The SHA-keyed primary write means each commit gets a fresh save; the prefix-keyed restore lets cache miss fall back to the most recent variant cache.

3. **Set `IDF_CCACHE_ENABLE=1`** in the build step's env, and bound the cache size with `ccache -M 2G` before invoking `idf.py build` so it doesn't grow unbounded across runs.

4. **Telemetry:** call `ccache -s` (statistics) after the build so the CI log shows hit/miss rates. Helps justify the change and spot misconfigs.

## Same treatment for host_tests.yaml?

Probably not — host tests build in <1 min already and the gain is marginal. Only add if profiling shows it helps. Skip in this issue.

## Verification

- First run: full build, ccache logs report 0% hit rate (expected — empty cache).
- Second run (no source change): ccache hits ~95%+, total firmware-job wall time drops from ~10min → ~3min per variant.
- Third run (touch one .cpp): partial hit, only the touched file recompiles.

Compare wall-times in the Forgejo CI logs and report in a comment on the PR.

## Out of scope

- distcc, sccache, BuildBuddy or other distributed-build setups. ccache is the simplest layer that delivers most of the win.
- Persistent shared cache across PRs / branches via S3 backend. The per-key cache restore is enough.
- Local-dev ccache integration. `IDF_CCACHE_ENABLE=1` works with brew's ccache too — document in README under Build section if useful, but not required for this issue.

## Notes for the agent

- Verify ccache works with the Xtensa toolchain — it does today, but historic compiler-detection bugs have hit this combo. `ccache -s` after the build should show non-zero `cache hit (preprocessed)` on the second run.
- Don't enable ccache for the WebUI / pnpm job; it's irrelevant.
- Container caches: the `~/.ccache` path is the runner user's home, NOT the container's `/root/.ccache`. Test that `actions/cache` writes/restores to the right path under the espressif/idf image — set `CCACHE_DIR=$HOME/.ccache` explicitly to be safe.
close_reason: Enabled ccache in .forgejo/workflows/release.yaml firmware matrix job: apt install ccache, separate actions/cache@v5 keyed on idf-v6.0 + variant_label + sha (with prefix-keyed restore fallback), IDF_CCACHE_ENABLE=1 + CCACHE_DIR=/root/.ccache in build step env, ccache -M 2G before build, ccache -s after. Commit ce8a5f6.

title: Enable firmware-side clang-tidy with curated ESP-IDF suppressions
description:
The current `.clang-tidy` setup runs against host-test sources only (`tools/lint/tidy.sh`, scoped to `test_host/*.cpp`). Firmware TUs under `components/` and `main/` are not gated because the IDF / mbedTLS / lwIP / FreeRTOS headers light up dozens of unactionable warnings (C-style macros, void* handles, ISR linkage, varargs, etc.).

## Plan

1. **Borrow Espressif's curated rule set** as a baseline. ESP-IDF ships its own `.clang-tidy` at https://github.com/espressif/esp-idf/blob/master/.clang-tidy used by `idf.py clang-check`. It enables `bugprone-*` + selected `clang-analyzer-*`, drops most `modernize-*` and all `cppcoreguidelines-*`. Vendor that into a second config file (e.g. `.clang-tidy-firmware`) so the host-test rules can stay tighter.

2. **HeaderFilterRegex scoping** must exclude `managed_components/`, `$IDF_PATH/components/`, and any `vendor/` paths so warnings on transitively-included IDF headers don't reach the report. Suppress at parse time, not at filter time, otherwise tidy still spends compute analyzing them.

3. **Per-build invocation** — clang-tidy needs `compile_commands.json` from one of the `build-*/` dirs. Pick Rev B as the canonical variant (matches the dev hardware) and run via `tools/lint/tidy_firmware.sh -p build-rev-b components/**/*.cpp main/**/*.cpp` or similar.

4. **Triage the first-wave warnings.** Expect 100–300 hits. Categories likely to appear (per ESP-IDF community experience):
   - `bugprone-easily-swappable-parameters` on legacy `init(int, int, int, int)` — disable.
   - `bugprone-exception-escape` on `extern "C"` ISR / task entrypoints — NOLINT inline.
   - `bugprone-narrowing-conversions` on hardware-register writes — NOLINT or cast.
   - `cert-err58-cpp` on static `unique_ptr` task handles — disable.
   - `clang-analyzer-cplusplus.NewDelete` false positives across IDF malloc family — verify before NOLINT.
   - Real findings (worth fixing): missing `nullptr` checks after `pvPortMalloc`, narrowing on `xQueueSend` length args, signed/unsigned mismatches in screen-coord math.

5. **CI integration.** Add a third job to `.forgejo/workflows/lint.yaml` that:
   - Uses the `espressif/idf:v6.0` Docker image (already used by `release.yaml`).
   - Configures one variant build with `idf.py reconfigure` (no full build needed — just `compile_commands.json`).
   - Runs `clang-tidy -p build-rev-b` over the project sources.
   - Starts in advisory mode (`WarningsAsErrors: ''` for the firmware config) until the warning set is at zero, then promote.

## Out of scope

- pyclang integration (https://github.com/espressif/pyclang). It's the wrapper Espressif use internally; worth evaluating only if direct clang-tidy invocation proves clumsy.
- Re-running tidy across all three variants (Rev A / Rev B / V8). Sources are 95%+ shared; one variant catches everything except a few `#ifdef BTCLOCK_BOARD == ...` blocks.

## Estimate

Half a day if the ESP-IDF baseline transfers cleanly. Up to a full day if we hit a wave of false positives that need NOLINT-with-comment per site.

## Related

- Closes the firmware-side gap left by `btclock_v4-lf9` (host-test tidy, already gating).
- Reference: ESP-IDF `.clang-tidy` and pyclang both linked above.

title: Triage clang-tidy advisory warnings to enable strict CI gating
description:
The new clang-tidy CI job (`.forgejo/workflows/lint.yaml::tidy`) runs in advisory mode (`WarningsAsErrors: ''` in `.clang-tidy`) — warnings are reported but don't fail the build. As of the initial setup commit there are 51 warnings across the host-test surface, broken down by check:

- 21 × `bugprone-argument-comment` — `/* name= */` comments drift from parameter names; mostly stale renames in test code.
- 14 × `bugprone-unchecked-optional-access` — test code dereferences `*opt` without checking; arguably acceptable in tests where a missing optional should fail loudly, but worth annotating.
- 5 × `bugprone-implicit-widening-of-multiplication-result` — int * int promoted to size_t.
- 4 × `modernize-use-emplace`.
- 2 × `bugprone-switch-missing-default-case`.
- 2 × `bugprone-incorrect-roundings`.
- 1 × `bugprone-float-loop-counter` — intentional in `components/fonts/include/fit_text_px.hpp` (binary-search-like font fit); should be NOLINTed.
- 1 × `bugprone-branch-clone`, 1 × `performance-enum-size`, 1 × `bugprone-macro-parentheses`.

Plan:
1. Triage each check: fix or NOLINT with a justifying comment.
2. Once a check has zero violations, promote it to an error in `.clang-tidy` `WarningsAsErrors`.
3. Eventually flip the whole tidy job to gating in CI.

title: Pool logo fetcher: retry-with-backoff
description:
The on-demand pool logo fetcher (`components/pool_logo_fetcher/`) is single-shot per pool selection. If the fetch races wifi association at boot — observed on Rev B hardware in this session — `esp_http_client_perform` fails, no .bin lands on LittleFS, and the slot is released without leaving any retry primitive in place. The next `MakeActivePoolSource` call (boot or pool-name PATCH) is the only retry trigger.

## Symptom

Fresh boot of a NVS-wiped device: `fsUsedBytes` stays at the pre-fetch baseline. Triggering a `POST /api/action/clear_pool_logos` (which now re-enqueues — bd `btclock_v4-5yi` follow-up landed in this session) succeeds because wifi is up by then. So the failure mode is timing, not API.

## Suggested fix

Inside `pool_logo_fetcher::FetchTaskTrampoline`, on a `DoFetch` failure that returns `ESP_ERR_*` from `esp_http_client_perform` or any TLS-error path, sleep for an exponential backoff (start at e.g. 5s, cap at 60s) and retry up to N=3 times before releasing the slot. The retry budget should NOT include 4xx/5xx responses (those are server-side, not transient).

## Out of scope

- A heavier event-driven approach ("retry when STA event WIFI_EVENT_STA_GOT_IP arrives") would be cleaner but invasive — the fetcher would need to subscribe to esp_event topics. Mention as an alternative in the PR.

## Related

- bd `btclock_v4-5yi` (parent: on-demand fetcher).
- Filed during the schema-default consolidation work on 2026-04-26.
close_reason: Implemented exponential backoff (5s/10s/20s, max 3 attempts) for transient fetch failures in commit 8838b47. Permanent failures (HTTP 4xx/5xx, response-shape mismatches) skip retry. Verified on Rev B hardware: clean build, flashed, retry path is wired and emits at WARN level — no transient failures occurred during the verification run since wifi was already up.

title: Add Foundry USA Pool support
description:
Adds the #1 BTC pool by hashrate to the catalogue. Header API key, account-scoped, returns hashrate AND earnings.

## API surface

- Base: `api.foundryusapool.com`
- Endpoint pattern: `GET /subaccount_hashrate_day/{name}?coin=BTC&startDateUnixMs=...`
- Auth: `X-API-KEY: <key>` header
- Returns: per-subaccount daily hashrate series + separate earnings/payouts endpoint
- TLS required
- Foundry membership is institutional — not all users will have credentials. Lower addressable user count than ViaBTC, but the brand recognition is the win.

## Scope

1. New component `components/mining_pool_foundry/`.
2. New settings fields: API key (string, secret-suppressed) and subaccount name.
3. Combine the hashrate endpoint with the earnings endpoint so `PoolStats` carries both fields populated. Decide whether to make two HTTP calls per poll cycle or interleave them across two cycles.
4. Register in `AvailablePoolNames()`. Add logo metadata for the runtime fetcher.

## Reference

- Docs: https://api.foundryusapool.com/ and https://pool-faq.foundrydigital.com/api

## Related

- bd `btclock_v4-5yi` — runtime logo fetcher.
- Shares `X-API-KEY + GET` pattern with ViaBTC. Worth a small `keyed_get_pool_base` mix-in.

title: Add ViaBTC support
description:
Adds a top-5 commercial BTC pool to the catalogue. Cleanest auth model among the majors: single-header API key, plain GET, no signing, returns hashrate plus active+inactive worker counts.

## API surface

- Endpoint: `GET /res/openapi/v1/hashrate?coin=BTC`
- Auth: `X-API-KEY: <key>` header (no signing, no timestamp)
- Returns: 10-min, 1-hour, 24-hour hashrate per account, raw H/s as string. Worker counts.
- TLS required.
- No documented public rate limit; conservative 60 s polling fits BTClock's existing `poolPollSec`.

## Scope

1. New component `components/mining_pool_viabtc/`.
2. New settings field for the API key (string, secret-suppressed in GET like `httpAuthPass`).
3. Hashrate value comes back as raw H/s — feed through the existing `mining_pool_common::hashrate.hpp` formatter to render "X.YY P".
4. Register in `AvailablePoolNames()`. Add logo metadata for the runtime fetcher.

## Reference

- Docs: https://github.com/viabtc/viapool_api/wiki
- Hashrate endpoint: https://github.com/viabtc/viapool_api/wiki/acquire_account_hashrate

## Related

- bd `btclock_v4-5yi` — runtime logo fetcher.
- Pattern shared with bd `btclock_v4-foundry` (Foundry USA): both use `X-API-KEY` header + GET. Worth a small `keyed_get_pool_base` mix-in.

title: Add NerdMiner Pool support (pool.nerdminers.org / pool.nerdminer.io)
description:
Lowest-cost addition to the mining-pool catalogue. Same JSON shape as the existing ckpool family; the existing `ckpool_family_parser` should handle it unchanged.

## Why

Strongest fit for the BTClock target audience (Bitaxe / NerdMiner solo-mining hobbyists). No auth — BTC address goes in the URL path. TLS. Same `hashrate1m / 5m / 1hr / 1d` JSON fields as ckpool.

- Pool home: https://nerdminer.io/

- Filed from a survey of public mining-pool APIs done 2026-04-26.

title: On-demand mining pool logo fetcher
description:
Restore the v3 pattern of fetching pool logos at runtime instead of vendoring all logos in flash.

## Background

v4 currently bakes ALL mining-pool logos into firmware as 1-bpp bitmaps in `main/screens/assets/pool_logos.cpp` (~45 KB of permanent .text). Generated offline by `tools/pool_logos/convert.py` from https://git.btclock.dev/btclock/mining-pool-logos.

v3 instead downloaded logos on demand from the same repo, keyed off a per-pool `hasLogo()` getter, and cached them in LittleFS. This saved flash and let users add new pool logos without a firmware reflash.

## Why now

The original justification given in `main/screens/assets/pool_logos.hpp:11` ("removes runtime dependency on an HTTPS logos-server") was incorrect — v4 already has hard runtime HTTPS dependencies for OTA (`esp_https_ota`), mining-pool stats (Braiins, Noderunners, Satoshi Radio, Ocean), and TLS WebSockets (`wss://ws.btclock.dev`, `wss://relay.primal.net`). Adding logo fetching does not expand the TLS attack surface.

The valid reasons for baking logos in flash are: (a) host-test + wasm-preview builds run without network/LittleFS, (b) survives NVS wipe with no re-provisioning, (c) simpler boot path. A future fetcher should preserve (a) and (b) by keeping a fallback to vendored bitmaps when no logo is cached.

## Scope

1. Add a `hasLogo()` (or `logo_filename()`) virtual on `PoolBase` (`components/mining_pool_common/include/mining_pool_common/pool_base.hpp`); subclasses opt in.
2. On pool selection, if no LittleFS cache hit for that pool's logo file, fetch from `poolLogosUrl + "/<pool>.bin"` and store under `/lfs/pool_logos/`.
3. Renderer: prefer LittleFS cache → vendored bitmap → text fallback.
4. After cutover, audit which vendored bitmaps in `main/screens/assets/pool_logos.cpp` can be dropped to reclaim flash. Keep a minimal set so first-boot before WiFi shows logos.
5. Honor existing `prefs::kPoolLogosUrl` setting (already in the schema, default `https://git.btclock.dev/btclock/mining-pool-logos/raw/branch/main`).

## v3 reference

Per-pool class hierarchy implementing `hasLogo()` and `getLogo()`. Look in `btclock_v3_fci/src/lib/screens/mining_pool/` for the pattern.

## Related

- bd `btclock_v4-7da` (umbrella: dead schema keys) — `poolLogosUrl` was briefly deleted then restored when this issue was filed.
- `main/screens/assets/pool_logos.hpp` — comment needs updating once this lands.
close_reason: Implemented in commit f9048e9: HTTPS fetcher + LittleFS cache + PSRAM resolver + hasLogo plumbing on PoolBase + 4 pool overrides; vendored bitmap audit dropped all four (ocean/braiins/noderunners/gobrrr); kLogoMetaTable retains metadata; new POST /api/action/clear_pool_logos endpoint; defaults flipped to noderunners with poolGlobalStats=true. Net flash delta vs pre-5yi baseline: +1,073 B. Verified on Rev B: device boots, currentScreen rotation up, free heap 120,603 B (improved over baseline). Follow-up issues filed: btclock_v4-ub6 (NerdMiner Pool), btclock_v4-8i2 (ViaBTC), btclock_v4-htp (Foundry USA Pool).

title: Rev A app partition overflows by ~6.5KB on ESP-IDF v6
description:
On ESP-IDF v6.0, the Rev A firmware binary is 1,775,968 bytes vs the 0x1B0000 (1,769,472 byte) app slot — overflows by 0x1960 bytes (6,496 bytes / ~6.3 KB).

For comparison: Rev A binary on v5.5.4 = 1,671,264 bytes; v6 adds ~104 KB (+6.3 %), likely from PSA Crypto / mbedTLS v4 default + PicolibC switch + esp_driver_* split layer.

Rev B (8MB, 0x1B0000 slot, 51 % free) and V8 (16MB, ~1.7 MB slot) both fit comfortably.

Options before adopting v6 on Rev A:
1. Tune sdkconfig — disable PSA crypto / unneeded mbedTLS suites / log levels.
2. Repartition: shrink storage (LittleFS) by 0x20000 to give app0/app1 +0x10000 each. Note: forces re-flash of every existing Rev A device.
3. Drop Rev A from the v6 release matrix (stay on v5.5 for the 4MB SKU).

See branch feat/idf-v6-upgrade for the rest of the upgrade work that does build cleanly.
close_reason: Resolved on main via 16d52a8 (sdkconfig trim) + d9d4d11 (Merriweather drop). Rev A now lands at 1,647,920 B / 0x1B0000 slot — 6.87 % free.

title: Implement mempool.space + kraken WSS data source for price/blocks
description:
## Background
v3 firmware supported a "BTCLOCK_SOURCE = mempool.space + kraken" data source that maintained two independent WebSocket clients:
- **kraken WSS** for live BTC price ticks
- **mempool.space WSS** for new block notifications + fee data

v4 currently ships only the consolidated BTClock WSS V2 source (`wss://ws.btclock.dev/api/v2/ws`) which carries both price and blocks over a single connection.

The legacy `connectionStatus.price` and `connectionStatus.blocks` fields in `/api/status` were intended to reflect those *separate* upstream WSS connections — they only make sense when the mempool.space+kraken source is selected.

## Current bug
`components/webserver/control_server.cpp:645-648` reports:
```cpp
const bool v2_up = cfg_.hub != nullptr;
cJSON_AddBoolToObject(conn, "price", v2_up);
cJSON_AddBoolToObject(conn, "blocks", v2_up);
cJSON_AddBoolToObject(conn, "V2", v2_up);
```

`cfg_.hub != nullptr` is just "the V2 data-source object was allocated at boot" — it never reflects the actual V2 WSS connection state, and it has nothing to do with whether mempool.space or kraken are reachable. So:
- When V2 is the selected source: `price` and `blocks` should be `false` (these fields semantically belong to the mempool.space+kraken source which isn't running). `V2` is the field WebUI should consult.
- When mempool.space+kraken source is selected: `price` should reflect kraken WSS connected state, `blocks` should reflect mempool.space WSS connected state, `V2` should be `false`.

`V2` field tracking is also broken (same `cfg_.hub != nullptr` check) but that's a smaller fix — see related comment.

## Plan
1. **Quick interim fix** (can land before the full source is implemented):
   - `price = false` and `blocks = false` unconditionally until the mempool.space+kraken source exists.
   - `V2` should track the actual V2 WSS connection (mirror the nostr pattern: `BtclockDataSource::IsConnected()` from a `std::atomic<bool>` toggled by `WEBSOCKET_EVENT_CONNECTED`/`_DISCONNECTED` events in `components/btclock_data/btclock_data.cpp:67-76`, plumbed through a `cfg_.v2_connected` callback in `ControlServer::Config`).

2. **Full implementation**:
   - Add a new data source component (e.g. `components/mempool_kraken_data/`) with two `esp_websocket_client_t` instances.
   - Kraken WSS: `wss://ws.kraken.com` — subscribe to `XBT/USD` or per-currency pair based on `actCurrencies` setting.
   - mempool.space WSS: `wss://mempool.space/api/v1/ws` — subscribe to blocks + fee data.
   - Hook into the existing `DataHub` / `LiveStatus` plumbing so the renderer doesn't care which source is active.
   - Add a settings field (e.g. `dataSource = "btclock_v2" | "mempool_kraken"`) gated by an existing settings catalog entry. v3 had `BTCLOCK_SOURCE` env var; v4 should make it a runtime toggle.
   - Wire `connectionStatus.price` to kraken connected state, `.blocks` to mempool connected state, only when mempool_kraken is the active source.

## References
- v3 source for kraken WSS: see https://git.btclock.dev/btclock/btclock_v3 history under `src/lib/data/`.
- v3 source for mempool.space WSS: same repo.
- Existing v4 nostr WSS pattern (good template for connection state plumbing): `components/nostr/src/relay_client.cpp` + the `cfg_.nostr_connected` callback in `control_server.cpp:653-654`.
close_reason: Implemented MempoolKrakenSource: two independent WSS clients (mempool.space + Kraken V2 /v2) feeding the DataHub. Wired in main/sources/sources.cpp for dataSource=1. Builds clean for REV_B; 665 host tests pass.

title: feat: OTA upload UX — quiesce services + UPDATE panel + LED progress bar
description:
Nice-to-have polish for firmware OTA upload (POST /upload/firmware, fixed in 2aafc59). User request:

1. **Stop data services** before flash starts to free internal heap — BtclockDataSource WS, nostr RelayClient, pool poller, bitaxe poller. The OTA operation will reboot the device anyway, so graceful disconnect vs abort doesn't matter.
2. **Paint 'UPDATE!' on every panel** (or a lightning-bolt icon + 'UPDATE' split) before starting the write. Use full-refresh and lock the panels so the active renderer can't paint over it.
3. **LED progress bar**: map upload fraction to LED count across the 4-LED strip. <25% = 1 green, 25-50% = 2 greens, 50-75% = 3 greens, 75-100% = 4 greens. Completion blink (3x) before the esp_restart.

Location: components/ota/ota_manager.cpp's WritePushImage — hook progress into an OtaStatusListener callback that the webserver's HandleUploadFirmware installs. Call into ScreenManager + LedController via the existing adapter callbacks.

Tests: can exercise the progress-fraction math pure-logic. LED fractions + screen paint behaviour need a small host helper.

title: panel_texts supply-% mirror emits ' % ' but renderer paints '%'
description:
BuildBitcoinSupply (show_percent=true) sets out.back() = " % " (three chars). RenderBitcoinSupplyScreen in bitcoin_supply.cpp emits a single-char "%" via PaintSlot::kDigit on the final cell. The /api/status mirror and device disagree on the last cell — WebUI renders "% " (3 chars) while device shows a big "%" glyph. v3 did this too (parseBitcoinSupply emits " % ") so it's an inherited cosmetic drift; low-impact but visible.

The " % " 3-char cell was historically rendered as small_chars (same font as 3-digit groups) in v3; v4 changed it to a full-size digit glyph in the renderer but left the mirror at the v3 string. Either: (a) change mirror to "%", or (b) change renderer to paint " % " via kSmallGroup.

Repro: supply percent mode, 7-panel. data[6] == " % " but EPD shows big %.
close_reason: Implemented: mirror now emits single-char % matching renderer.

title: perf: follow-ups to TLS/PSRAM audit
description:
Leftover PSRAM / heap wins after 4b58bfb + fef399b (btclock_v4-740):

1. Consider CONFIG_MBEDTLS_DYNAMIC_FREE_CONFIG_DATA=y — frees key/DHM data after handshake. For a TLS client with no client cert, should be a no-op. Needs a quick verification with esp_crt_bundle that CA access post-handshake isn't needed.

2. Consider CONFIG_MBEDTLS_EXTERNAL_MEM_ALLOC=y (or MBEDTLS_DEFAULT_MEM_ALLOC) to route mbedtls internal allocations to PSRAM. Trade-off: slower handshake latency vs ~more DRAM freed. DEFAULT mode keeps tiered behavior with SPIRAM_MALLOC_ALWAYSINTERNAL=16384 so < 16 KiB stays internal; probably the right middle ground to try next.

3. Bitaxe source body is only 4 KiB and on internal heap — small enough to leave, but could also move to PSRAM for consistency with pool_base. Low priority.

4. OTA hashing uses a std::vector<uint8_t>(4096) on internal heap (components/ota/ota_manager.cpp:190). Only alive during OTA, so not steady-state pressure, but PSRAM would be a small easy win.

5. Webserver request body ReadFullBody (components/webserver/control_server.cpp:250) uses plain malloc. Request bodies can be up to few KiB for /api/show/* handlers. PSRAM candidate.

6. Measure actual runtime internal-heap delta on Rev B after flashing. Update FEATURE_MATRIX.md or similar if heap pressure analysis is tracked there.
close_reason: Implemented items 1-5: mbedtls dynamic-free + DEFAULT alloc + PSRAM moves for OTA hash buffer, bitaxe body, webserver ReadFullBody. Verified on Rev B at 630s uptime: espFreeHeap=107795, espFreePsram=1953304. Item 6 measurement done; steady-state heap delta within noise — PSRAM moves help burst windows, not steady state.

description: Nostr zap notification screen. When a zap comes in via nostr_zap_listener, briefly overlay a full-screen 'ZAP' notification (icon + amount + zapper msg) for ~30s, then auto-restore the previous rotation screen. Gated behind 'nostrZapNotify' + 'scrnRestoreZap' prefs. title: gmtOffset stored but never applied — hide or remove it
description:
gmtOffset appears in GET /api/settings and can be PATCHed (directly or via
tzOffset minutes→seconds), but nothing reads it back. SCREEN_TIME renders via
localtime_r() which only respects setenv("TZ", <posix>)/tzset(), and the
post-07862b1 fix now drives that from tzString alone.

Old firmware supposedly fed gmtOffset into sntp_set_time_sync / the clock
computation as a fixed offset, but that path never landed in the IDF port.
Offering it to the WebUI now is actively misleading: a user who PATCHes
gmtOffset expects their clock to move and nothing happens.

Options:
  (a) Drop gmtOffset + tzOffset from the schema; keep tzString only.
  (b) Wire tzOffset → additive offset in SCREEN_TIME after tzString.
      (Not recommended — the POSIX TZ string already carries the DST rules
      and adding a separate offset makes the two fields conflict.)
  (c) Keep gmtOffset but mark it read-only in the WebUI and stop accepting
      the PATCH.

My suggestion: (a) — old behaviour that nobody misses because the current
IDF firmware never used it.
close_reason: Verified complete (resolution a): gmtOffset + tzOffset dropped from /api/settings emit and PATCH (settings_api.cpp:355-361, schema.hpp:129-133). Only tzString is consumed (timezone.cpp + init_control_api.cpp:153 setenv/tzset). Host tests cover the regression at test_settings_api.cpp:1011-1079. kGmtOffset constant retained for migration only.

title: Many /api/settings fields stored in NVS but never read by firmware
description:
Audit during the settings bug cluster found a long list of schema fields whose
PATCH writes land in NVS but nothing on the device reads them back. They all
appear in GET /api/settings because BuildGetResponse walks the schema — so the
WebUI can show and change them — but changing them is a no-op until the
downstream subsystem is ported.

Confirmed unread on main@07862b1:
  - bitaxeEnabled, bitaxeHostname        (no Bitaxe data source yet)
  - miningPoolUser, poolGlobalStats,
    poolLogosUrl, localPoolHost          (pool subsystem only reads
                                          miningPoolStats + miningPoolName)
  - mempoolInstance, mempoolSecure,
    dataSource, ceEndpoint, ceDisableSSL (legacy data-source toggles; IDF only
                                          runs btclock WS v2)
  - blockFeeDec, mcapBigChar,
    supplyPercent, useBlkCountdown,
    useMscwTime, useSatsSymbol,
    suffixPrice, suffixShareDot,
    verticalDesc, mowMode                (renderer layout flags — most screens
                                          ignore them)
  - blockFlashColor                      (LED subsystem uses a different path)
  - flEffectDelay, flFlashOnUpd,
    flFlashOnZap, flMaxBrightness,
    flOffWhenDark, flAlwaysOn,
    flDisable, luxLightToggle            (frontlight controller reads its own
                                          "frontlight" NVS namespace)
  - refrScrnChange, scrnRestoreZap,
    stealFocus, inverseButtons           (screen-manager behaviour flags)
  - fullRefreshMin                       (no periodic full-refresh yet — see
                                          btclock_v3_fci-6fi)
  - enableDebugLog                       (log level hardcoded)
  - gitReleaseUrl                        (OTA manager reads it at boot, not
                                          runtime)
  - inverseButtons, ledTestOnPower,
    ledFlashOnUpd                        (button/LED wiring ignores these)

Each one needs a small audit to decide:
  (a) Wire the downstream subsystem, or
  (b) Remove from the schema so GET doesn't lie, or
  (c) Document as "reboot required / not yet applied" in the field's
     boot_only flag + a WebUI tooltip.

Not blocking today's live bugs — these are all "PATCH is accepted but doesn't
do anything," which is the same behaviour the old firmware had for some of
these fields during the Arduino-era port.

title: IDF: timezone support (IANA name -> POSIX TZ string + setenv)
description:
## Problem
The IDF C++ PoC currently renders the clock screen in UTC. ESP-IDF v5.5's newlib supports POSIX TZ strings via setenv("TZ",...)/tzset() but ships no zoneinfo database, so we need our own IANA->POSIX mapping.

## Old firmware baseline
- `include/timezone_data.hpp` (742 lines, committed — the generator script lives outside this repo) encodes 484 IANA zone IDs mapping to 93 unique POSIX TZ strings via a compact `uint8_t`-backed enum.
- `src/lib/system/config.cpp` calls `setenv("TZ", ...); tzset()` after SNTP sync, reading the IANA name from NVS key `tzString` (namespace `btclock`, default `Europe/Amsterdam`).
- WebUI settings page carries the dropdown; values are plain IANA IDs posted to `/api/settings` and stored verbatim in NVS.

## ESP-IDF v5.5 options surveyed
- newlib: POSIX TZ strings only, no zoneinfo. No `CONFIG_NEWLIB_*TZ*` Kconfigs exist.
- components.espressif.com: two matches —
  - `qb4-dev/tzdata` — same approach (POSIX-string table, ~15 KB) but GPL-2.0; cannot bundle into this Apache-ish tree.
  - `espressif/brookesia_service_sntp` — framework-coupled, not useful standalone.
- Full IANA tzdata (~200 KB binary) is available as third-party components but is an order of magnitude larger than the compact approach and offers no user-visible advantage over POSIX strings for a clock that only needs wall time + DST transitions.

## Design choice
Port the old firmware's compact table unchanged. Baked-size after -Os is ~17 KiB of app image — well under the 50 KiB budget and one-tenth the cost of full tzdata. Ported via a new Python generator at `idf_cpp_proto/tools/timezone/generate_tz_table.py` that reads `include/timezone_data.hpp` and emits a flat `constexpr std::array<std::pair<std::string_view, std::string_view>, 484>` into `components/timezone/include/timezone/tz_table_generated.hpp` (committed so IDF build has no Python step).

## Implementation plan
- New component `components/timezone/` with:
  - `tz_table_generated.hpp` (484 entries, auto-generated)
  - `timezone.hpp` — constexpr `PosixForIana()` (pure lookup, host-test-friendly) + `SetTimezoneByName(const char*)` + `GetTimezoneName()` + `InitFromNvs()`
  - `timezone.cpp` — setenv/tzset + NVS persistence (namespace "time", key "tz")
- `main.cpp`: call `InitFromNvs()` right after `Prefs::InitOnce()`, before SNTP. Clock screen already uses `localtime_r` so renders local time once TZ is set.
- Host test `test_timezone.cpp` covering 5 well-known zones + unknown-zone fallback + full-table invariants (non-empty, sorted by name).

## Out of scope for this issue
- Settings-schema UI / webserver `/api/settings` write-back — tracked under epic `jwz`.
- WebUI dropdown / locale code — lives in `data/` submodule.
- Per-zone DST alerts / notifications — independent future work.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] IANA->POSIX lookup table baked into app image (~484 zones, <=50 KiB delta)
- [ ] Python generator committed under tools/timezone/, regeneration is idempotent
- [ ] SetTimezoneByName() wired to setenv+tzset+NVS; rejects unknown names with ESP_ERR_NOT_FOUND
- [ ] GetTimezoneName() reads NVS with UTC fallback
- [ ] Boot path (main.cpp) calls InitFromNvs() before SNTP, logs chosen zone
- [ ] Clock screen renders local time (verified via localtime_r pathway)
- [ ] Host tests pass for the 5 canonical zones (UTC, Europe/Amsterdam, America/New_York, Asia/Tokyo, Pacific/Auckland) plus unknown-zone empty-view check
- [ ] idf.py REV_B build succeeds; binary delta documented
- [ ] NVS schema documented: namespace 'time', key 'tz' (string)
- [ ] Settings-schema UI write-back deferred with pointer to jwz epic
