title: Emscripten/WASM parity: data parser as JS + HTML pixel preview
description:
Mirror btclock-ws-nostr-publish's `emscripten.sh` for the ESP-IDF tree so the WebUI (or any JS/TS consumer) can call the same parsing logic the firmware uses — single source of truth for frame decoding. Stretch goal: pixel-for-pixel HTML preview of the EPD render by also exposing the screen renderers to WASM and drawing into a canvas.

## Context

`~/src/btclock-ws-nostr-publish/emscripten.sh` compiles `src/lib/btclock/data_handler.cpp` + `utils.cpp` (Arduino tree) with `em++ -lembind --no-entry` into `btclock_datahandler.{js,wasm}` and ships a type-check script (`scripts/check_wasm_types.mjs`) that diffs `EMSCRIPTEN_BINDINGS` against a TS interface to catch signature drift. Goal is parity in the IDF tree.

## Phase 1 — parser to WASM

The current parser lives in `components/btclock_data/btclock_data.cpp` (WS v2 MessagePack) and `components/data_core/hub.cpp` (DataSnapshot merge). Neither compiles on emscripten because of ESP-IDF headers (`esp_websocket_client`, `esp_log`, `esp_crt_bundle`, etc.). Work needed:

- **Split btclock_data into transport + protocol.** A new `btclock_data/protocol.{hpp,cpp}` carries the pure MessagePack → `DataSnapshot` function (depends only on ArduinoJson + `data_core/snapshot.hpp`, both portable). The existing `btclock_data.cpp` shrinks to the ESP-IDF transport glue and calls `ParseFrame(bytes, len) → DataSnapshot`.
- **Add an `emscripten/` build target.** Under `idf_cpp_proto/emscripten/` put:
  - `bindings.cpp` — `EMSCRIPTEN_BINDINGS` block exposing `ParseFrame` and `DataSnapshot::Merge`/`PriceOf`.
  - `CMakeLists.txt` or a shell script wrapping `em++` (match the upstream style — standalone script is simplest for a side-tooling directory).
  - A `check_wasm_types.mjs` port or reuse; keeps TS bindings pinned to the C++ signatures.
- **Output**: `idf_cpp_proto/emscripten/out/btclock_protocol.{js,wasm}` + `.d.ts`. Intent is for the WebUI repo to consume via a git-submodule or published artifact — design is TBD, track separately.

## Phase 2 — HTML pixel preview (stretch)

Expose the screen renderers (`RenderBlockHeightScreen`, `RenderMoscowTimeScreen`, `RenderBtcPriceScreen`) + font rasteriser (`font.cpp` uses stb_truetype which already compiles on emscripten). Render into a pixel buffer that JS maps onto a `<canvas>` using the same SSD1680-style 1-bpp dithering the panels show. Shows exactly what the physical EPD would show for a given DataSnapshot without flashing a device.

Constraints:
- `EpdPanel` writes into a framebuffer via `DrawFramebufferStart` + `WaitForRefresh`; for WASM we skip the SPI/busy-pin path and just expose the framebuffer bytes.
- The `fb_storage[N][16*296]` layout + rotation mapping (`SetPixelLandscape`) are pure memory operations — portable.
- Need a small `wasm_panel.hpp` shim that mimics enough of `EpdPanel` for the renderers to write, returning the buffer to JS.

Either phase 2 or a thin shim layer over it is valuable for font/padding debugging — the iteration loop for things like the sats-glyph centering would be seconds rather than flash-and-photograph.

## Effort

- Phase 1: M (1-2 days) — mostly mechanical split + CMake/embind wiring.
- Phase 2: M-L (2-4 days) — need to shim EpdPanel for WASM and stub the framebuffer interface cleanly.

## Prereqs

- Emscripten ≥ 3.1.0 (same minimum the WS-nostr-publish repo uses).
- Node (for the type-check script).

## Related

- `~/src/btclock-ws-nostr-publish/emscripten.sh` — upstream build script.
- `~/src/btclock-ws-nostr-publish/scripts/check_wasm_types.mjs` — TS drift checker; likely portable as-is.

title: IDF Phase 0: C++ PoC — drive EPDs, NeoPixels, frontlight on v5.5
description:
First proof-of-concept for the pure ESP-IDF v5.5 C++ rewrite. Pre-scaffolding spike: prove that the display, LED, and frontlight paths work end-to-end in C++ on real hardware before we invest in CI and full library ports.

## Deliverable
A single-binary ESP-IDF v5.5 project, built with idf.py, that on btclock_rev_b hardware:
1. Renders a static bitmap to all 7 e-paper panels.
2. Animates the 4 WS2812B NeoPixels through an RGB cycle.
3. Fades the PCA9685 frontlight from 0% to 100% and back, gated by the BH1750 lux reading.
All running in idiomatic C++ (classes, RAII, std::array, std::mutex), not C.

## Why this PoC
These three subsystems together exercise everything that would force us to rethink the rewrite: shared I2C bus contention (MCP + PCA + BH), multiple SPI devices sharing one bus with per-panel CS gating (EPD), RMT-based signal generation (WS2812), and the Pin-abstraction-over-MCP pattern that the universal_pin library in the current firmware provides. If this PoC works clean, the remaining phases are mostly porting. If the per-panel esp_lcd custom driver path doesn't work for SSD1680, we learn that cheap.

## C++ stack choices (confirmed via context7 on docs.espressif.com)
- app_main defined as extern "C" void app_main() in a .cpp file.
- std::thread, std::mutex, std::condition_variable work (backed by pthread → FreeRTOS tasks). CONFIG_PTHREAD_* knobs for stack size and priority.
- Exceptions + RTTI are supported but off by default (cost binary size). Keep them OFF for PoC; use absl::StatusOr-style Result<T,Error> or ESP_ERROR_CHECK.
- std::filesystem available.
- esp-idf-cxx managed component (espressif/esp-idf-cxx) provides official C++ wrappers for NVS (nvs::NVSHandle), I2C, SPI, GPIO, esp_timer. Use it for NVS; consider for I2C/SPI in Phase 1+ where it's a good fit.

## Native ESP-IDF components we leverage (no libraries written for these)
- driver/i2c_master.h: new v5.5 API with i2c_master_bus_handle_t + per-device i2c_master_dev_handle_t. Built for multiple devices on one bus — perfect for MCP + PCA + BH.
- driver/spi_master.h: spi_bus_config_t + spi_device_interface_config_t with cs_ena_pretrans/posttrans for hardware CS, or manual CS via the spics_io_num=-1 path for MCP-routed CS.
- esp_lcd component: has a generic panel-io + panel-driver framework (used for SSD1306, ST7789, etc.). The framework is ideal for SSD1680 — we write a custom panel driver (esp_lcd_new_panel_ssd1680) that plugs into the same framework. Much less work than raw SPI.
- espressif/led_strip managed component: RMT-based WS2812B driver, drop-in.
- esp-psram built-in: frame buffers in PSRAM via heap_caps_malloc(..., MALLOC_CAP_SPIRAM).

## Libraries we write in this PoC
All as ESP-IDF components under components/. Public headers are C++ classes; internal .cpp uses the C APIs above.

1. components/pin_bus (shared abstraction)
   - Pin abstract base class (digital_write, digital_read, set_mode).
   - NativePin subclass wrapping gpio_set_level / gpio_get_level.
   - Mcp23017Pin subclass holding a ref to a Mcp23017 + pin index.
   - Replaces dsbaars/universal_pin.
   - Header-only or tiny .cpp.

2. components/mcp23017
   - class Mcp23017 { Mcp23017(i2c_master_bus_handle_t, uint8_t addr); ... };
   - RAII-owns its i2c_master_dev_handle_t.
   - Port only the register ops we use: IODIR, GPPU, IPOL, GPINTEN, INTCAP, GPIO read/write, interrupt flag read.
   - Makes Mcp23017::pin(n) -> Mcp23017Pin factory.

3. components/pca9685
   - class Pca9685 { Pca9685(i2c_master_bus_handle_t, uint8_t addr); ... };
   - set_frequency(hz), set_channel(ch, uint16_t duty_0_4095), set_all_off().
   - RAII ownership; destructor drives all channels low.

4. components/bh1750
   - class Bh1750 { Bh1750(i2c_master_bus_handle_t, uint8_t addr); ... };
   - set_mode(ContinuousHighRes / OneShotHighRes), read_lux() -> float.

5. components/epd_ssd1680
   - Custom esp_lcd panel driver registered via esp_lcd_new_panel_ssd1680(io_handle, &cfg, &panel_handle).
   - class EpdPanel wrapping the esp_lcd handle + a 1bpp framebuffer in PSRAM (250*122/8 = 3800 bytes per panel for 2.13").
   - draw_bitmap(x, y, w, h, const uint8_t*), fill(color), refresh_full(), refresh_partial().
   - class EpdCluster managing NUM_SCREENS EpdPanels over one shared SPI bus; per-panel CS via Pin abstraction; one std::mutex per panel for the GxEPD2-style discipline.
   - Init + LUT derived from GxEPD2_213_BN.cpp / GxEPD2_290_BS.cpp.

6. components/ws2812_ring
   - class WsRing wrapping espressif/led_strip managed component.
   - Exposes set_pixel(i, RGB), show(), rotate(), fade_all(brightness).
   - Trivial; mostly a typed wrapper.

## Concrete PoC tasks
- CMakeLists.txt, main/main.cpp with extern "C" void app_main(), idf_component.yml listing espressif/led_strip and espressif/esp-idf-cxx.
- sdkconfig.defaults: CONFIG_IDF_TARGET=esp32s3, CONFIG_SPIRAM=y, CONFIG_SPIRAM_MODE_OCT=y for Rev B's 8 MB PSRAM, CONFIG_ESP_DEFAULT_CPU_FREQ_MHZ_240=y, PSRAM cache heap enabled.
- Bring up i2c_master_bus_handle_t on SDA=GPIO 35, SCL=GPIO 36 (matches [platformio.ini](platformio.ini) Rev B).
- Instantiate Mcp23017 at address 0x20 (default), Pca9685 at 0x42 (matches PCA_I2C_ADDR), Bh1750 at 0x23.
- Bring up spi_bus_initialize on HSPI; for each of NUM_SCREENS=7 create a spi_device_handle_t with spics_io_num=-1 and gate CS via Pin. Wrap in esp_lcd_panel_io handles.
- Instantiate EpdCluster; for each panel call esp_lcd_new_panel_ssd1680 + panel_reset + panel_init. Render a test bitmap identifying panel number.
- Start a std::thread (pthread) that cycles the WS2812 ring through red/green/blue/white every 1 s via WsRing.
- Start a second std::thread that reads BH1750 once a second and sets the PCA9685 frontlight PWM inversely proportional to lux.
- Serial log of each step; nothing fancy.

## Acceptance
- idf.py -DSDKCONFIG_DEFAULTS='sdkconfig.defaults;sdkconfig.defaults.rev_b_213' -B build_rev_b_213 build flashes and boots.
- All 7 panels show their test bitmap after first boot.
- LEDs animate.
- Frontlight visibly fades with hand-over-sensor light changes.

## Scope guardrails
- No WiFi, no webserver, no NVS, no OTA, no screen rotation, no data sources.
- Just the three risky hardware paths, in C++, on v5.5.

## Depends on
Nothing. This is Phase 0 — runs before Phase 1 scaffolding matures into multi-variant CI. If the PoC succeeds, port the components into the Phase 1 tree as-is.

RAM budget: glyph cache in PSRAM, ~100 KB bounded LRU. At 80pt on a 250x122 panel a single glyph raster is ~10 KB, so ~10 glyphs per size in cache is plenty.

Consequences for other beads:
  - Phase 3 (btclock_v3_fci-pjv) 'Font renderer: port the GFXfont bitmap format reader' is replaced with 'TTF + stb_truetype + glyph cache + pyftsubset build step'. Same public API surface (draw_text(x,y,str,font,size)) so application code doesn't care which backend.
  - src/fonts/*.h and src/fonts/fonts.hpp are retired.
  - Sats symbol stays as a special case (1-glyph bitmap kept, or merged into Antonio as private-use codepoint U+E000 — cleaner).

Font source files to add to repo: Antonio-SemiBold.ttf, Oswald-Medium.ttf (both Google Fonts, OFL-licensed — compatible with Apache-2.0). ~60 KB and ~45 KB respectively; these are build-time inputs, not shipped.

title: IDF Phase 6: OTA, timers, DND, frontlight, cutover to Rev B
description:
Last-mile polish: both OTA paths, periodic timers, DND window, frontlight policy, watchdogs. End state: Rev B firmware built on pure ESP-IDF ships, Arduino-on-ESP-IDF is retired from main.

## Deliverable
Rev B firmware built on pure ESP-IDF v5.5 replaces the Arduino-on-ESP-IDF build and passes the full parity test matrix.

## Tasks
- Streamed web OTA via esp_https_ota with on-the-fly SHA-256 (same design as today, just the C API instead of Update.write()).
- ArduinoOTA push: evaluate usage — if non-zero, hand-port the ~200 line protocol state machine; if effectively unused, drop with a changelog note.
- minuteTimer + screenRotateTimer via esp_timer (IRAM-safe, can notify task handles from ISR context). Port the 'cache volatile TaskHandle_t, null-check before notify' pattern from src/lib/system/timers.cpp.
- DND window port (lib/btclock/dnd_window.* — pure algebra, trivial).
- Frontlight policy port (handleFrontlight + led_handler frontlight_* methods) using pca9685 component + led_strip for the LED ring.
- main.cpp-equivalent: 5-second ping SSE, frontlight handler, WiFi reconnect watchdog, LiveServiceRegistry::monitor(), 24-hour time resync. Mechanical translation.
- Firmware-size guard re-run: confirm Rev A (lolin_s3_mini_213epd, 1.75 MB OTA slot) still fits. This is the tightest variant; native IDF without Arduino should give us headroom, not steal it.

## Depends on
Phases 2, 3, 4, 5.

title: IDF Phase 5: Data plane — LiveService registry + all upstream feeds
description:
Port every upstream data source to esp_websocket_client (managed component) and esp_http_client. Preserve the LiveService abstraction and the tls_gate mutex pattern.

## Deliverable
Every data-source mode (BTCLOCK, CUSTOM, NOSTR, THIRD_PARTY) and every always-on feed (NostrZap, Bitaxe poll, mining pool poll) work in the IDF port with reconnect + staleness semantics identical to today.

## Tasks
- Port src/lib/data_sources/live_service.* as a plain-C trait (vtable struct).
- tls_gate: a single SemaphoreHandle_t guarding every TLS handshake across esp_websocket_client + esp_http_client (v5.5 still uses mbedtls for both). Non-negotiable — without it the boot-time simultaneous handshakes OOM mbedtls. See docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:193-199 for the pattern we must preserve.
- BlockNotify: esp_websocket_client on wss://mempool.space/api/v1/ws + REST fallback on 45-min silence.
- PriceNotify: esp_websocket_client on wss://ws.kraken.com with per-currency subscribe built from actCurrencies CSV; port data_sources/price_policy.hpp parser.
- V2Notify: esp_websocket_client + msgpack parsing (cmp or mpack library as managed component). Dispatch task.
- NostrNotify: esp_websocket_client + hand-rolled NIP-01 subscribe + NIP-57 zap receipt parser. Port from the nostrduino fork subset we actually use.
- BitaxeFetch: esp_http_client poll + cJSON.
- MiningPoolStatsFetch: per-pool adapters (Braiins, Ocean, Noderunners, Satoshi Radio, public-pool.io, local Public Pool, GoBrrr, CKPool, EU CKPool) mirroring src/lib/data_sources/mining_pool/*.
- LiveServiceRegistry watchdog on a 5-second cadence from app_main.

## Why
The data sources are the largest block (~5-6 kLOC of the ~17 kLOC total) and the most algorithmically stable — network protocols don't change every release. Once phase 4 is up, moving a data source over is low-risk per-source work.

## Depends on
Phase 4 (needs NVS + event loop + something to render into).
notes:
Mining-pool subsystem port plan (2026-04-23):

1. TLS gate landed first (btclock_v3_fci-3kt) — components/tls_gate
   header + host doctest, commit a6b2017 on worktree-agent-a7d7097f.
2. DataSnapshot extended with nested PoolStats substruct
   (name/hashrate/daily_sats/workers) in commit 1735322.
3. Seven per-pool subtasks created (one per old-firmware dir under
   src/lib/data_sources/mining_pool/): Braiins 093, Ocean zxk,
   Noderunners zs3, Satoshi Radio qmh, Public-pool g7h, Ckpool dhs,
   Gobrrr 9c1. No eu_ckpool dir exists — not filed.
4. Each pool subtask depends on 3kt (tls-gate). lcw depends on each
   pool subtask, so this issue blocks until all seven land.
5. Child agents spawned in parallel to implement each pool; each is
   told NOT to wire into main.cpp — follow-up orchestration of the
   mining_pool_stats_handler (pool selection + polling cadence) is
   deferred to a separate issue once per-pool sources exist.

title: IDF Phase 4: WiFi, HTTP server, SSE, NVS, mDNS, provisioning
description:
Replace the Arduino networking stack with esp_wifi + esp_http_server + wifi_provisioning (v5.5) and port all REST endpoints + SSE.

## Deliverable
All routes documented in docs/API.md served by esp_http_server with the same auth gate, CORS policy, and SSE event stream. WiFi credentials persisted in NVS; first-boot goes through SoftAP provisioning.

## Tasks
- esp_wifi init + event loop; STA reconnect logic ported from checkWiFiConnection() in main.cpp.
- wifi_provisioning via SoftAP transport (replaces WiFiManager). Captive-portal page lives in LittleFS next to the WebUI.
- esp_netif + mDNS (espressif/mdns managed component) for hostname + _http._tcp service advertisement.
- NVS: port PrefKeys:: inventory from src/lib/system/pref_keys.hpp to a single .c with typed getters/setters. Preserve 15-char key cap. Port the pref-keys lint CI guard.
- esp_http_server with CONFIG_HTTPD_MAX_OPEN_SOCKETS bumped to at least 7 (today's SSE clients + REST).
- CORS middleware (Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *, allowed headers: Content-Type, Authorization — same as today).
- HTTP Basic auth gate as a single helper require_http_auth(req) called at the top of every state-changing handler.
- SSE: per-client async request via httpd_req_async_handler_begin, 5-second ping loop via httpd_queue_work, text/event-stream chunked via httpd_resp_send_chunk.
- Route modules mirroring src/lib/net/webserver/ split: status.c, settings.c, actions.c, lights.c, dnd.c, ota_routes.c.
- Static serving from LittleFS for /: gzip-encoded WebUI assets direct from data/build_gz.
- buildStatusJson replaced with a cJSON builder; single source of truth reused by GET /api/status and SSE 'status' events.

## Why
This phase is the most visible surface of the rewrite. Every functional difference here is a user-visible regression. Good news: esp_http_server's async_handler + chunked API genuinely covers SSE without a third-party library (confirmed in IDF v5.5 docs), and esp_websocket_client handles TLS on the same mbedtls stack we use today.

## Depends on
Phase 1 for component manifest + LittleFS; not blocked by 2 or 3.
notes: Static WebUI file serving (catch-all /* GET) landed on worktree-agent-a089d7c3 commits d22af6a (MIME helper + 6 host tests, 103→109) and 95bf6b7 (HandleStatic). Serves /lfs/www/ with gzip preference, path-traversal protection, streaming reads, Cache-Control: no-cache for index.html. 503+Retry-After when LittleFS unmounted. Auth deferred (TODO in code) — the static surface must load before the user can auth. Verified registration order via reading esp_http_server source (httpd_uri.c: httpd_find_uri_handler walks forward, first match wins; httpd_register_uri_handler rejects duplicates via the same matcher, so /* MUST be last). Builds pass: REV_A/REV_B/V8. Leaving in_progress — SSE, mDNS, auth still pending.

title: IDF Phase 3: SSD1680 display driver + font/icon/QR pipeline
description:
Replace GxEPD2 with a purpose-built SSD1680 driver and a plain-C text/icon/QR renderer. GxEPD2 is C++ Arduino-centric with no good ESP-IDF equivalent; writing a thin driver is less work than shimming GxEPD2 onto raw SPI+MCP-pin drivers.

## Deliverable
components/epd: SSD1680 driver covering the 2.13" and 2.9" Waveshare/GoodDisplay panels we ship, per-panel partial + full refresh, rendered text from the existing bitmap fonts, icons, and QR codes. Same NUM_SCREENS-panel array + per-panel mutex discipline.

## Tasks
- SPI bus setup on HSPI/FSPI; one shared bus, per-panel SpiDevice struct gated by a handed-in CS GPIO.
- CS/BUSY/RESET pin abstraction: accept either a native GPIO number or an mcp23017 pin handle. Rev A/B use native CS + BUSY, MCP RESET. V8 routes all three through two MCP chips.
- SSD1680 init sequence + LUT for full and partial refresh (ported from GxEPD2's GxEPD2_213_BN.cpp / GxEPD2_290_BS.cpp initialisations).
- Framebuffer: 1bpp B/W, 250x122 (2.13") or 296x128 (2.9"), in PSRAM on Rev B/V8.
- Font renderer: port GFXfont bitmap format reader (same struct layout as antonio-semibold*.h / oswald-medium*.h). Zero-copy — the existing .h files stay as embedded data.
- Icon renderer: same bitmap format as current src/icons/.
- QR renderer: use lib/qrcode/qrcodegen.c as-is (already plain C).
- Update queue + dispatcher matching today's updateDisplayTask: one FreeRTOS task per panel, xQueueReceive-driven, lockless in steady-state.
- Partial/full refresh cadence parity with today's lastFullRefresh array.

## Why
This is the single biggest block of code to port and the thing most at risk of subtle regressions (ghosting, wrong LUT, inverted colors, wrong partial-window command). Doing it as a self-contained component with a clean test harness on a single panel first means we can validate each panel behaviour in isolation.

## Depends on
Phase 2 (MCP component provides the pin handles).

title: IDF Phase 2: Peripheral components — MCP23017, PCA9685, BH1750, WS2812B
description:
Replace the Arduino peripheral libraries with ESP-IDF components built on the new i2c_master and RMT drivers.

## Deliverable
components/ directory with: mcp23017, pca9685, bh1750, each a tiny idf_component_register wrapper around i2c_master. WS2812B via managed component espressif/led_strip. All usable from the main app via CMake REQUIRES.

## Tasks
- components/mcp23017: register IODIR/GPPU/IPOL/GPINTEN/INTCAP/GPIO reads-writes over i2c_master_bus. Port robtillaart's MCP23017 API surface we actually use (see src/lib/drivers/buttons/ and epd code) — not the full thing. Include interrupt register reads for button path.
- components/pca9685: 16-channel 12-bit PWM at the frequency the frontlight uses. Port only the set-channel-duty + set-frequency + OE pin control we call from led_handler.
- components/bh1750: single-shot + continuous high-res mode reads. Lux conversion identical to existing claws/BH1750 output.
- idf_component.yml adds espressif/led_strip@^2.5. Port led_handler to use led_strip_new_rmt_device + led_strip_set_pixel + led_strip_refresh.
- Delete universal_pin: each driver takes its own i2c_master_dev_handle; pin abstraction was never needed outside the EPD layer.
- Unit tests: use IDF test framework (pytest + esp32 target board, or native host tests for pure-logic).

## Why
These four components together are about 200 lines of actual hardware protocol wrapped in Arduino convenience. Porting them first gives us a clean separation between hardware and application layers that the current code blurs (the MCP23017 library is consumed directly by both button_handler and EPDManager).

## Depends on
Phase 1 (build scaffold).

title: IDF Phase 1: Native CMake scaffolding + CI matrix + partition tables
description:
Stand up the native ESP-IDF project structure and CI matrix before porting any code. Goal is to have an empty firmware build successfully for every board variant out of one source tree.

## Deliverable
Repo layout that supports 'idf.py build' for rev_a_213, rev_a_29, rev_b_213, rev_b_29, v8_213 with one source tree. CI job per variant.

## Tasks
- Top-level CMakeLists.txt using IDF's project() macro.
- main/ with a minimal app_main that prints a banner + board variant.
- sdkconfig.defaults (shared) + per-variant sdkconfig.defaults.<variant> files derived from existing sdkconfig.btclock_rev_b_213epd and sdkconfig.lolin_s3_mini_* and boards/sdkconfig.btclock_v8.
- partition tables ported 1:1 from partition.csv / partition_8mb.csv / partition_16mb.csv.
- Custom board JSONs (boards/btclock_rev_b.json, boards/btclock_v8.json) replaced with IDF Kconfig choices + CMake cache values in the per-variant defaults.
- managed_components via idf_component.yml: joltwallet/esp_littlefs, espressif/mdns, espressif/esp_websocket_client, espressif/led_strip.
- CI workflow (GitHub / Gitea Actions) with a matrix over variant using espressif/esp-idf-ci-action@v1, IDF v5.5 release branch. One upload-artifact per variant producing firmware.bin + partition-table.bin + littlefs.bin.
- Firmware-size guard ported from scripts/extra_script.py: a shell step that fails if build_lolin_s3_mini_213/app.bin exceeds the OTA-slot ceiling.
- Dockerfile (optional) for local dev matching the CI IDF version.

## Why
Getting the multi-variant build right on day one is where PlatformIO has historically saved effort. If we prove native ESP-IDF can match that with SDKCONFIG_DEFAULTS chains, every subsequent phase gets to assume a clean build matrix.

title: Epic: Rewrite firmware on pure ESP-IDF v5.5 (drop Arduino core), path to v6.0
description:
Investigation epic for migrating the BTClock firmware OFF Arduino-as-component and ONTO native ESP-IDF v5.5 as the first target, with a follow-up to v6.0 once breaking changes are absorbed. Current stack: platformio.ini pins espressif32@^6.13.0 with 'framework = arduino, espidf'. The Arduino core is the thing we're removing; ESP-IDF we're already on.

## Verdict
Feasible, and strictly safer than the Rust rewrite because the language and RTOS stay identical. Estimated effort 2-4 months single-dev for feature parity because most of the work is library swap-out, not logic reimplementation. Every Arduino-facing API has a direct ESP-IDF equivalent except ESPAsyncWebServer (esp_http_server needs glue for async + SSE) and GxEPD2 (no drop-in C replacement — we either write a thin SSD1680 driver or keep GxEPD2 as a C++ island).

## Target v5.5 first, v6.0 second
ESP-IDF v5.5 is the current stable LTS; v6.0 has absorbed real breaking changes we would have to address in a second pass:
- wifi_provisioning removed, renamed to network_provisioning (now a managed component).
- Several FreeRTOS compat shims removed (vTaskDelayUntil -> xTaskDelayUntil, ulTaskNotifyTake is macro-only, xQueueGenericReceive gone).
- esp_ping.h removed; use ping/ping_sock.h.
- esp_adc_cal removed; use esp_adc.
- Bluedroid / NimBLE API renames (PREFERED -> PREFERRED etc).
- Various typo-fix renames.

Going to v5.5 first keeps the diff reviewable. v6.0 becomes a follow-up epic where the code touches are mechanical.

## Build system: native ESP-IDF CMake, not PlatformIO
The current PlatformIO espressif32 platform (v6.13.0) lags behind official ESP-IDF and is tied to Arduino packaging. pioarduino is more current but still community-maintained. Native ESP-IDF (idf.py + CMake + the IDF Component Manager) gives us:
- Immediate access to the latest IDF version.
- First-class SDKCONFIG_DEFAULTS chaining: 'sdkconfig.defaults;sdkconfig.defaults.rev_b_213' per board without env duplication.
- Managed components via idf_component.yml (espressif/esp_websocket_client, espressif/mdns, espressif/led_strip, joltwallet/esp_littlefs, etc).
- One CMake source of truth instead of a pre/post-script pipeline (scripts/pre_script.py's WebSockets.h patch goes away).
- Official espressif/esp-idf-ci-action for GitHub/Gitea Actions, matrix over target + board variant.

## Library replacement map
| Arduino dep (current) | ESP-IDF replacement |
|---|---|
| WiFi.h / WiFiManager | esp_wifi + esp_netif + wifi_provisioning (v5.5) / network_provisioning (v6.0) |
| ESPAsyncWebServer | esp_http_server with httpd_req_async_handler_begin + httpd_resp_send_chunk for SSE |
| Links2004/WebSockets client | espressif/esp_websocket_client (managed component, TLS via esp-tls/mbedtls, same stack as today) |
| ArduinoJson | cJSON (built-in) |
| Adafruit NeoPixel | espressif/led_strip (managed component, RMT-based) |
| robtillaart/MCP23017 | custom components/mcp23017 on i2c_master |
| robtillaart/PCA9685 | custom components/pca9685 on i2c_master |
| claws/BH1750 | custom components/bh1750 on i2c_master |
| GxEPD2 | write a thin SSD1680 driver for 2.13" and 2.9" (the protocol is simple; GxEPD2 is C++ library-of-drivers overkill for our fixed panel set) |
| lib/qrcode (qrcodegen) | keep as-is, already plain C |
| universal_pin | delete; use our own pin abstraction directly |
| ArduinoOTA | hand-port or drop; esp_https_ota already covers the streamed web path |
| nostrduino | vendor / trim to just NIP-01 subscribe + NIP-57 zap parse |
| scripts/pre_script.py WebSockets.h patch | gone — esp_websocket_client max frame size is a Kconfig (CONFIG_WS_BUFFER_SIZE) |

## CI matrix sketch
GitHub/Gitea Actions matrix over (board_variant, epd_size):
- rev_a_213, rev_a_29, rev_b_213, rev_b_29, v8_213
Each job:
  idf.py --preview set-target esp32s3
  idf.py -DSDKCONFIG_DEFAULTS='sdkconfig.defaults;sdkconfig.defaults.rev_b_213' -B build_rev_b_213 build
Artefacts: firmware bin + partition table + littlefs image. Firmware-size guard stays — just ports from the current PlatformIO extra_script to a plain grep over build_*/size.txt.

## Out of scope
- Keeping the Arduino layer. This epic is specifically about dropping it.
- WebUI rewrite. SvelteKit stays.
- Simultaneous upgrade to v6.0. That's a follow-up epic.

## References
- ESP-IDF v5.5: https://docs.espressif.com/projects/esp-idf/en/release-v5.5/esp32s3/
- ESP-IDF v6.0 migration: https://docs.espressif.com/projects/esp-idf/en/release-v6.0/esp32c6/migration-guides/release-6.x/6.0/
- esp-protocols (esp_websocket_client, mdns): https://github.com/espressif/esp-protocols
- IDF Component Manager: https://docs.espressif.com/projects/esp-idf/en/release-v5.5/esp32s3/api-guides/tools/idf-component-manager.html
- docs/ARCHITECTURE.md for current task/mutex layout
- platformio.ini for the build envs being retired
notes: Parent epic still open — child issues tracked individually

title: Rust Phase 5: OTA + polish
description:
Port both OTA paths and the last-mile polish items (timers, watchdogs, DND window, frontlight policy).

## Deliverable
Firmware updates work from the WebUI and (optionally) via ArduinoOTA push.

## Tasks
- Streamed web OTA via esp_https_ota — /api/ota/update and /api/ota/webui handlers. Stream straight into the OTA writer; compute SHA-256 on the fly (same design as C++).
- ArduinoOTA push protocol: decide drop vs hand-port. ~200 lines of state machine over UDP + TCP on the standard mDNS port. Not bundled in any Rust crate.
- DND window (lib/btclock/dnd_window.* — pure time-range algebra, trivial port).
- Frontlight policy port (handleFrontlight in main.cpp + led_handler frontlight_* methods).
- minuteTimer / screenRotateTimer IRAM ISRs using esp-idf-hal timers; follow the 'cache TaskHandle, null-check, notify-from-isr' pattern from timers.cpp.
- Watchdogs (WiFi reconnect, 45-min block silence probe) in the main loop.

## Why
Everything in this phase is self-contained and easy individually, but collectively represents real user-facing functionality that's not covered by phases 2-4.

## Depends on
Phases 2, 3, 4. This phase is the last merge before cutover.

title: Rust Phase 4: Web / config plane — HTTP, SSE, NVS, auth
description:
Port the webserver, SSE event stream, NVS preferences, and WiFi provisioning. The WebUI (SvelteKit in data/ submodule) is served unchanged from LittleFS.

## Deliverable
Rust firmware that exposes the same HTTP API documented in docs/API.md with the same auth semantics, serves the current WebUI, and supports WiFi provisioning.

## Tasks
- esp-idf-svc::http::server setup with CORS, static serving from LittleFS.
- PrefKeys inventory ported from src/lib/system/pref_keys.hpp into a Rust module with type-safe accessors. Preserve the 15-character NVS name cap.
- PrefKeys lint CI guard ported to Rust.
- Auth gate (requireHttpAuth) as a middleware / helper.
- SSE /api/events implementation on the raw response writer (text/event-stream + heartbeat; esp-idf-svc has no first-class SSE helper).
- Status / settings / actions / lights / dnd / ota route modules (mirror src/lib/net/webserver/).
- buildStatusJson single source of truth.
- WiFi provisioning: replace WiFiManager. Either adopt ESP-IDF's wifi_provisioning component (SoftAP) or build a minimal captive-portal equivalent.
- mDNS service advertisement.
- LittleFS volume mount via esp_littlefs.

## Why
This is the user-facing surface. Any functional regression here is a visible regression. Keeping it in parity means the WebUI (which stays SvelteKit) needs zero changes.

## Depends on
Phase 3 for the status payload content. Not blocked by Phase 2 display work.

title: Rust Phase 3: Data plane — LiveService registry + all data sources
description:
Port every upstream data feed: BlockNotify (mempool.space WS), PriceNotify (Kraken WS), V2Notify (BTClock MsgPack WS), NostrNotify, BitaxeFetch, MiningPoolStatsFetch, and the LiveServiceRegistry watchdog.

## Deliverable
All existing data sources work in Rust with the same reconnect + staleness semantics as the C++ firmware. THIRD_PARTY_SOURCE mode is the bar to clear first.

## Tasks
- LiveService trait + LiveServiceRegistry (direct translation of src/lib/data_sources/live_service.hpp).
- tls_gate mutex pattern (see docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:193-199) reproduced around esp_websocket_client handshakes and esp_http_client requests. This is non-negotiable — without it the boot-time concurrent TLS handshakes OOM mbedtls.
- BlockNotify: mempool.space WS client + REST fallback on 45-min silence.
- PriceNotify: Kraken WS + per-currency subscription from actCurrencies CSV. Keep priceMapMutex equivalent.
- V2Notify: MsgPack over WS (use rmp-serde). Dispatch task + reconnect.
- NostrNotify: slim client covering subscribe, event receive, NIP-57 zap parsing. nostr-sdk is too heavy; write a minimal one. Reuse the WebSocket client from esp-idf-svc.
- BitaxeFetch: HTTP poll + JSON deserialise with serde.
- MiningPoolStatsFetch: per-pool adapters (Braiins, Ocean, Noderunners, Satoshi Radio, public-pool.io, local Public Pool, GoBrrr, CKPool, EU CKPool). Keep pool_factory pattern.

## Why
The data sources are the most algorithmically stable part of the firmware (network protocols don't change every release) and the biggest surface — roughly a third of the total LoC. Porting them early de-risks the schedule.

## Depends on
Phase 2 (so there's something to render into) and esp-idf-svc WebSocket client maturity (github issues #266, #514 — verify works before relying on it).

title: Rust Phase 2: Display subsystem — 7/8 panel EPD on MCP-driven pins
description:
Port the multi-panel EPD driver, the highest-risk piece of the Rust rewrite. This is where GxEPD2's generality earned its keep in C++; epd-waveshare does not natively support our layout.

## Deliverable
All 7 (Rev A/B) / 8 (V8) e-paper panels driven from Rust, showing arbitrary text, icons, and QR codes. Same refresh cadence, same full-refresh-every-N-partials cadence as today.

## Tasks
- Shim port-expander MCP23017 pin output as embedded-hal::digital::OutputPin so epd-waveshare can consume it for CS/BUSY/RESET.
- Per-panel SpiDevice wrapper that takes the mcpMutex equivalent only around the CS toggle.
- epd-waveshare SSD1680 driver integration. Handle both the 2.13" and 2.9" variants behind a feature flag equivalent to VERSION_EPD_2_13 / VERSION_EPD_2_9.
- Font rendering: port the GFXfont bitmap format (antonio-*, oswald-*) to either u8g2-fonts or a direct embedded-graphics renderer. Do not regenerate fonts unless necessary.
- Icon rendering port (src/icons/).
- QR code rendering via qrcodegen crate (same upstream as lib/qrcode).
- Display update queue + prioritisation matching updateDisplayTask.
- Per-panel displayMutexes + forceFullRefresh logic parity.

## Why
This phase validates the single weakest part of the ecosystem mapping. If the MCP-pin shim works, every other subsystem port is orders of magnitude easier. If it doesn't, we fork epd-waveshare or port GxEPD2's display abstraction into Rust — significant scope bump worth knowing early.

## Depends on
Phase 1 spike (toolchain, MCP, I2C).

title: Rust Phase 1: Spike — toolchain, boot, WiFi, MCP button, NeoPixel
description:
First real-hardware spike of the Rust rewrite on Rev B. Prove the toolchain pipeline and core peripherals work before committing to the full port.

## Deliverable
A Rust binary on btclock_rev_b that boots, connects to WiFi, lights the 4 NeoPixels, and reads one button press from the MCP23017.

## Tasks
- cargo-espflash / espup toolchain setup (Xtensa target for ESP32-S3).
- Bring up esp-idf-sys + esp-idf-svc + esp-idf-hal against ESP-IDF v5.x matching the existing sdkconfig as closely as possible.
- Minimal CMakeLists / Cargo.toml template.
- WiFi connect via esp-idf-svc::wifi with credentials from NVS (placeholder).
- WS2812B test via ws2812-esp32-rmt-driver on GPIO 15 (Rev B) — cycle the 4 LEDs through colours.
- MCP23017 via port-expander on the same I2C pins the C++ firmware uses (SDA 35, SCL 36). Read one button; print on serial.

## Why
This single spike proves the three non-negotiable building blocks: the Rust toolchain actually targets ESP32-S3 in a reproducible way, esp-idf-svc services work on our specific board, and the MCP pin abstraction model (port-expander exposing embedded-hal pins) carries through. If the spike works, the rest of the port is mostly porting code. If it doesn't, we learn cheaply.

## Acceptance
- cargo run --release boots and prints serial output.
- WiFi associates with a test SSID.
- All 4 NeoPixels visibly animate.
- Button 1 press logs a line.

title: Epic: Evaluate firmware rewrite in Rust (ESP-IDF Rust / esp-idf-svc)
description:
Investigation epic for porting the BTClock firmware from C++/Arduino-on-ESP-IDF to Rust on ESP-IDF (std, via esp-idf-svc + esp-idf-hal). Captures feasibility findings, ecosystem mapping, risks, and a phased plan. Target hardware: ESP32-S3 on Rev A (Lolin S3 Mini), Rev B (btclock_rev_b), and V8 prototype.

## Verdict
Feasible. Target the ESP-IDF-std Rust path (not bare-metal esp-hal) because the firmware is network-heavy. Estimated effort 3-6 months single-dev for feature parity with ~17 kLOC of current C/C++ code.

## Ecosystem mapping
| Subsystem (current) | Rust replacement |
|---|---|
| MCP23017 buttons + EPD pins | port-expander crate (exposes MCP pins as embedded-hal InputPin/OutputPin) |
| PCA9685 frontlight | pwm-pca9685 |
| BH1750 ambient | bh1750 |
| WS2812B LEDs | ws2812-esp32-rmt-driver + smart-leds |
| e-paper SSD1680 (2.13/2.9) | epd-waveshare + embedded-graphics |
| WiFi/NVS/OTA/HTTP server/mDNS/TLS | esp-idf-svc |
| JSON / MsgPack | serde_json / rmp-serde |
| QR code | qrcodegen crate (same upstream as current lib/qrcode) |
| Nostr | slim hand-rolled client (nostr-sdk is too heavy) |

## Key risks
1. Multi-panel EPD over MCP expander pins. epd-waveshare assumes one display per SPI bus; we drive 7-8 panels with CS/BUSY/RESET partly on MCP. Needs a per-panel SpiDevice adapter + mutex discipline equivalent to today's mcpMutex.
2. WebSocket client maturity in esp-idf-svc (issues #266, #514). Still wraps esp_websocket_client + mbedtls, so tls_gate mutex pattern must be reproduced.
3. Nostr: no slim embedded crate; port nostrduino subset or build in-repo.
4. SSE: esp-idf-svc HTTP server has no SSE helper; implement on raw response writer.
5. ArduinoOTA push: no Rust crate; drop or hand-port ~200-line state machine.
6. GFXfont bitmap fonts (antonio/oswald): either runtime-read the GFXfont struct format in Rust or regenerate as embedded-graphics BDF.
7. Build toolchain: espup/cargo-espflash replaces PlatformIO; CI needs to install Xtensa LLVM.

## Phased plan
Phase 1 Spike: boot + WiFi + 4 NeoPixels + 1 MCP button on btclock_rev_b.
Phase 2 Display subsystem: port-expander shim, per-panel SpiDevice, epd-waveshare, fonts, QR, mutex discipline. Hardcoded content across all panels.
Phase 3 Data plane: LiveService trait + BlockNotify, PriceNotify (proves tls_gate), then V2 MsgPack, Bitaxe, mining pool adapters, Nostr last.
Phase 4 Web/config plane: HTTP server, SSE, NVS PrefKeys, auth gate, WiFi provisioning (replaces WiFiManager). WebUI unchanged.
Phase 5 OTA + polish: web-streamed OTA; ArduinoOTA optional.
Phase 6 Cutover: Rev B first, then Rev A, then V8.

## Out of scope
- WebUI rewrite (stays SvelteKit, served from LittleFS).
- Bare-metal esp-hal / no_std path (rejected: incompatible with the network surface).

## References
- docs/ARCHITECTURE.md for current task/mutex layout and tls_gate pattern
- platformio.ini for current build envs and HW defines
- https://github.com/esp-rs/esp-idf-svc
- https://lib.rs/crates/epd-waveshare
- https://crates.io/crates/port-expander
notes: Investigation conducted 2026-04-22. Context7 MCP was not providing tools during initial investigation so fell back to WebFetch + WebSearch; driver coverage verified through crates.io listings.

title: NWC: full set (pay/make/tx-list) — gated to Rev B / V8
description:
Scenario 4 from the sizing study. Adds outgoing payments + tx history. Gated behind CONFIG_BTCLOCK_NWC_FULL=y; default off on Rev A (overshoots OTA headroom in the 95% CI band), default on for Rev B and V8.

## Adds (on top of v1 read-only + notifications)
- JSON-RPC methods: pay_invoice, pay_keysend, make_invoice, lookup_invoice, sign_message.
- Tx-list screen (paginated, scroll state).
- Invoice-display screen (LN invoice string + amount; optional QR if a glyph atlas approach is feasible at panel sizes — Rev B / V8 only anyway, panel size isn't the bottleneck on those boards).
- Webserver: POST /api/nwc/pay_invoice, POST /api/nwc/make_invoice (auth-gated).

## NOT in this issue (already in v1, lwf.6)
- Notification screen for payment_received / payment_sent — those land in lwf.6 as the primary v1 feature; this issue does NOT touch that path.

## Risks
- Per-request RAM peak grows to 8-12 KiB for list_transactions JSON; mitigate via streaming parse or PSRAM-allocated response buffer.
- cJSON tree fragmentation for large transaction lists.
- max_uri_handlers budget needs +1 (would push past 50 limit) — bump in this issue.

## Verification
- Live test on Rev B: pair, fetch tx list, send a 1-sat invoice from the device.
- Re-measure flash delta and compare to ~9 KiB estimate (~35 KiB vs ~26 KiB scenario 3 baseline).

## Acceptance
- Kconfig gate exists and is wired through CMake; default rules per board.
- Build matrix: rev-a with NWC_FULL=n must fit OTA partition; rev-b / v8 with NWC_FULL=y must fit.

title: Defer on_tz_changed to main task (libc tz race)
description: on_tz_changed in init_control_api.cpp:129 calls setenv(TZ,...)/tzset() from the HTTP task. The main task reads tz globals via localtime_r in screen_manager.cpp:727 each Render. picolibc/newlib does not lock between tzset writers and localtime_r readers; the worst case is a corrupt tm_now read for one frame. No heap corruption. Defer to main via kSetTimezone ControlCommand for cleanliness. Identified in audit btclock_v4-jo3.
close_reason: Implemented as kSetFont and kSetTimezone ControlCommands (commit 82675fd). Verified on Rev B: four fontName PATCHes + two tzString PATCHes all returned 200, device stayed up, panels rendering cleanly.

title: Defer on_font_changed to main task (atomic font swap)
description: on_font_changed in init_control_api.cpp:153 calls AppFonts::SetFamily from the HTTP task, writing 4 raw const Font* pointers (role_digit_, role_label_, role_small_chars_, role_unit_). Pointer writes are 4-byte aligned and atomic on ESP32-S3 so there's no UAF, but a render frame could read two of the four roles before the swap and two after — producing a single-frame mixed-family glyph set. Cosmetic only. Defer to main via kSetFont ControlCommand to make the swap atomic with respect to any in-flight render. Identified in audit btclock_v4-jo3.
close_reason: Implemented as kSetFont and kSetTimezone ControlCommands (commit 82675fd). Verified on Rev B: four fontName PATCHes + two tzString PATCHes all returned 200, device stayed up, panels rendering cleanly.

title: mDNS: live re-advertisement when mdnsEnabled / hostnamePrefix change
description:
Both prefs are flagged boot_only in components/settings/include/settings/schema.hpp,
so changing them via PATCH /api/settings does not re-advertise mDNS until
the device reboots.

To support live changes, init_mdns.cpp would need a teardown +
re-init cycle invoked from a settings-change hook (similar to the
on_tz_changed wiring in init_control_api.cpp). The schema field
flag would also flip from boot_only to live.

This is a quality-of-life fix only; reboot is a working workaround
today.

- main/app/boot/init_mdns.cpp:148
- components/settings/include/settings/schema.hpp:213
close_reason: Closed

title: Nostr: schnorr signature verification (vendor secp256k1)
description:
The Nostr data source currently trusts the WSS-to-relay channel and
does NOT verify the schnorr signature on incoming events
(`components/nostr/src/nostr_data_source.cpp`, `OnEvent`). This is
deliberate listen-only mode — see FEATURE_MATRIX (Nostr row).

To verify, vendor libsecp256k1 with --enable-module-schnorrsig and
plumb a verifier into `OnEvent` before the kind/d-tag dispatch.

Until that lands, the device accepts whatever the configured relay
sends. Acceptable for the current zap-listener use case (the worst
case is a bogus zap notification from a hostile relay), but blocks
any future "trust this NostrDataSource pushed value" wiring.

- components/nostr/src/nostr_data_source.cpp:62
close_reason: Closed

title: IDF Phase 7 (follow-up): Upgrade v5.5 → v6.0
description:
Separate, mechanical follow-up epic to bump the IDF baseline once the v5.5 port is stable on main.

## Deliverable
Same firmware, same feature set, now on ESP-IDF v6.0.

## Known touch points (from v6.0 migration guides)
- Replace wifi_provisioning with network_provisioning (now a managed component, must be added to idf_component.yml). Remove wifi_provisioning via EXCLUDE_COMPONENTS in CMakeLists.txt.
- FreeRTOS compat removals:
  - vTaskDelayUntil() -> xTaskDelayUntil()
  - ulTaskNotifyTake as function -> ulTaskNotifyTake macro
  - xQueueGenericReceive() -> xQueueReceive() / xQueuePeek() / xQueueSemaphoreTake()
  - xTaskGetAffinity()/xTaskGetCurrentTaskHandleForCPU()/xTaskGetIdleTaskHandleForCPU() -> Core variants
- esp_ping.h removed -> use ping/ping_sock.h (we use this inside checkWiFiConnection via DNS rather than ICMP ping, so may be a no-op).
- esp_adc_cal component removed -> use esp_adc (if we end up reading the BH1750 via i2c we don't touch esp_adc; check v8 board).
- Minor typo-fix API renames (ESP_GAP_BLE_CHANNEL_SELETE -> _SELECT, _PREFERED -> _PREFERRED) — does not affect us unless we add BLE.
- No changes expected to esp_http_server, esp_websocket_client, NVS, esp_netif, or esp_http_client.

## Why a separate epic
v5.5 is the LTS baseline most examples and managed components are tested against today. Doing the framework swap and the IDF bump simultaneously would conflate two independent sources of breakage. Bump in a single PR once v5.5 parity has real user hours on it.

## Depends on
Phase 6 (Rev B cutover complete on v5.5).

title: Rust Phase 6: Cutover — Rev B, then Rev A, then V8
description:
Production cutover strategy. The Rust branch runs in parallel with the C++ main branch until Rev B parity ships.

## Deliverable
Rust firmware replaces C++ as the shipping build for all three hardware variants.

## Tasks
- Rev B parity release first (best RAM/flash headroom, every subsystem exercised).
- Rev A (Lolin S3 Mini) second — tighter flash budget, check firmware size against the OTA slot early.
- V8 prototype last — MCP-routed EPD CS/BUSY adds contention pressure; validate mcpMutex-equivalent behaviour on real hardware before declaring parity.
- Migration guide for users with existing NVS contents (pref key names are preserved, so none should be needed, but verify end-to-end).
- Deprecation policy for the C++ firmware: how long both trees are maintained in parallel, when the C++ tree freezes for bug-fix-only.

## Why
Cutover last. Never cut over before the spike-through-polish sequence is proven.

## Depends on
All prior phases.
